records.summary: Studio Gang's 23-story, 254-unit rental tower at 1070 Bridgeview Way, the fourth and last Phase 1 building. Construction started March 2022, leasing began April 2024, residents moved in from June 2024 and the ribbon was cut September 3, 2024; 59 of its units are below market rate after a 2024 re-mix toward 90% AMI. Chipotle's own location page for 365 Toni Stone Xing, Unit C gives an opening date of September 23, 2026 (a date stated by the business, on a page captured the next day).

open_questions: Commercial Property Executive's July 14, 2026 article (the only source for the $116.2 million Wells Fargo construction loan and the $117.8 million Ares Management loan) refused access on 2026-10-12, and a second page listed in a web search for the same loan (traded.co) did too, so neither amount, lender nor what the Ares loan replaced is confirmed by a page read here.

Jobs Housing Equivalency Fee subsidy received by Parcel F: the Port's September 2019 budget report lists a minimum of 75.6 ($ millions) for Parcel F when it was planned with 106 below-market units (it has 59), and says the residential projects "will request a proportionate share of the JHEF when the residential building foundations have been completed"; no source read gives the amount actually paid to Parcel F.

Construction cost: no source read states one. DBI permit 201910073784 carries a $99,907,840 estimated and revised cost, which is a filed permit valuation rather than a cost, and the only financing figure is the reported $116.2 million Wells Fargo loan, which is unconfirmed (see the first question).

Exact TCO date: the Port's October 2023 memo projected a June 2024 TCO, and its April 2024 memo said Parcel F "is expected to receive a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) in May" with move-ins in June 2024 (both are projections); no document read gives the date the TCO was issued.
Topping-out date: the Port's October 2023 memo only says it had topped out; no dated press item found.

Total square footage disagrees across sources (287,000 / 314,508 / 315,000 / 330,000: a trade-press article reposted by Mitsui Fudosan America, the Port's 2019 appraisal table, the 2026 refinancing report, and SF YIMBY in March 2022); no document read says which is the gross floor area, and the DBI permit records read carry no floor area.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (until 2020 the parcel was the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.

A Mapillary storefront photo of Ike's Love & Sandwiches (a sourced retail tenant, see the retail fact above) was hosted briefly and then removed: on review it read as too cluttered (a trash bin, a parked car and several pedestrians in front of the sign) to keep. Still on the shot list for a cleaner frame.
Arsicault Bakery's Verde shop is shown open on a March 11, 2025 release; it has not been re-confirmed since.

A business registration for BVNK at 365 Toni Stone Xing Fl 3 exists since 2025-03-30 (System Pay Services (Us), Inc., no end date, DataSF Registered Business Locations); no source read shows an office open there, so BVNK is not listed as a tenant. Searches found no page that names BVNK at Mission Rock.

Chipotle Mexican Grill is shown open from 2026-09-23. That date is the 'c_openDate' on Chipotle's own location page for 365 Toni Stone Xing (locations.chipotle.com, whose data carries a timestamp of 2026-09-24 and which was read on 2026-10-12); it is a date the company states, not one confirmed by a news report or a visit. The page lists daily hours of 10:45 a.m. to 10 p.m. and online ordering. DataSF has a registration for Chipotle Mexican Grill #5956 at suite C from 2026-08-25, which is a registration date, not an opening date.

First move-in month: SF YIMBY (September 4, 2024) says the building "has been open to new residents since June", while the Port's March 2025 memo says "As of February 2025, seven months into lease-up", which would put the start of lease-up around July 2024. No certificate of occupancy or lease document read dates the first move-in, so "June 2024" is approximate.

Resolution number for the Board of Supervisors' March 6, 2018 action: the Port's October 2023 memo gives Resolution 33-18 for the Board's affirmation of the EIR certification, but the same memo (and the Port's September 2019 and April 2024 reports) also cites Resolution 33-18 for the Board's February 2018 approval of the Development Agreement (with Resolution 42-18 for the DDA); the Notice of Determination gives only File No. 171286.

Unit mix of Verde: SF YIMBY (Sept 2024) gives 30 studios, 129 one-bedrooms, 91 two-bedrooms and 4 three-bedrooms; the Port's March 2025 memo, Table 2 'Parcel F Housing Table 2022', gives 30 studios, 132 one-bedrooms, 88 two-bedrooms and 4 three-bedrooms.

Total square footage of Verde, by source: 314,508 total per the 2019 Port appraisal table; 287,000 per a Yield Pro article of April 30, 2024 reposted by Mitsui Fudosan America; 330,000 per SF YIMBY (March 2022); 315,000 per the 2026 refinancing report, whose page was unreadable, so that figure is unconfirmed.

LEED rating of Verde: Mission Rock's April 2024 release (via Yield Pro) and Studio Gang's undated page, written after June 2024, both say "targeting" LEED Gold; the 2026 refinancing report is cited as calling it certified, but that page was unreadable, so certification is unconfirmed.

records.summary: The first Mission Rock residential building: a 283-unit rental tower by MVRDV on Parcel A (sources count 23 or 24 stories; see open questions) at 3rd Street, with two office floors and ground-floor retail; TCO May 2023, first residents June 1, 2023, opening ceremony June 21, 2023. open_questions: Number of stories: 23 or 24. MVRDV (2022-04-19 and 2023-06-26) calls it "a 23-storey mixed-use building" and SF YIMBY (2022-04-13 and 2023-06-22) "a 23-story residential tower"; the DBI site permit 201910073782 says "to erect a 24 story, type 1a , 283 residential building" (number_of_proposed_stories "24"), Swinerton calls it "the new 24-story apartment building", and SF YIMBY's December 20, 2021 report says the podium would introduce "Mission Rock's first housing across 24 floors". No source read explains the difference (the permit figure is a proposal; the other counts were published during or after construction).
Construction cost of The Canyon: no source found; the Port memos cover only the horizontal (site-level) budget.

Street address: DataSF's parcel data for lot 8719B002 gives an address range, 1011 to 1023 3rd St; the Assessor roll lists 1011 3rd St, Wikipedia gives 1023 3rd St, and DBI lists both 1011 (primary) and 1023 for permit 201910073782. No Port document read gives a street address.

Whether the Board of Supervisors approved the Parcel A lease amendment that the Port took up with the March 2025 Housing Plan amendment: no outcome found on Legistar as of 2026-09-24. (The Housing Plan amendment half is settled: the Board adopted Resolution No. 193-25 on April 29, 2025, 11-0.)

Groundbreaking date for Parcel A: Wikipedia says December 2020 without a citation, and Swinerton says 'beginning of 2021'. The Port's FY2025 continuing disclosure says the developer 'broke ground on Phase 1 of the project in 2020, including work on horizontal infrastructure and two of the four parcels in Phase 1' and that 'Construction of the third building commenced in the fall of 2021', without naming the parcels; the Port's December 2021 update says the project is 'approximately one year into Phase 1A horizontal and vertical construction activities'. No Port document names Parcel A's start date, so it is kept as approximate 2021.

records.name: Pier 48
records.summary: A 1928-30 reinforced-concrete finger pier with two transit sheds around an open 'valley' and Tudor/Gothic Revival bulkhead buildings, the southernmost contributor to the National Register-listed Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District. The Mission Rock environmental review analyzed a rehabilitation of the pier under the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for light industrial, restaurant, retail and exhibition uses (261,000 gsf in the 2016 historic resource evaluation, 242,500 gsf in the EIR project table), and the 2018 development agreement lets a rehabilitation go forward only once a feasible pier use plan is developed. The planned anchor tenant in the 2013-2016 proposals, Anchor Brewing, announced in July 2023 that it was ceasing operations; on May 31, 2024 (publication date) the San Francisco Standard reported that Anchor and its Potrero Hill brewery had been bought by Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya's firm, which plans to restart brewing there (the article does not mention Pier 48). In 2018 the Board of Supervisors approved a ten-year lease of up to about 212,000 sq ft of the pier to the Giants' affiliate China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and special events; no later document confirming that lease is still in force was found, and Giants Enterprises markets the pier as an event venue.

open_questions: Whether the 2018 ten-year China Basin Ballpark Company lease was later amended or replaced: a five-year interim lease covering Seawall Lot 337 parking and Pier 48 sheds is described on a secondary site (citizenportal.ai) but the Port memo behind it was not located.
Any rehabilitation cost estimate or seismic/substructure study for the pier: none found in the Port memos read.
Responses to the 2018 historic piers RFI that named Pier 48: the response bundles were not read.

No source states that the Pier 48 brewery plan was formally cancelled; the inference rests on Anchor's 2023 closure and its 2024 buyer's stated Potrero Hill plan (this record previously said the buyer 'will not reopen an SF brewery', which the May 2024 reporting does not say; corrected 2026-09-29).
Whether the Port Commission Resolution 18-10 rent-credit terms for capital repairs were ever exercised.
Images: no rendering of the entitled rehabilitation is hosted; none appears in the public-record documents read (the 2013 Anchor Brewing scheme was never published as a Port or Planning figure).

No source read gives a planned start date for the current Pier 48 rehabilitation. It was announced for the Anchor Brewing scheme in February 2013 (ENR, February 28, 2013: "Construction, beginning late 2014"), and the Port's January 26, 2018 staff report makes a rehabilitation conditional on "the parties' development of a feasible pier use plan".

Images: the 2013 photo of the 'valley' is HRE Figure 13, credited to Christopher VerPlanck, the HRE's author; the HRE states no reuse licence for it, so its 'public-record' licence label is Pier & Point's own judgment and is unconfirmed.

Whether Pier 48's current condition would need substructure pile repair or seismic work before a rehabilitation: no Port document read states the pier's present condition. The 2016 historic resource evaluation says the north apron and the east end of the south apron "are severely deteriorated and therefore closed to public access" and records a partial seismic retrofit of the substructure in 2002, and the EIR says "Seismic upgrades ... are necessary in order to support the proposed uses at Pier 48" (replacing 675 apron piles); both describe the Anchor Brewing scheme, not a current plan.

Pier 48 dimensions: the 2016 historic resource evaluation (HRE) says the pier was originally to have been a much longer pier (the HRE gives no length), drastically shortened to 623 ft because of a mud-filled 'valley' 800 ft offshore; the 1924-26 Biennial Report quoted in the HRE announced Pier 48 as 610 ft long and 376 ft wide (the 1,200-ft figure in that passage is Pier 45's).

Current use of Pier 48: the 10-year lease approved in 2018 to China Basin Ballpark Company, LLC covers up to about 212,000 sq ft; no later document confirming the lease is still in force was found. Giants Enterprises (whose office is 24 Willie Mays Plaza) markets Pier 48 as a 200,000+ sq ft venue for up to 10,000 people.

Status of the Pier 48 rehabilitation: the Port's Mission Rock project page (read 2026-09-24) still lists 'Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48' among what Mission Rock 'will be'; no Phase Submittal including Pier 48 was found in the documents read. The Port's January 2018 staff report says a rehabilitation may proceed 'based on the parties' development of a feasible pier use plan and practicability in relation to the buildout of the remainder of the Project' and that staff and the sponsor would work with state and federal preservation offices to qualify it for historic tax credits (the report notes pending federal tax reform threatened them); no later source on the tax credits was found.

records.notes: Pier 48 -- historic pier (two parallel steel-truss transit sheds, Shed A and Shed B, plus a connecting Shed C added 1937-38 at the bayward end; 261,000 gsf per the Historic Resource Evaluation, which also describes an open-air 'valley' between Sheds A and B, paved in asphalt with remnants of the Belt Line Railway spur tracks). Built 1928-30 (substructure begun 1928; bulkhead wharf completed July 17, 1929); a contributing resource to the Port's National Register-listed Embarcadero Historic District. IDENTIFICATION: this blklot has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll, but its real, surveyed shape (including the visible gap between sheds matching 'the Valley') matches Pier 48's footprint and location when overlaid on satellite imagery (Pier & Point's own overlay check, not a cited source). Marketed by Giants Enterprises as an event venue (corporate events, trade shows, concerts, conferences, galas, per its venue page) and approved in 2018 for a ten-year lease to China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and special events (Board of Supervisors Resolution 43-18; no later document confirming the lease is still in force was found); the historic rehabilitation (to follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards) had not happened as of the Port's Mission Rock project page (read 2026-09-24), which still lists 'Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48' as part of what Mission Rock 'will be'. Anchor Brewing was slated as primary tenant for about 209,000 gsf of useable space (182,000 gsf brewery/distillery) spanning Sheds A, B and the valley (HRE); Anchor announced in July 2023 that it was ceasing operations (KQED), and in May 2024 its Potrero Hill brewery was bought by Hamdi Ulukaya's Shepherd Futures, which is working 'to help restart the brewery operations' (SF Standard); no source read states that the Pier 48 plan was formally cancelled. Recorded as 'existing' (a real, actively-used historic structure, not yet redeveloped per the masterplan) rather than 'complete' or 'planned'. LOT CORRECTED 2026-09-17: this row joined blklot 9900048, which DataSF's Assessor roll retired on 2020-06-12 (the date DataSF records for dropping it from the roll); the live lot for the pier is 8719A001 (recorded the same day, active; DataSF Parcels acdm-wktn). Its shape also takes in the pier aprons -- the Design Controls' 'Pier 48 Apron' open space (Section 3.6) is therefore inside this record rather than drawn separately (Pier & Point's own reading of the lot shape).

open_questions: Whether the building is Visa's global headquarters or its market support center: Bisnow (2019-11-06) headlined "Visa Will Move Global HQ" to Mission Rock and the Port's October 2023 memo says "Parcel G will serve as Visa's global headquarters"; SF YIMBY (2024-09-05) says "Though once expected to serve as the Global Headquarters for Visa, the building is currently operating as the Visa's Market Support Center", and Fieldwork's September 9, 2026 release calls it "the new commercial tower that is home to Visa's Market Support Center". The SF Examiner (2024-09-04) reports Visa's June 2024 announcement that it had located its "headquarters and global market support center" there. Visa's own June 7, 2024 company post uses both terms (subtitle "Visa's New Headquarters and Market Support Center"; "our new HQ"). Visa's FY2024 annual report (Form 10-K) could not be read (sec.gov refused access). Also, no source gives the date Visa signed its lease: Bisnow (2019) says "Visa will lease", and the Port's April 5, 2024 memo says the office space "is 100% leased to Visa".
Construction cost and Visa's lease term and rent: not disclosed in anything read (Bisnow gave no term).
Vertical construction start date: SF YIMBY says early summer 2021; the Port's December 2021 update says the site was 'approximately one year into' Phase 1 construction. No groundbreaking date found.

LEED: SF YIMBY (September 2021 and March 2022) says the project "is aiming to receive LEED Gold certification"; no certification record has been found, and the U.S. Green Building Council's project directory was not searched.

Address: this record previously gave Visa's address as 1051 3rd St, an address that two Building B sources (Mitsui Fudosan press page, CommercialSearch listing) attach to Building B; removed 2026-09-29. The building is at Toni Stone Crossing and Dr. Maya Angelou Lane (SF Examiner, Sept 2024), 300 Toni Stone Crossing (Fieldwork page).

Fieldwork taproom opening: the company's press release (dateline July 28, 2026) announces the "grand opening" for "Saturday, July 26" and also says the taproom "officially opens to the public on Monday, July 26"; July 26, 2026 was a Sunday, so the day is not settled. A later company release (EIN Presswire, September 9, 2026) says Fieldwork Mission Rock "has been welcoming guests since its soft opening earlier this summer" and that it "will celebrate the official grand opening of its Mission Rock taproom September 25–27". This record shows only that the taproom was open to the public by late July 2026, per the company. An official grand opening on September 25-27 is not shown as an event: both releases are announcements, and no source written after those dates has been read.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (the parcel was part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot before Mission Rock construction; no source read dates the end of parking use) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.

Visa's exact move-in date: the Port's Oct 2023 and April 2024 memos give expected occupancy (1Q24, April 2024); the earliest post-event sources read are Visa's June 2024 announcement (per SF Examiner) and SF YIMBY on Sept 5, 2024.
Tenants shown open on old sources (Via Aurelia, Proper Food) rest on sources dated Oct 2025 and Sept 2024 respectively; not re-confirmed since.

Date of the Phase 1 submittal: the Port Commission documents (Item 8B, 2023-10-06; Item 12A, 2025-03-07) say "On April 4, 2019, Developer submitted to the Port its 'Phase Submittal' for 'Phase 1' of the Project"; the developer's Phase 1 Overview (Port Commission Item 11D, Attachment 1, submitted 2019-07-02) says "The Phase 1 submittal (submitted on December 4, 2018 and revised on April 24, 2019)". The sources do not agree, so the milestone is dated to April 2019, the one month both name, and neither day is shown.

A business registration for Cybersource at 300 Toni Stone Xing exists since 2024-06-06 (Cybersource Corporation, no end date, DataSF Registered Business Locations); no source read shows an office open there, so Cybersource is not listed as a tenant. Searches found no page that names Cybersource in this building.

records.summary: WORKac's 8-story commercial building on Parcel B, with Breakthrough Properties assisting on the life-science real estate (SF YIMBY, 2022) and marketed as Class A office/life science after its June 2023 TCO. It houses the district's blackwater recycling plant and has since leased to the Golden State Warriors (71,000 sq ft, October 2024), Coinbase (150,000 sq ft, 2025) and Nvidia (45,000 sq ft, reported November 2025). A July 21, 2026 report (publication date) says Grey's Florals is set to open a store inside MNT Studio's space at 1090 Dr. Maya Angelou Lane in August 2026 (an announced, expected date; no opening is confirmed).

open_questions: Construction cost: no actual or contract construction cost appears in anything read; the only figure is the $78,083,460 estimated and revised cost on the building permit, which is a filed valuation.

Groundbreaking date: no source read gives one. The Registry's June 22, 2021 article (paywalled after the lede) has a "Breaks Ground" headline, but its lede says Tishman Speyer "is planning to break ground"; the Port's December 2021 update says Parcel B "completed all necessary pile driving work" and was preparing to begin vertical construction; SF YIMBY (March 7, 2022) says "Less than three months ago, the vertical work started for the structure"; the Port's October 2023 memo lists "Commenced construction of all four Phase 1 vertical buildings" without a date.

Square footage: sources give 272,770 (SF YIMBY), 281,639 (the Port's 2019 appraisal table), 295,000 (The Real Deal), 313,952 (a Commercial Real Estate Direct repost of Commercial Property Executive) and 300,000 (ArchDaily and Hathaway Dinwiddie). The split in this record's map notes (258,994 office + 13,773 retail, which adds to 272,767) comes from a contractor page that could not be read.
Lease terms and rents for the Warriors, Coinbase and Nvidia: undisclosed in every report read.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (the parcel is part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot that Mission Rock replaces; no source read says when parking use ended) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.
When Nvidia's lease commences: The Real Deal (Nov 21, 2025) says only that it 'is slated to occupy 45,000 square feet'; no commencement date appears in any source read.

Loeb & Loeb's pages (an undated experience page and a news item dated May 27, 2025) describe a 150,000 sq ft Building B lease for 'a leading cryptocurrency company' without naming Coinbase in their text (the name appears only in the experience page's URL). The Real Deal (May 28, 2025, citing the San Francisco Business Times) names Coinbase for 150,000 sq ft at Building B.

MNT Studio is shown as open because its own Mission Rock page says 'CLASS SCHEDULE IS NOW LIVE' and that classes can be bought with a membership, two-week trial or class credit packages (page read 2026-10-12). The page gives no opening date and no 'now open' statement, and no news report or post-opening source has been read, so the studio's opening date is unknown. Grey's Florals' August 2026 opening inside MNT's space has not been confirmed.

A business registration for Fort Point Physical Therapy at 1090 Dr Maya Angelou Ln Ste E exists since 2026-07-03 (DataSF Registered Business Locations; the same owner registered a second location at 290 Division St Fl 2 the same day); no source read shows the clinic open, so it is not listed as a tenant. A booking page on Jane App lists a 'LuxFit' location at 1090 Dr Maya Angelou Ln with a contact email at fortpointpt.com, and LuxFit's own page mentions physical therapy services without naming the clinic; neither gives an opening date.

Flour + Water Pizza Shop's opening date: PMQ Pizza (April 9, 2025) says the company 'has opened' the shop, while Appetito (published 11:00 AM EDT on April 14, 2025, before the shop's 11:30 a.m. opening hour in Pacific time) says it 'has landed at Mission Rock' and gives no opening date. The sources do not agree on a day, so only April 2025 is shown.

Board of Supervisors approvals in 2018: the Notice of Determination and the Port's October 2023 memo date the Board's affirmation of the EIR certification to March 6, 2018 (Resolution 33-18 per the Port), but the Port's September 2019 report says the Board "approved the Project" on February 13, 2018 and its recitals also cite Resolution 33-18 for the Development Agreement approval in February 2018; this record shows only the March 6 EIR action.

Square footage by use: SF YIMBY gives 272,770 at topping out (230,890 office, 13,760 retail); the Port's 2019 appraisal table gives 281,639 total and 265,205 office; the Warriors release gives 295,000; the 2025 Coinbase report gives 313,952.
Warriors' space in Building B: The Real Deal gave 71,000 sq ft on two floors in October 2024 and 70,000 sq ft in its May 2025 article.

records.summary: Pedestrian paseo on the Shared Public Way north of Exposition Street, between Parcels A (The Canyon) and G (the Visa building). records.summary: The 1941 Navy-built plate shop and mold loft at the heart of the World War II 'New Yard' (about 248 by 242 ft in plan, Aiken monitor roof), the first and so far only Phase 1 building delivered under Brookfield's Pier 70 DDA: lifted about ten feet against sea-level rise (12 ft per the contractor), rebuilt by Perkins&Will (architect) and Plant Construction (contractor) as a ground-floor market hall, second-floor maker studios and third-floor offices, and issued a temporary certificate of occupancy in January 2022. The DDA terms call for a 66-year, $1-a-year Port lease (no executed lease has been found); nearly 90% leased per a Port staff report dated August 7, 2026 (heard as an informational item on August 11, 2026; the minutes call Building 12 the only vertical project so far), with two venture capital firms leasing the whole third floor (The Real Deal reports General Catalyst signed for it).

open_questions: Construction cost of the Building 12 rehabilitation itself: not stated anywhere; only the $237.4M Phase 1 total (Oct 2022) and the $150M infrastructure Notice of Completion figure exist.

Whether the 66-year Building 12 lease has been executed, and its date: the DDA sets the trigger, but the Port documents read (Item 11A dated August 7, 2026, and the Commission minutes of July 8, 2025 and August 11, 2026) do not mention a Building 12 lease approval. Item 11A says the Developer "has also signed leases with two venture capital firms for the entire third-floor office space", which does not say whether the Port lease exists. Other Commission agendas from 2018 to 2026 were not searched.
The lift height is given as 9 ft (Port, 2018), 10 ft (Perkins&Will) and 12 ft (ENR, Plant); square footage as 200,000-230,000 depending on source.
The address appears as 1070 Maryland Street (Brookfield, 2026 reports) and 180 Maryland Street (2023 Real Deal report); this record uses 1070.
Sven Ceramics' opening date at 1070 Maryland St is not given by any source found.

Tenants named in Port Item 11A are current as of its Aug 7, 2026 date only; the two third-floor venture capital firms are not named by the Port, and The Real Deal names General Catalyst as taking the entire third floor and Monograph Capital as having leased in 2024, so which firms occupy which space is unresolved.

Standard Deviant's exact opening day: the Chronicle (June 4, 2025) announced Friday, June 6, and SFist's same-day roundup (June 6, 2025) says "Open as of today (Friday)"; the SF Standard (June 25, 2025) reports it open and, on a visit whose date it does not give, "less than two weeks in". No source dated after the opening states the day itself.

No hosted photograph: the four D4D photographs of Building 12 and the D4D Figure 6.6.1/6.6.2 page were removed on 2026-09-29 because the D4D credits its photos to SITELAB urban studio and to Shae Rocco / Forest City (private parties) and grants no reuse licence. No 'now' photograph with a stated open licence was found.

Floor area of Building 12, by source: 118,890 sq ft over two floors historically (NRHP), while ENR calls the original a 60,000-sq-ft warehouse; after adaptive reuse, 230,000 sq ft per the architect; the contractor's page gives both 220,000 sq ft (in its text) and 230,000 sq ft (in its Size field), with 45,000 sq ft of mezzanine and 60,000 sq ft of office; about 200,000 sq ft per the 2026 Real Deal report.

Lift of Building 12, as built: the structure was raised approximately 10 feet per the architect and 12 feet per ENR and the contractor, to sit above 100-year sea-level-rise projections. Planned: the Port's 2018 release said it would be elevated 'nearly nine feet'; that is a plan, not an as-built figure.

Tenants of Building 12, in full: Port Item 11A (Aug 2026) names Standard Deviant Brewing, Breadbelly, Sven Ceramics, Bay Padel, The Plenary Co., Studio Duskus, Marbled Mint, Prowl Studio, Scuderia, Zai Divecha and Emi Grannis, and says two venture capital firms have leased the entire third-floor office space but does not name them. The Real Deal (Jan 2026) reports General Catalyst signed for 70,000 sq ft, taking the entire third floor, and that Monograph Capital 'inked a lease there in 2024'; which firms share the third floor is not stated.

records.name: Sophie Maxwell Building
records.summary: Eight-story, 105-unit, 100% affordable workforce housing building at 1212 Maryland St (corner of Humboldt St), the first building completed in the Potrero Power Station redevelopment; designed by Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects, built by Swinerton for owner Fifth Space (formerly Associate Capital; the Development Agreement annual reports name Found Middle LP as developer of Block 7B), which the Port says was completed in August 2025 (DBI closed its new-construction permit in August 2026), held its grand opening in October 2025 and began housing households at 50-110% AMI in November 2025; the SF Chronicle reported in July and August 2026 that it was about 90% leased, the August report attributing the figure to Fifth Space.

open_questions: Bond amount and issuer for the CalHFA bond-recycling debt (and whether CSCDA or another conduit was involved): looked in the Port memo 10A, the four DA annual reports, the Chronicle (Oct 2023, Aug 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025), SF YIMBY, Hoodline; no dollar amount for the bonds is stated anywhere.

Total development cost: only Hoodline (Dec 2025, citing the Chronicle) gives '$50 million'; the Standard gives $670,000 per unit (105 x 670,000 = about $70M). The two figures are inconsistent and neither is from a primary document.

Construction completion and Certificate of Occupancy dates: the Port memo says construction was 'completed in August 2025', while DBI's record for the new-construction permit (202212229038) shows it completed on 2026-08-28 (a permit closing, with its related revision permits closed the same day); no Temporary Certificate of Occupancy date was found. The 2025 DA annual report (due 2026) is not yet on the SF Planning page.

Construction start: the 2023 annual report and press give the groundbreaking ceremony as Oct 12, 2023 (site permit issued Oct 25, 2023), but the 2024 annual report says Found Middle 'commenced construction ... in June 2024' and the 2023 report says the construction contract 'commenced in 2024'. Both are recorded; the June 2024 date is probably the DA-defined commencement.

Design review dates: the annual reports list Block 7B as 'Approved by Planning Department, 1.5.22; Planning Director Memo dated 3.2.22'. The signed approval letter is dated March 2, 2022; the Jan 5, 2022 event is not otherwise documented. The submission day also differs: the staff memo says the Design Review Application was submitted on December 17, 2020 (its plan index lists a Planning pre-application dated 12/17/2020), while the annual reports' table gives 12.18.20. Likewise the site permit application: the 2023 annual report says 12.20.22, DBI says filed 2022-12-22.

Parcel: the design review memo lists parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006; the block/lot 4232020 used here must post-date the Phase 1 Final Map (recorded July 26, 2022). The plan sheets in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports print "PARCEL NUMBER: 4232 - 020", and DataSF lists block/lot 4232020 as active at 1212 Maryland (record added 2022-08-30); the design review plan sheets label it 'Block 7B - Lot 10', and DBI's permit record for the new-construction permit still shows block 4232, lot 006.

Land conveyance to Found Middle: the DA Housing Plan requires conveyance at no cost in fee or by ground lease; the approved Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (March 19, 2024) was not among the documents reviewed, so fee vs. ground lease and term are unknown.

Lottery: the SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says a random lottery would be held later that month, while the May 2025 Housing Plan amendment exempts 100% affordable projects that receive no direct City money from the MOHCD lottery. Whether Sophie Maxwell is a 'City Financed Unit' project is not stated.
Unit mix as built: Swinerton (contractor's own material) gives 70/21/14; the 2022 approval gives 63/28/7 of 98. No City document with the 105-unit mix was found.
Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) calls it a 'six-story building'; every other source says eight stories. Treated as an error in Hoodline.

No hostable 'now' photograph found: Wikimedia Commons searches for 'Sophie Maxwell Building', 'Potrero Power Station' and 'Dogpatch Power Station' returned no photo of the building (only pre-2011 power plant images). Henrik Kam's photos (SF YIMBY, AIA CA) are not openly licensed; linked only.

Citizen Portal's AI-generated summary of the Oct 2025 opening mentions six Homeless Prenatal Program families among the first residents and 'resident parking'; not used because it is machine-generated from a video and the design approval states no vehicle parking.

Whether Fifth Space's Essential Housing Fund closed and the Sophie Maxwell Building was contributed to it: the SF Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) said the fund was expected to close the following week; searches on 2026-09-29 found no later source confirming either.

Exact day residents first moved in: ABC7 (Oct 20, 2025) gave Nov 1 as the planned date and Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) says only that first families began moving in during November; no source gives the actual day.

Developer of the Sophie Maxwell Building: the annual reports name Found Middle LP as developer of Block 7B, and their notices are addressed c/o Associate Capital, now called Fifth Space, the owner named by the contractor; no source states in words how the entities are related. The project sponsor for design review was California Barrel Company LLC.

Landscape architect: Plural Studio is listed as landscape architect in the plan-set legend of the 2023 annual report; the firm's own project page lists the project and its collaborators (LMS, CBG Engineers, RMA Irrigation) but does not state its role.

Lender negotiations: the SF Chronicle (August 3, 2026) says the developer pitched "roughly six banks before finding one willing to structure the deal" and "Negotiations with JPMorgan took another seven months"; the SF Standard (October 15, 2025) says that to qualify for the program the firm "had to work 18 months with five banks and three law firms". The counts and durations differ and may describe different phases.

open_questions: The UC Regents' Finance and Capital Strategies Committee had the project before it as Action Item F5 for its September 18, 2024 meeting (asked to adopt the CEQA findings, approve Amendment No. 12 to the 2014 Long Range Development Plan and approve the design); no minutes or action record was read, so the outcome of that item is not confirmed.

Reported square footage varies across four dated sources (Aug 2025 SF YIMBY, Feb 2026 SF YIMBY, the Feb 2026 Planning Director memo, and Bisnow) by up to about 22,000 sq ft (about 278,000 sq ft is Pier & Point's own sum of the Planning Director memo's three figures, 685 + 89,476 + 187,819 = 277,980 sq ft; SF YIMBY's August 2025 figures sum to 278,915; 285,500 in February 2026; about 300,000 in Bisnow), and the figures do not all measure the same thing; no single figure is treated as final here.

Overall completion date is reported inconsistently: Chronicle (Jul 2026) says opening in phases from 2028; Bisnow (May 2025) said completion by 2029; SF YIMBY (Feb 2026) says overall completion expected 2030. Not reconciled.
The Real Deal's May 9, 2025 article on the $575M bond issuance is paywalled and could not be checked; Bisnow's coverage of the same financing was used instead.

No source found giving a signed lease date between UCSF and the developer. The UC Regents' September 18, 2024 item F5 says "All lease terms are expected to be 30 years in duration", an expected term for the proposed structure, not a signed lease.

As of 2026-09-29, the Regents' September 2024 CEQA-findings attachment says the project 'is now being considered for final approval'; no Regents minutes or action record recording adoption (or its date) was found, so the timeline says the findings were put before the Regents.

Who the general contractor is: SF YIMBY (February 9, 2026) says "Webcor Builders is the general contractor", while IBank's April 2025 staff report says "The Construction Company/Developer is DPR Associate Capital". No building-permit contractor of record was checked.

As of 2026-10-12, no closing or pricing document for the IBank bonds was found. IBank's staff report for its April 23, 2025 board meeting (Resolution No. 25-09) is a request for authorization with an "Expected Closing Date" of May 28, 2025; the ground-lease/sublease arrangement is recorded as the plan described there and in Bisnow's May 2025 report.

The $575 million figure is a ceiling: IBank's staff report (board meeting April 23, 2025, Resolution No. 25-09) recommends bonds "in an aggregate amount not to exceed $575,000,000" and gives an expected closing date of May 28, 2025, and says the bonds "will be secured by an Indenture and sold through a public offering to Goldman Sachs & Co., LLC, as representative of the underwriters". Bisnow (2025-05-13) reports a plan to sell bonds, not a completed sale. No closing document or issued amount was found, so no financing is recorded as closed.

Floor area of the building, by source: the Design Review approval (Feb 2026) gives approx. 685 sf retail, 89,476 sf laboratory and 187,819 sf Institutional Healthcare (Non-Hospital); SF YIMBY (Aug 2025, citing Sept 2024 plans) gives 188,550 sf institutional healthcare, 89,680 sf laboratory and 685 sf retail; SF YIMBY (Feb 2026) gives 285,500 sf occupiable floor area in total (182,650 institutional healthcare, 102,200 lab, ~700 retail); Bisnow (May 2025) gives ~300,000 sf overall.

Ground lease structure: as announced in May 2025 (Bisnow), the California IBank would sell more than half a billion dollars in tax-exempt bonds to Goldman Sachs and lend the proceeds to the nonprofit Campus Facilities Improvement Association, which would ground-lease from the Regents of the University of California and sublease to Associate Capital, which would build out the site. This is the planned structure; no closing or pricing document has been found.

open_questions: Whether the final parcel map has been recorded: the CEQA Notice of Exemption covers only the tentative map, and DataSF's parcels layer showed lots 8711029A and 8711029B (active) and no new lots for Block 4-East on 2026-10-12, so the Phase I and Phase II lots do not yet exist as separate Assessor parcels.

Affordability figures differ across sources and are not reconciled: the April 2026 CEQA Notice of Exemption says all residential units other than manager units "will be dedicated to lower-income households (earning no more than 70% of Area Median Income" (HUD and TCAC basis); the September 2024 ENA staff memo says 30-80% of AMI as defined by MOHCD, with a subset up to 95% MOHCD AMI; the developer's own project site (mb4e.com, undated, and mentioning a July 1, 2026 event) says 35% to approximately 95% of the area's median income. The binding restriction will be the TCAC regulatory agreements, which the Notice of Exemption says are to be recorded before building permits; no recorded agreement was found.

Construction start and completion dates are all expected dates, not events. The developer's own project site (mb4e.com, undated) gives Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and completion Q2 2029, Phase II start Q1 2028 and completion Q3 2030, pending financing. OCII's schedules of performance (Exhibit L to Resolutions 03-2026 and 04-2026) give estimated Notice to Proceed of February 2027 (Phase I) and February 2028 (Phase II) and estimated Certificate of Final Completion and Occupancy of July 2029 and October 2030.

Two of the February 2026 resolutions name the Phase I borrower "Mission Bay 4 Associates, L.P." (Resolution No. 02-2026's recital on the concurrent Phase I loan, and the resolving clause of Resolution No. 03-2026), apparently a slip; the September 2024 staff memo, the operative clause of Resolution No. 02-2026 and the loan agreement in Exhibit A to Resolution No. 03-2026 name it "Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P.", the name used here.

No public official's or community group's stated position on the project as a whole has been found and sourced. OCII's September 2024 staff memo records that OCII staff presented the recommended developer to the Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee on May 9, 2024 and "the MB CAC had no objections".

OCII's September 2024 staff memo and its attached RFQ say the site "is currently in use as a temporary parking lot without any structures" and "is currently serving as a surface parking lot", with termination of the parking operator's lease "anticipated for early 2027"; these are 2024 statements, and Pier & Point's own on-site observation of a parking lot on 2026-09-13 is not a published source. No cited document says whether the project is administratively separate from the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan; the memo mentions only modeling "bulk and tower separation restrictions similar to those applied to the Mission Rock project".

A City Spring 2026 development forecast was cited for the same schedule, but its document is no longer available at the published address and could not be read; the construction start dates rest on the developer's own site (mb4e.com: Phase I Q1 2027, Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing).

records.notes: Mission Bay South Block 4 East -- 398-unit, 100% affordable (30-95% AMI per SF YIMBY, 2025) two-phase development (Phase I: 165 units/16 stories on the southern half of the block, facing China Basin and Third Streets; Phase II: 233 units/23 stories on the northern half, facing Mission Rock and Third Streets, per the 2026 OCII Notice of Exemption), plus an approximately 1,253 sq ft ground-floor retail space (same Notice of Exemption; SF YIMBY's 2025 article gave 1,280 sq ft), at 1290 3rd St (DataSF Parcels) on the block bounded by Mission Rock, Third and China Basin Streets. Developed by Curtis Development + Bayview Senior Services under SF's Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) in the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Project Area. No cited source describes it as part of, or administratively separate from, the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan (the Verde/Canyon rows above), though it sits next to that area and faces a street named Mission Rock St. Site use: Pier & Point observed a surface parking lot here on the ground (2026-09-13); OCII's September 2024 staff memo and its attached RFQ also describe the site as a surface/temporary parking lot (a 2024 statement). Construction: the developer's project site (mb4e.com) lists Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing, with bid packages through Q3 2026; a City Spring 2026 development forecast was cited for the same schedule, but its document is no longer available at the published address and could not be read. Not under vertical construction as of 2026-09-13 (Pier & Point's own observation), despite likely visible fencing/site-prep activity. NOTE: added after Pier & Point's own on-the-ground observation of this lot; the other facts were checked against OCII commission exhibits, the Notice of Exemption and DataSF parcel records. (mb4e.com; sfyimby.com/2025/06/renderings-revealed-for-23-story-affordable-housing-in-mission-bay-san-francisco.html)

records.summary: Block 12 West -- the 1.6-acre parcel that OCII's August 2026 presentation calls the last remaining development parcel in Mission Bay South (listed as vacant land in the 2015 property management plan) -- is the subject of an MOU between OCII and landowner FOCIL-MB LLC to subdivide the site into a roughly 1.16-acre, ~265-unit 100%-affordable project (up to 90 ft) and a roughly 0.43-acre, ~270-unit market-rate project with inclusionary affordable units (up to 250 ft); on October 6, 2026 the OCII Commission voted to adopt Resolution No. 23-2026, authorizing the MOU (agenda item 5(c); five commissioners voted yes per the minutes). The MOU is only a first step: the minutes record the Executive Director saying the Commission was "just agreeing to talk" and was "in the beginning of the planning process".

open_questions: No named developer was found for either half of the split parcel; OCII's presentation references a forthcoming RFP for the affordable-housing half only.

No firm entitlement timeline beyond 'environmental review, late 2026' was found; subsequent steps (Owner Participation Agreement amendment, Redevelopment Plan amendment, Design for Development, Blocks 11-12 Major Phase application, subdivision map) are listed only as an ordered sequence with no dates. The only dated term is the MOU's own: it expires on the earlier of two years after its effective date and the completion of those steps (MOU attached to Resolution No. 23-2026, section 2).

No press coverage (SF Chronicle, SF Standard, Mission Local, Potrero View, YIMBY) of the 2026 MOU proposal was found; all substantive detail traces back to OCII's own documents, so this remains a thin, single-source record pending independent coverage.

No cost, budget or subsidy figures for developing Block 12 West were found in any source reviewed. The only dollar figure read is a not-to-exceed amount of $440,817 in an OCII staff memo (Agenda Item 5(d), Meeting of November 7, 2023) for a consultant's environmental review of Blocks 4 East and 12 West together, which is a contract ceiling, not a project cost.

No construction-start or completion date has been found for either half of the subdivided parcel, and no expected-completion milestone has been added (as of 2026-09-20): the only whole-plan-area date in OCII's own documents is the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Plan's own 30-year administrative term (Ordinance No. 335-98, effective from Nov 2, 1998), which sets when OCII's authority under the Plan ends, not when a project actually gets built -- using it as a stand-in for a construction-buildout target would misrepresent an undeveloped, still-unentitled parcel as complete in about two years. It stays on the timeline's open-ended 2038+ placeholder until a real entitlement/construction schedule exists.

As of 2026-09-29, the site's current use is not stated in any source read (the OCII deck does not describe it; the 2015 plan says 'Vacant Lot/Land'); the earlier 'surface parking lot' wording had no source and was removed. The OCII CAC agenda link previously cited is no longer available (page not found); no record of the August 13, 2026 meeting itself was found.

The minutes print the Block 12 West resolution number two ways: the item heading on p. 4 reads "(Resolution No. 23-2026)", as do the October 6, 2026 agenda and the resolution itself ("Resolution No. 23-2026, Adopted October 6, 2026", in capitals), but the adoption line on p. 5 reads "Resolution No. 22-2026" (in capitals), the number the minutes also print for item 5(b), the Mission Bay North refunding bonds. This record uses No. 23-2026. The minutes' opening quorum call lists Commissioner Hakimi as absent, yet they record Commissioner Hakimi moving and voting on items later in the meeting; the vote on item 5(c) is recorded as five yes votes. The minutes are a PDF created October 14, 2026 and posted on OCII's public-meetings page; whether the Commission has yet approved them is not stated in the sources read.

Current use of Block 12 West: DBI permits at 385 Channel describe a warehouse or storage building on the parcel: permit 201306179714 (filed 2013-06-17, "demolition of portion of building (warehouse", status expired) and permit 201712055462 (filed 2017-12-05, "demolish 1 story storage bldg", recorded complete 2019-05-17), so a building may have stood there in 2015 despite the December 2015 Long-Range Property Management Plan's 'Vacant Lot/Land' classification. No source read observes the demolition itself.

The 2015 Long-Range Property Management Plan lists it as 'Vacant Lot/Land' at the northeast corner of Channel Street and Mission Bay Drive (APN 8710-006); its current use is not stated in any source read. OCII and land owner FOCIL-MB LLC have proposed a Memorandum of Understanding to subdivide it (the August presentation targeted OCII Commission approval in September 2026; the MOU was item 5(c) on the Commission's October 6, 2026 agenda as Resolution No. 23-2026, and no source read confirms whether the Commission voted) into a 1.16-acre, ~265-unit affordable project (up to 90 ft) and a 0.43-acre, ~270-unit market-rate project with an inclusionary requirement (up to 250 ft) -- both preliminary and subject to change, with entitlements (Redevelopment Plan/Design for Development amendments, OPA housing-program amendment, tentative/final subdivision map) still ahead as of the August 2026 presentation.

open_questions: Exact opening/occupancy month is not confirmed; no source read gives one. In January 2021 Potrero View said the building 'is expected to welcome inhabitants as early as January 2022' (an expected date); HomeRise's own site gives only 'Opened: 2022'; the landscape architect's page reads 'STATUS: Completed, 2023'; DBI records permit 201901281440 complete on 2023-04-24 (a permit closeout, not an opening date); and this record's map notes give 'late 2022' per sfchronicle.com, which could not be read. The milestone is recorded as the bare year 2022, approximate.
Unit count is 141 in nearly all sources but the architect's own current portfolio page says 140.

Square footage varies: ~92,000 sq ft (Potrero View, 2021) and 92,535 SF (the architect, Leddy Maytum Stacy) vs. 100,000 sq ft (SF YIMBY, 2021). No source says what is counted, so the difference is not explained.

No AMI-specific figure was found tied officially to this project beyond the general permanent-supportive-housing program description; no official OCII/MOHCD underwriting document for Block 9 itself was located.
Could not confirm whether any units are specifically set aside for veterans.

HomeRise's project page footer lists 'David Baker Architects' and 'James E. Roberts-Obayashi Corp.' under 'Our Partners & Sponsors'. The same donor and sponsor list (which also names Amazon, Google and Microsoft) appears on HomeRise's home page and does not name an architect or contractor for this project. BRIDGE Housing, the architect's own site and SF YIMBY identify Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects and Cahill Contractors.
Construction cost figures conflict across sources ($42M construction/$86M total per SF YIMBY, vs. a per-unit figure in Potrero View that implies roughly $54M); not reconciled.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.
The date the 410 China Basin St building was confirmed 100% affordable is not stated in the permit data found.

Residents' incomes: Potrero View (January 2021, before opening) said residents 'will likely have incomes below 20 percent AMI and pay 30 percent of their income towards rent', and HomeRise's CEO described a typical resident as on Social Security of roughly $1,100 or $1,200 a month; no post-opening data on residents' incomes was read.

records.summary: 400 China Basin is a 148-unit, 100% affordable homeownership condominium development (8 stories; sources give different building areas, see open questions) in Mission Bay South, developed by China Basin Partners LLC (Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers), designed by Mithun with associate architect YA Studio, and built by general contractor Nibbi Construction/Baines Group; it held a ribbon-cutting on September 26, 2025 (Office of the Mayor release of that date; the project's press release had announced the date and SF YIMBY reported on October 2 that it had taken place the week before).

open_questions: Square footage is inconsistent across sources: 180,063 sq ft (OCII 2021 filing) vs. ~200,000 sq ft (SF YIMBY 2025) vs. 165,000 sq ft (the architect's own page) -- possibly different measurement conventions, not resolved.

Total development cost is not shown because the figures differ. OCII's November 5, 2021 Evaluation of Request for Financing gives \"Total Development Cost (TDC): $134,220,472\" and \"TDC/unit: $906,895\" on its project-description page, and a sources-and-uses total of $135,145,636 ($913,146 per unit) on page 5 (both pre-construction estimates); the developer's August 21, 2025 press release calls it a \"$130 million project\"; no final as-built figure was found in a post-completion OCII/MOHCD document.
OCII's Oct 2023 memo projected a temporary certificate of occupancy in August 2024, roughly 13 months before the Sept/Oct 2025 opening; no source explains the gap.

The general contractor's name appears variously as 'Nibbi Construction,' 'Nibbi Brothers' and 'Baines-Nibbi JV' across OCII documents; the OCII evaluation lists the contractor as 'Nibbi | Baines' in its project table and 'Nibbi Construction/Baines' in a later table, and its section 5 says 'selecting a JV of Baines-Nibbi JV'; the two firms are treated as one pairing, and the architect's news post names only 'Nibbi'.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

When construction began: OCII's loan memo of 2023-10-20 (Loan Committee, 400 China Basin additional gap funding) says "Project financing closed in June 2022, and construction began in July 2022" (Section on financing); SF YIMBY (2025-10-02) says "Construction had started for the eight-story multiunit complex in 2023". The sources disagree by a year, so this record shows no construction-start milestone. The OCII memo, written after the event, also reports construction 50% complete as of September 1, 2023, which is the earliest construction date shown here.
Building area: OCII's 2021 filing gives 180,063 sq ft of total building area (129,712 residential); SF YIMBY's 2025 completion article cites approximately 200,000.

records.name: Mission Bay School
records.summary: SFUSD's Mission Bay School is a four-story TK-5 campus at 1415 Owens St (about 81,800 sq ft per the design team; SF Standard says approximately 80,000) designed by DLR Group and built by McCarthy Building Companies, the design-build team SFUSD hired in 2022, under a reported $95.4 million construction contract funded by SFUSD's 2016 bond program (Proposition A). SFUSD held the ribbon cutting on August 6, 2026, and the first students (nearly 200, per the SF Chronicle) arrived on the first day of school, Monday, August 17, 2026. That makes it Mission Bay's first public elementary school; the SF Standard calls it SFUSD's first new school in a decade, while the Chronicle counts 20 years since the last new school (Dianne Feinstein Elementary, 2006), since Willie L. Brown Jr. Middle was rebuilt in 2015.

open_questions: Full-build-out (2032) enrollment capacity is reported differently: SFUSD's August 7, 2026 press release says the school will "grow to a 550-student elementary school serving Pre-K through 5th grade", SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says more than 400 students, and 2022 pre-construction reports said up to 550 and 600. The district's own figure is 550.

Project cost is reported two ways: SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says the school "was built under a $95.4 million construction contract" (it does not name the parties; SFUSD's August 7, 2026 release names McCarthy Building Companies and DLR Group as its delivery partners), while The Registry (August 6, 2026) calls the project a "$129 million design-build effort" and the SF Chronicle (August 17, 2026) "the nearly $130 million project". No source read breaks down the difference.
No SFUSD document names a square-footage figure officially; the 81,800/82,000 sq ft figures come from trade press, not the district itself.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

CORRECTED 2026-09-24: the 2032-08 grade-growth milestone (school growing one grade per year to full TK-5) was tagged with a 'planned' status, which the site's timeline read as the whole record reverting to pre-construction 'planned' status for any date past August 2032 -- even though the school is already built and open. The same error had been found on 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)', and every record was then checked for the same pattern, which found this one. That milestone describes enrollment growth, not a change in construction status, so it should never have carried a status at all; the status was removed. The milestone's date, text and sources are unchanged.

The school site's transfer: SFUSD's August 7, 2026 press release says "The land parcel was formally transferred from UCSF to SFUSD in 2022, although the plan for a school in Mission Bay has been in the works since 1998" (an event year stated by the district; no day is given). No source was found for a 1988 set-aside, so that was removed on 2026-09-29. No exact construction-completion date was found: SFUSD scheduled completion by January 2026 and the SF Chronicle (August 17, 2026) says construction wrapped up late last year; [Updated 2026-10-12: the first day of school, Monday, August 17, 2026, is now confirmed from a readable source written the same day, after the event: the SF Chronicle (Aug 17, 2026) reports "A brand-new school had opened. Nearly 200 San Francisco students poured into Mission Bay School" and describes the first day of class there.]

Fourth floor of Mission Bay School: SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says the 'Mission Bay Hub' STEM program draws students from six high schools; SF Chronicle (August 17, 2026) says about 90 students from five high schools are enrolled this year, with capacity at 120 (the sources may count different things). In 2022 it was described as a STEM-focused linked learning hub preparing students for careers in health, bioscience and STEM fields.

records.notes: The Exchange on 16th, 1800 Owens St -- formerly Dropbox's headquarters, now partly rebranded 'Icona: Labs at Mission Bay' -- a 750,370 sq ft, 12-story office/life-science campus on a ~3.25-acre lot (141,415 sq ft per the Assessor roll), built by Kilroy Realty Corporation in 2018 as Dropbox's single-tenant headquarters (15-year lease, per Kilroy's October 2017 announcement as reproduced in its Q3 2017 SEC supplemental). Sold in 2021 for $1.08B to KKR and Longfellow Real Estate Partners, who by May 2022 were marketing more than 406,000 sq ft as 'lab-capable' space and building out turnkey labs (The Real Deal, May 18, 2022); OpenAI signed a roughly 280,000 sq ft sublease, reported in March 2026 with confirmation from a March 2026 Newmark market report (The Real Deal, Mar 16, 2026), which also reports Dropbox is planning to vacate the building entirely. Blklot confirmed against the DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls dataset (wv5m-vpq2), whose property_location and square-footage/year-built fields match the published building exactly, since the base parcel map's own address field is a stale street-frontage number (701-707 16th St) rather than the building's current mailing address. open_questions: Parcel 8721035 first appears on the Assessor roll for 2023 with the same location as lot 8721033 (rolls to 2022) and a lot area of 38,459 sq ft; the permits are filed under lot 033. No source read explains the lot merger, so the permit and 2021 year-built evidence is attached to this record through the shared 1455 3rd St address.

The map note's 486,600 sq ft combined OpenAI sublease figure and 'largest SF office lease since 2018' (The Real Deal) could not be read (access refused); the San Francisco Standard says only 'nearly a half-million square feet' and 'largest office lease in San Francisco since 2018'.

No source read gives a groundbreaking date or an opening or move-in month; the Department of Building Inspection completed date is a permit closeout date. SocketSite (2016) expected occupancy by mid-2018; the permit shows 2021.
Sources disagree on stories (11 on the Assessor roll, 12 proposed on the permit, eleven in ArchDaily).

Stories: ArchDaily describes "an eleven-story tower at 1455 Third Street" and the Assessor roll (parcel 8721033, roll year 2022) gives 11.0 stories, while DBI new-construction permit 201508245071 reads "erect 12 stories for office, daycare" with 12 proposed stories (DataSF i98e-djp9). The permit may count a level the other two do not; no source explains the difference.

Completion year: sources give different dates of different kinds. The Department of Building Inspection shows new-construction permit 201508245071 complete on 2021-04-01 (permit completion event; DataSF i98e-djp9, filed under lot 033); the Assessor roll for lot 033 (2022 roll) gives year built 2021 (Assessor year built; parcel 8721035's own 2023 to 2025 rolls give none); ArchDaily's project page says 'Completed in 2022' (completion year for the two-building project). The page shows the 2021-04 and 2022 entries side by side, each labeled by kind; no source read reconciles them.

Whether OpenAI occupies 1455 3rd St, and since when, is not settled by any source read. Its status here is 'announced', the 2023 expected state from lease reports (the San Francisco Standard, 2023-10-27, says OpenAI 'will be taking over' the space). Later reports speak of OpenAI's footprint without naming a building as occupied: the San Francisco Standard (2026-02-26) says OpenAI 'now occupies more than 1 million square feet in San Francisco’s Mission Bay neighborhood'; Hoodline (2026-01-09) says the company 'controls about 486,600 square feet through a sublease it picked up from Uber at 1455 and 1515 Third Street'; The Real Deal (2026-03-16) says OpenAI 'in recent years has subleased two buildings from Uber at 1455 and 1515 Third Street'. DataSF Registered Business Locations lists OpenAI registrations at 1455 3rd St starting 2022-12-28 and 2024-03-05; those are registration dates, not opening dates.

open_questions: Whether Uber still occupies 1515 3rd St is not settled by any source read. Uber's FY2025 annual report (Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025) gives its principal executive offices as '1725 3rd Street, San Francisco, California 94158' and says in Note 6 (Leases): 'We own two adjacent office buildings, Mission Bay 1 & 2'; it does not name 1515 3rd St or say that Uber left it. The Real Deal (2023-10-29) reported that Uber 'has leased two of the four buildings of its Mission Bay headquarters' to OpenAI and 'will continue to occupy the remaining buildings on its campus'. DataSF Registered Business Locations (read 2026-10-12) still lists 'Uber Technologies Inc' at 1515 3rd St with a location start date of 2020-06-25 and no end date, while a registration for Portier LLC (owner Uber Technologies, Inc.) at 1515 3rd St ends 2023-12-31. These are a 2023 lease report, a headquarters address and business registrations; none is a source written after an Uber move-out, so the tenant list's 'closed' for Uber at 1515 is an inference that has not been confirmed.
Uber's FY2022 annual report, which the changelog says gave 1515 3rd Street as its principal executive offices, could not be read (the SEC's site refused access) and is not relied on here.

OpenAI's occupancy of 1515 3rd St is not dated, and the tenant list's 'announced' is a 2023 expected state: the San Francisco Standard (2023-10-27) says OpenAI is leasing the two buildings and 'will be taking over' the space. Later reports speak of OpenAI's footprint without naming a building as occupied: the San Francisco Standard (2026-02-26) says OpenAI 'now occupies more than 1 million square feet in San Francisco’s Mission Bay neighborhood'; Hoodline (2026-01-09) says the company 'controls about 486,600 square feet through a sublease it picked up from Uber at 1455 and 1515 Third Street'; The Real Deal (2026-03-16) says OpenAI 'in recent years has subleased two buildings from Uber at 1455 and 1515 Third Street'. The DataSF registration for OpenAI at 1515 3rd St (location start 2024-12-09) is a registration date, not an opening date.

No source read gives a groundbreaking date or an opening or move-in month; the Department of Building Inspection completed date (2021-04-01) is a permit closeout date, the Assessor gives 2021 as year built and ArchDaily lists the project year as 2022.
The permit proposed 7 stories while the Assessor roll and ArchDaily give 6; not reconciled.

Developer of 1515 3rd St: the joint venture terms come from Alexandria's 3Q14 report, which is cited as saying 49% of the $125.0 million purchase price was funded by Uber; an ownership share for Uber is not stated. The report itself could not be read on the SEC's site, so these quotations are unconfirmed.

open_questions: No post-opening source was read: the March 2016 opening rests on Potrero View's February 2016 announcement ('opens next month'), the permit closeout and the Assessor year built. Kaiser's own facility page redirected in a loop and could not be read.

The STUDIOS Architecture project page (cited in the map note for architect, 220,000 sq ft, Whiting-Turner, LEED Platinum and the purchase by Kaiser) was not found when requested, so architect, contractor, LEED rating and the sale are not recorded here.

The developer (map note says Alexandria Real Estate Equities, citing its 3Q14 supplemental) is not named in the pages read: that supplemental lists other Owens Street addresses but not 1600 Owens. One SocketSite (2013) reader comment calls it "a developer building which was already approved by the planning commission and building department"; the comment does not name the developer, and comments are not a source. No source read says Kaiser bought the building.
Kaiser's sale price and date, and the construction start date, are not stated in any source read.

Stories: Potrero View (2016-02), the 2013 altered site permit (201308083838, reduced from 10 to 9 stories) and the interior fit-out permit (201312194614, a 9-story shell) say nine; the Assessor roll cited here gives number_of_stories 10.0 for parcel 8709020 (DataSF wv5m-vpq2, roll year 2022). The difference is not resolved; the 10 may reflect the original design or a counting convention.

records.notes: Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices, 1600 Owens St -- a 9-to-10-story outpatient medical office building (sources disagree: STUDIOS Architecture's own project page says nine stories with 220,000 sq ft; Potrero View also says nine stories, while the DataSF Assessor tax roll says 10 stories and gives property_area 250,884 sq ft, likely including garage/below-grade area; Potrero View cites 200,000 sq ft) with primary care, OB/GYN, pediatrics, dermatology, orthopedics, optical and occupational health -- no emergency department. Built speculatively by developer Alexandria Real Estate Equities, architect STUDIOS Architecture, design-build general contractor Whiting-Turner; STUDIOS Architecture's project page says Kaiser Permanente "purchased the project" from that speculative development; the sale date, price and seller are not stated in any source read here. Completed 2016 (STUDIOS); Potrero View reported in February 2016 that the offices would open in March 2016 (a pre-opening announcement; no post-opening source read). LEED rating also disputed (STUDIOS claims Platinum; Potrero View says Gold) and left unresolved. Blklot 8709020 confirmed via DataSF's Assessor Parcels dataset and Historical Secured Property Tax Roll (property_location '1600 OWENS ST', use_code COMO/property_class OMD, year_property_built 2016); zoning_district 'MISSION BAY REDEVELOPMENT' (MB-RA) in DataSF's Assessor parcel data confirms the Mission Bay South project area.

records.name: Five88 (Mission Bay South Block 7 West)
records.summary: A ~230,000 sq ft affordable apartment building (sources differ on its height; see open questions) at 588 Mission Bay Blvd North (Mission Bay South Block 7 West) with 200 affordable apartments (SocketSite, 2015) and over 10,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, developed by Related California in partnership with Chinatown Community Development Center and designed by David Baker Architects. SocketSite reported in January 2015 that groundbreaking was expected in April 2015, and the architect's own project page lists the building as completed in 2017. In October 2025 the city issued a $8,000,000 building permit (202506037829) to excavate and shore tunnels under the podium slab so the plumbing main trunk lines can be replaced.

records.notes: Five88 (Mission Bay South Block 7 West), 588 Mission Bay Blvd North -- 200 affordable apartments (SocketSite, Jan 2015), a ~230,000 sq ft mixed-use development (sources differ on its height: SocketSite says four stories, the architect five stepping down to four, DBI permits five) with over 10,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, 52 parking spaces and 306 bike spaces. Developed by Related California in partnership with Chinatown Community Development Center; architect David Baker + Partners. Targets households averaging up to 60% of Area Median Income, with 50 of the 200 units reserved with a preference for university/healthcare employees. SocketSite (Jan 2015) reported groundbreaking as expected in April 2015 with occupancy targeted for September 2016 (no report of the groundbreaking itself found); DataSF's Assessor roll (wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8711226 with year_property_built 2017 and 208 units on the 2023-2025 rolls (no year built or units on earlier rolls). Explicitly identified as 'Block 7 West' in SocketSite's own January 2015 coverage, which is how this record was matched to the plan's '7W' label after an error in fitting the plan drawing to the map had placed that label on the wrong side of 4th St (see the changelog). DataSF's Building Footprints layer records no footprint of its own for this parcel (the one fragment intersecting it, mblr SF8711227, actually belongs to the neighboring Family House parcel at their shared boundary) -- confirmed visually against satellite imagery -- so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly, the same treatment as Mission Bay Block 6 East on this same block face.

records.notes: 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East) -- 142 affordable apartments plus a manager's unit, owned by Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation (TNDC) per Ventura Partners (SocketSite, 2016, names TNDC as the units' manager), designed by Mithun Solomon and Studio VARA, ~$76M cost. Serves households up to 50% of Area Median Income, with 20% of units reserved for formerly homeless families; includes a mews of 12 townhomes and 10 flats facing a mid-block walkway (up to three stories along the western edge) and up to seven ground-floor commercial spaces fronting 4th St. SocketSite (Aug 2016) reported construction slated to commence in late September 2016 and take two years (a forecast; no report of the groundbreaking itself found); Ventura Partners, its commercial property manager, lists the project as completed in 2019; DataSF's Assessor tax roll lists blklot 8711505 as 'Multi-Family Residential' with no year built recorded. OCII's 2016 resolutions give the whole 143-unit development the address 626 Mission Bay Boulevard North; the Assessor lists the separate parcel 8711506 as 626 Mission Bay Bl, Commercial Retail (not part of this parcel). DataSF's own Building Footprints layer only captures small fragments of this building's roof (a handful of small fragments, a few over 100 sq m, totaling well under the real footprint) rather than its full mass, confirmed visually against satellite imagery -- so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary (a single-building, single-parcel site) rather than the incomplete building-footprint layer, consistent with how every other real-parcel record here is drawn.

records.notes: Channel Pump Station, 455 Berry St -- an above-grade SFPUC wastewater pump station between 6th and 7th Streets, constructed in 1979 and upgraded in 2010, with a pumping capacity of 103 million gallons per day, operating continuously in both dry and wet weather; conveys flows through the Channel force main to the Southeast Treatment Plant (source: SF Planning, Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7 Wastewater, 2020, which describes it as operating). OCII's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map marks this site 'X1' in its gray/non-developable category; X1 had earlier been left without a record here after an unrelated mislabeling of a street cluster. DataSF Assessor confirms blklot 3806006 as 'Industrial Gov Mixed/Other Use' at this address, with no building data on the roll. Status 'existing' (the 2020 SF Planning report above describes the station as operating; not touched by Mission Bay's redevelopment, staying as-is) per this project's own convention for pre-existing infrastructure untouched by redevelopment (e.g. UCSF's own Utilities Plant, Pier 70's Building 21).

records.name: 1450 Owens Street
names: Alexandria Center for Science and Technology – 1450 Owens
records.summary: 1450 Owens Street is a 7-story laboratory/office building (133,000 sq ft of laboratory, 49,999 sq ft of office and 2,600 sq ft of ground-floor retail, per SF YIMBY in February 2023; sources give different total areas, see open questions) at the Alexandria Center for Science and Technology's Mission Bay Megacampus, developed by Alexandria Real Estate Equities. Sources conflict on when it came online (see open questions); in March 2026 Gladstone Institutes announced a long-term lease of more than 105,000 sq ft as its anchor tenant, with about 20 labs opening there in early 2027. DBI permit records show a permit to build out offices and R&D labs on levels 1 and 5-7 was issued on July 14, 2026, and a further alterations permit amending it was filed on September 17, 2026 (permit events, not an opening).

open_questions: Total building area is not settled: Bisnow (2026-03-25) calls it a "208K SF facility" (and separately mentions 110K SF of above-ground parking); the DBI new-construction permit 202012281760 describes "a 7-story, type 1-a, warm shell and core for approximately 192,000 gross square feet"; SF YIMBY (February 2023) lists 133,000 sq ft of laboratory, 49,999 sq ft of office and 2,600 sq ft of retail, which add to 185,599 sq ft. Commercial Property Executive (2026-03-27) is the source this record had used for "~215,000 sq ft"; its page refused access on 2026-10-12, so that figure is not shown.
Exact topping-out date is not sourced; only that it had occurred by the San Francisco YIMBY article's February 2023 publication.

When the building came online is in conflict: this record had taken 2024 from Commercial Property Executive's March 2026 coverage, which could not be read on 2026-10-12 (access blocked), so that year is not verified; Bisnow (2026-03-25) says the property "is expected to come online in 2027"; DBI new-construction permit 202012281760 (7-story warm shell and core) has status 'complete' with a completed date of 2025-05-19 (DataSF i98e-djp9), which records the permit's closure, not an opening or occupancy date. No month or day is sourced, and no source read states that the building came online in 2024.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the summary dated Gladstone's anchor lease to 2024, a year this record had taken as the building's online year. Gladstone announced the lease on March 25, 2026 (labs opening early 2027) and Commercial Property Executive reported it on March 27, 2026; the summary now says so. Changelog row 542 had reported this fixed in September, but the summary had not changed.

records.notes: 1450 Owens Street -- a 7-story, ~1-acre laboratory/office building at the Alexandria Center for Science and Technology's Mission Bay Megacampus, shell-and-core construction permit shown complete by DBI on 2025-05-19 (one trade-press report says the building came online in 2024; Bisnow says 2027 for the leased space; the sources disagree) (133,000 sq ft lab space, ~50,000 sq ft office, 2,600 sq ft ground-level retail per Commercial Property Executive/EurekAlert coverage of the building). Gladstone Institutes (whose own separate headquarters at 1650 Owens St, blklot 8709008, is already tracked) announced in March 2026 that it had secured 105,000+ sq ft of laboratory space here (occupancy expected in early 2027) for its data science and genomic immunology institutes, per Gladstone's own release and Bisnow (both dated 2026-03-25) -- this record tracks the real Alexandria-owned building/parcel, not a separate Gladstone-owned site. DataSF Assessor confirms blklot 8709017 at 1450 Owens St; the DataSF Building Footprints layer only captures small roof fragments (~688 sq m total) of this real ~4,607 sq m parcel, so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly, consistent with how this project handles other footprint-layer gaps (e.g. 1300 Fourth Street, Block 6E).

open_questions: Exact month/day of the 2020 completion is not sourced, only the year.

A WRNS Studio project page titled 'UCSF Parking Structure' (wrnsstudio.com/projects/ucsf-parking-structure/) lists a completion of 2012 and describes a 10-story, 627-stall, 223,602 sq ft structure that it calls the 'Owens Street Parking Structure', without giving a street number. Watry Design's page for 1470 Owens lists completion 2020, 4 levels, 317 stalls and 109,200 sq ft, and the Assessor's year built for this parcel is also 2020, so the WRNS page is treated here as describing a different, earlier building, not this parcel. Which building the WRNS page depicts is not confirmed.

As of 2026-09-29, no source found dates the start of physical construction; the timeline carries the permit issue date (2018-10-03) and completion (2020) only. Watry Design's page lists its owner as 'Developer', so no source read names UCSF as the garage's owner.

WRNS Studio was earlier named as the designer; the only cited designer page (Watry Design) names Watry, and the WRNS 'UCSF Parking Structure' page has not been confirmed to be this garage, so WRNS is not stated here.

records.notes: 1470 Owens Street -- a parking structure serving multiple UCSF Mission Bay life-science buildings and the adjacent Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices, designed by Watry Design (its project page lists the owner only as 'Developer'; no source read names the garage's owner); garage entrance on Nelson Rising Street off Owens St (ParkChirp). Features a green-wall security screen and 25 EV charging spaces (per the designer's own project page); ParkChirp lists it as a parking facility. Identified by Pier & Point during a map review of open ground between already-mapped sites. DataSF's Assessor data (dataset wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8709019 at 1470 Owens St; this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary (the DataSF Building Footprints layer has no captured footprint at all for this parcel, likely a parking-structure gap in that dataset).
