records.summary: Mission Bay by Windsor is a 129-unit, 5-story apartment building at 360 Berry St, completed in 2017 per DataSF Assessor records and then known as "Eviva at Mission Bay"; GID announced on August 8, 2017 that it had acquired the property and that it would be known as Mission Bay by Windsor. City permit records show the original building permit (#201312265046) marked complete on June 15, 2017, and a later lobby-upgrade permit (#202106152477, $60,000 estimated cost) completed on October 7, 2022; both are permit-record dates, not opening dates.

records.name: Prequel Park
names: Portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72
records.summary: The interim Prequel Park: about 2 acres per the Port memo (2.5 acres per the Power Station website, 2.75 per press), designed with Heatherwick Studio around Unit 3 and the 300-foot Stack, on the Power Station sub-area (which the 2018 Draft EIR describes as owned by the project sponsor) and on Port-owned shoreline land (portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72, leased to California Barrel Company for 66 years under Port Lease L-16662), of which about 0.4 acre is on Port property. The Port Commission amended the lease's permitted uses on Nov 18, 2025 (Resolution 25-70); the Port memo of Nov 2025 targets construction in 2026 and opening in 2027, and the project's BCDC amendment was issued June 26, 2026. No source found confirms construction has started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Pier & Point's own composition, not a drawn plan: no source read draws Prequel Park's boundary (the Port memo's Exhibit 1 is an unscaled schematic of the ownership sub-areas and the interim improvements; the Power Station website's map page shows an aerial rendering with no outline). The shape is the band of shoreline between Block 9's south edge and Block 4's north edge (each extended to the shore), joined with Block 9, Block 4 and Humboldt Street Plaza, which the interim park is read to occupy until those are built. That makes it 13,876 m2 (3.4 acres). Sources give about 2 acres (Port memo, Calendar Item 10A, Nov 14, 2025), 2.5 acres (Power Station website) and 2.75 acres (press), so none of these figures is certain. It overlaps Block 9, Block 4 and the plaza on purpose, and the overlap ends when those are built.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 (shoreline shown as 'Waterfront Park'); Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A) for the ~2-acre interim Prequel Park. (An earlier version also cited a Spring 2026 development-forecast listing that could not be located online and is not relied on.)
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own: 92% of the shape lies inside DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St), an undivided lot that also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza, the Stack and parts of the shoreline parks (checked 2026-10-11).
notes.regulatory_context: The Potrero Power Station-land portion of the ~2-acre Prequel Park interim open-space project (see 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' for the Port-jurisdiction portion and its own sourcing; the Port memo of Nov 14, 2025 puts about 0.4 acre on the Port premises). Per the Port memo the park is to include a multi-purpose lawn and sport courts, amphitheater seating, a quarter-mile walking and running track, water access and restrooms. Construction start is targeted for the third quarter of 2026 per the memo's p.4 (p.2 says the first quarter of 2026); no source confirms a start, so the status is 'planned'.

open_questions: Corrected 2026-09-24: the timeline had shown 'under construction' today but 'planned' a couple of years in the future, because this record's map-shape status ('under construction') had not been updated to match its own sourced finding that no dated source confirms a construction start. The status was changed to 'planned', matching the related 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' record. Still true as of that correction: no dated source confirms construction has started; the latest primary statement is the Port memo (Nov 2025, start Q1 or Q3 2026) and ICA SF ('Construction begins in 2026', Oct 2025).

Whether the 2024 annual report's temporary activation east of Delaware Street and Stack Plaza ('Delaware East Park/Stack Plaza'; Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture, schematic design from Aug 2024, construction then expected Q1 2026) is the same scheme later branded Prequel Park with Heatherwick Studio is not stated by any source.

Application filing: Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says the application was expected to be filed 'on Thursday'; SF YIMBY (Oct 2025) says 'In May, the developer submitted plans'. No Planning case number found.

Cost: the developer's own $15-20 million estimate (Chronicle, Potrero View) is the only figure for the whole park. DataSF building-permit applications for Prequel Park, all with status 'filed' and no issued date in the data read on 2026-10-12, list estimated costs of $4,000,000 (202512051053, block 9 landscape and exterior work, filed 2026-07-01), $1,500,000 (202512051066, Unit 3, filed 2026-07-01) and $1,500,000 (202512081182, admin building level 1, filed 2026-01-15): about $7.0 million for those three scopes. These are applicants' estimates for permit scopes, not contract values or the cost of the park; no construction contract was found.

BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA; Board of Supervisors final passage Oct 6, 2026, enacted Oct 13, 2026 per Legistar's 'Enactment date') amends the Phasing Plan; whether it changes hotel or interim-park obligations is not stated in the legislative digest, and the draft DA text was not read.

Has Prequel Park construction started, and has the 2026 start been rescheduled? No dated source confirms that construction has started as of 2026-09-17 (searched sfport.com, sfplanning.org, Chronicle, SF YIMBY, Potrero View, SF Standard, developer site, ICA SF); as of 2026-10-10 no source read reports a groundbreaking or a new start date, and the developer's site still describes the park without reporting construction. DataSF's building-permit data read on 2026-10-12 shows the three Prequel Park applications (202512051053, 202512051066, 202512081182) as 'filed', with no issued date, and the BCDC permit tracker shows only the June 26, 2026 issuance of Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02. The map status of this record is 'planned'.

BCDC amendment 2019.006.02: this record's mapping notes and timeline said it was 'issued June 19, 2025' (corrected 2026-09-29). The BCDC permit tracker gives June 19, 2025 as the date the application was RECEIVED and June 26, 2026 as the date ISSUED. The amendment document itself was not found on bcdc.ca.gov (2018-2019 DRB/Commission URLs now return 404; the tracker is an embedded table that could not be saved as text). Treat 2025-06-19 as application date, 2026-06-26 as issuance.

Port memo 10A is internally inconsistent: p.2 says construction start Q1 2026 / opening Q1 2027; p.4 says Q3 2026 / Q3 2027. Both are recorded; the p.4 dates follow the DBI-submittal sentence and are the more detailed statement.

The 'Spring 2026 SF development pipeline' listing ('Potrero Power Station - Prequel Park', developer FIFTH SPACE, scope demolition/grading/utilities/stormwater/landscaping) cited in this record's mapping notes could not be located online; no URL is on file.
Lease commencement date and the recorded lease are not in the corpus; 'March 2087' implies a ~March 2021 start but no source states it.
Exact footprint of the ~0.4 acre on Port land: memo Exhibit 1 is an unscaled rendering; not digitized.
Planning temporary use authorization (June 2025): no case number or document found on sfplanning.org.

Port Commission minutes of Nov 18, 2025: item 10A passed on consent with no discussion or public comment; the minutes URL is https://www.sfport.com/media/10953/download?inline (the meeting page's 'm11182025.pdf' link returns 'page not found').

No source read draws Prequel Park's boundary. The Port memo's Exhibit 1 is an unscaled schematic of the Power Station and Port sub-areas and the interim improvements, and the Power Station website's map page is an aerial rendering with no outline, so the shape on the map is Pier & Point's own composition.

Area of the whole interim park differs by source: about 2 acres (Port memo, Calendar Item 10A), 2.5 acres (developer site), 2.75 acres (Chronicle, ICA SF), 'almost three' (Potrero View); the BCDC amendment scope is 57,000-62,000 sq ft within the shoreline band only. The shape on the map is larger (about 3.4 acres) because it includes the ground of Blocks 4 and 9 and Humboldt Street Plaza, which the interim park is read to occupy until they are built. The developer-land share is not stated anywhere.

How long the interim park will run: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says Thursday through Sunday 'for a period of at least five years beginning in 2027'; the San Francisco Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says it 'would likely last for five years'; the Potrero View (October 2025) says it would be 'replaced by a hotel sometime after 2032'. No source gives a closing date or says what replaces it on each parcel.

Historic structures in the park: the Potrero View (October 2025) describes Unit 3 as a former eight-story fossil gas-powered boiler; ICA SF's exhibition page (undated) plans a 'vertical gallery' in the Stack from fall 2027 (expected date). The San Francisco Chronicle (May 22, 2025) describes 'a skeleton-like structure that sits adjacent to the stack and used to hold a turbine' that 'will be filled with plants'; it does not name it Unit 3, and treating the two as the same structure is Pier & Point's reading.

Port land share of the park: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025), p.3, says 'approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises'; its Exhibit 1 splits that as about 0.15 acre for access to the future dock and about 0.25 acre for a multiuse lawn. The memo's text does not say who owns the rest of the roughly 2-acre park; Exhibit 1's ownership legend shows the interim improvements over the 'Power Station sub-area' and the 'Port sub-area', and the Draft EIR (October 2018) describes the Power Station sub-area as 'currently owned by the project sponsor'. Whether any of the park lies on other ownership is not stated.

Port parcel area: the Port's Item 13B memo (February 20, 2020) and the Draft EIR (October 2018) describe 2.9 Port-owned acres in three pieces: the largest, 1.6 acres, between the Power Station sub-area and the Bay (including water area for a potential recreational dock); 1.3 acres along 23rd Street; and a piece under a tenth of an acre ('Port Lands = 1.6 acres' on the memo's Exhibit 5, February 2020). The Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says about 2 acres of the project's open space will be on Port-owned shoreline property (the lease Premises). No source says the Premises equal the 1.6-acre piece or where the Prequel Park footprint lies within it.

Sea level rise design: the Port's Calendar Item 10A memo (November 14, 2025) says the shoreline is elevated for projected sea level rise of 66 inches, adaptable if exceeded; the Port's Item 13B memo (February 20, 2020) gives 90 inches of sea level rise plus 42 inches of storm surge, 132 inches above current MHHW.

Public Trust Easement: under Resolution 20-12 the option covers approximately 1.97 acres of the developer's lands along the shoreline and in the 23rd Street right-of-way (the Port's Item 13B memo, February 20, 2020: 'approximately 1 acre of shoreline area and approximately 0.97 acres of roadway'). No source read shows the option was signed or recorded.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 21 (Substation No. 5)
records.summary: A circa-1900 steel-framed, corrugated-metal-clad shop with a double-gable monitor roof (101 ft 2 in by 75 ft 6 in, 10,172 sq ft), the only surviving Risdon Iron Works building and the earliest steel-clad structure in the district, later Bethlehem's Substation No. 5. One of the three historic buildings the DDA obliges Brookfield to rehabilitate: a 66-year lease at $1 a year must be signed within a year of completing the building on Parcel E1 (placed in Phase 2C by the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan, presented at an informational hearing on August 11, 2026 with no action taken, and not adopted), so no rehabilitation has begun.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) as of 2026-09-17 -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 21: position rests on satellite imagery and the D4D's building figures (the Port's 'fronting Slipways Commons' wording describes its planned position after a future relocation, not where it stands now) and its combined size (734.96 sq m) is within 4.4% of the 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) footprint given in D4D Figure 6.5.4. The match rests on position, size, and satellite corroboration, not an explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there). A small 49 sq m footprint ~9m away was not included. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. Superseded history: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-13 -- this building's rehabilitation has not started as of the most recent primary sources found (see regulatory_context). Pier & Point reads Assessor lot 4052010 (1,215 m2, active) as the lot on which the D4D's Building 21 box, the planned relocated position, falls; this surveyed footprint (734 m2) lies instead 587 m2 inside lot 4052009, which is assigned to Parcel E1, and 147 m2 inside lot 4052007. No document read names these lots, so the drawing from the surveyed footprint is kept.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. This replaced, on 2026-09-17, a long chain of diagram- and text-based approximations (their sources are kept below for history). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, PDF p.11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility" (future tense: a planned relocation as part of the rehabilitation); (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in the Assessor parcel data and no distinct lot was identified for it: DataSF's Building Footprints carry the legacy lot id mblr SF4052001 for it and many other structures across central Pier 70, but blklot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), and which current lot holds Building 21 was not established from a cited source. This feature therefore uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.regulatory_context: Building 21, which the Port and the D4D call "Substation No. 5", is planned to be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast as part of its rehabilitation (Port Commission memo dated Aug 3, 2017, Item 11A, Exhibit F: "would be relocated"; no source records that the move has happened). Sources name different original uses without saying which came first: the same memo says the building "dates to the Risdon Iron Works period circa 1900", and the Port's 2011 RFI calls it "the former Risdon Ironworks Building", and is one of three historic structures (with Buildings 2 and 12) the Pier 70 Design for Development commits to rehabilitating per the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (Pier 70 D4D S6.6.1). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row marked it "complete," inferred (not directly cited) from Building 21 being grouped in the D4D's rehabilitation commitment alongside Buildings 2 and 12. Follow-up research found the Port's own 28-acre site page (sfport.com/projects-programs/pier-70-28-acre-site) describes Building 21's rehabilitation as still to come -- the page shows a rendering, not a photo, captioned "Rendering of Pier 70 Building 21," under a "Rehabilitation of three historic buildings" heading, implying a future vision rather than a completed project. This is corroborated negatively by the Port's own June 2025 project-update deck (sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/Pier%2070%20Update%20-%20June%202025%20v3.pdf), which shows Building 15's relocation and several Building 12 milestones but never mentions Building 21. Status corrected from complete to existing -- a standing historic structure, not yet rehabbed, with no confirmed construction timeline. The use "mixed" is taken from the Port's plan that Building 21 "will accommodate arts and institutional uses" (Item 11A, Exhibit F); no source read describes any present use of the building.

records.name: Mission Rock Block C
records.summary: A future Commercial Mixed Use block on 3rd Street south of Building B, entitled for a 190-ft building over a base with a maximum height of 90 ft on one side and 60 ft on the other with required ground-floor retail. Not yet built as far as the record shows: the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and Phase 2 is in pre-development, with construction possible 'as early as 2027' (the update does not name Block C), and the Commission's minutes record Resolution 26-34, a $10 million Port Capital investment in Phase 2 pre-development, as passed unanimously on June 9, 2026; in 2023 a Port Commission resolution recited that Phase 2 was not currently financially feasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one: treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping this record from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial Mixed Use only (no residential option) per the Design Controls' Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1) -- ground-floor retail required. Max building height 190 ft per Figure 6.2, confirmed exactly. Positioned south of Block B, fronting 3rd St to the west and the Shared Public Way (and Mission Rock Square beyond it) to the east. No construction-start source found; the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update (Item 11A) describes the site as 'a surface parking lot' and puts Phase 2 construction 'as early as 2027'.

open_questions: No architect, program or unit/square-footage figure for Block C exists in any document read; the EIR's project-wide range is 972,000 to 1.4 million gsf of commercial space.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found; the Port's June 5, 2026 staff memo schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal for Winter/Spring 2027. No source read states Block C's present condition, so whether it remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 parking lot (Lot A) is not confirmed.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block C. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (Board of Supervisors File No. 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18 on 2/13/2018; the Port's fact sheet gives 8/15/2018 as the Development Agreement's effective date, and no source read states the DDA's own effective date) places Parcel C in Phase 2 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of May 2023 for completing Phase 2's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with Phase 2 not begun, and the Outside Date for actual completion is left to a future Phase Schedule that was never approved (Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones). No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding above that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (contractor procurement 'Winter - Summer 2027') and a 'Potential Construction Start' of Summer/Fall 2027; the memo says construction could begin 'as early as 2027' once anchor tenants are secured and gives 2027/2028/2029 vertical-start scenarios only as illustrative repayment estimates, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.

records.name: Mission Rock Block D1
records.summary: The residential half of Block D at 3rd and Mission Rock streets: a Residential Mixed Use tower entitled to 240 ft (one of three 240-ft sites with Blocks A and F) wrapping the Block D2 parking structure along Third Street, with roughly 250,000 gsf of housing in the EIR description. Not yet built as far as the record shows: the Port's June 5, 2026 staff memo says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and Phase 2 is in pre-development, and the Commission's June 9, 2026 minutes record its $10 million Phase 2 pre-development item (Resolution 26-34) as passed unanimously (neither document names Block D1).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (the method is logged in this shape's mapping log): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. The D1/D2 line is a land-use zone boundary inside one Design Controls block, not a lot line; the Appendix marks Block D's parcel dimensions as illustrative.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m. D1/D2 split from Figure 1.1 (p.10) and the Block D standards sheet (Appendix p.190).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping each block from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use per the Design Controls' Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1). Max height 240 ft -- one of the three tallest towers planned for the site (tied with Blocks A and F), NOT a 'mid-rise' as sometimes described in secondary summaries. Sits at the 3rd St / Mission Rock St corner, fronting 3rd St -- 'marks the Mission Rock MUNI Metro Station along 3rd Street' per the Design Controls' own narrative text (Section 6.5.2, 'Block D1 marks the Mission Rock MUNI Metro Station'). Part of the same larger Block D parcel as D2, subdivided into a residential tower (D1) and a parking structure (D2).

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding above that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (contractor procurement 'Winter - Summer 2027') and a 'Potential Construction Start' of Summer/Fall 2027; the memo says construction could begin 'as early as 2027' once anchor tenants are secured and gives 2027/2028/2029 vertical-start scenarios only as illustrative repayment estimates, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.

Area of Block D1: the 97,498 sq ft (2.24 acres) figure is for Block D as a whole in the developer's March 2012 proposal, which predates the 2018 Design Controls that divide the block into D1 and D2; the table gives no D1/D2 split and the block outline may have changed.

Driveways for Block D1: the Design Controls provide driveways at the shared Block D parking facility ('Driveways shall be provided at Block D to accommodate parking facility ingress and egress'); no separate D1 driveway is stated in the passages found.

records.name: Mission Rock Block D2
records.summary: The site of Mission Rock's only permitted stand-alone parking structure, a 100-ft-max garage on the Bridgeview Street side of Block D sized in the EIR at about 2,300 spaces (837,200 gsf) to replace Giants event parking. The Port's October 2023 memo says 'Phase 2 will include the parking garage' and that the Garage Report was submitted on October 14, 2022; the memo does not name Parcel D2, so the link to this block comes from the Design Controls, which allow stand-alone above-grade parking only here. Phase 2 was slowed in 2023. The Port's June 2026 staff memo on up to $10 million for Phase 2 pre-development does not mention the garage; the Commission's minutes record that item (Resolution 26-34) as passed unanimously on June 9, 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see the mapping log): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. The D1/D2 line is a land-use zone boundary inside one Design Controls block, not a lot line; the Appendix marks Block D's parcel dimensions as illustrative. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m. D1/D2 split from Figure 1.1 (p.10) and the Block D standards sheet (Appendix p.190).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping this block from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Structured Parking per the Design Controls' Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1) -- a flat 100 ft max height (not a 90-110 ft range as sometimes described), with no upper/tower zone. Occupies the larger, eastern portion of the combined Block D parcel (D1 is the smaller residential tower at the 3rd St corner; see that entry). The April 2017 Draft EIR (Table 2-4) puts about 2,300 spaces in the above-grade parking structure on Block D (D2), with a further 700 in a below-grade garage under Mission Rock Square. The Central District Energy System was tentatively planned for Parcel A, not Block D, per a 2019 Mission Rock Partners submittal to the Port -- despite some secondary summaries placing it here.

open_questions: The Garage Report's actual space count and levels are not in the Port memo; the report itself was not located.

A 2019 Phase 1 submittal placed the district energy plant on Parcel A rather than Block D: the developer's July 2, 2019 Phase 1 overview says 'We have tentatively planned for the Central DES to be in Parcel A due to its large footprint', and the Port's June 2026 report lists the 'District Energy System (heating and cooling) located in Parcel A'.

The Port's June 5, 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal ('proposal for Phase 2 including development summary and Phase budget') for Winter/Spring 2027 and a 'Potential Construction Start' for Summer/Fall 2027 (Table 2; expected dates, not events). No source read reports a construction start, a Phase 2 budget approval or a vertical design submittal for this block, and none states the block's current use; the Developer's July 2019 Phase 1 overview forecast that Lot A, the remainder of Seawall Lot 337, would keep serving parking pending future-phase construction.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

The Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (Table 3, DDA Major Terms) describes the DDA's outside date for commencing construction of each later Phase as 'the earlier of 5 years after completion of vertical construction of the prior Phase or 14 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 2, 20 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 3, and 25 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 4'. These are legal deadlines, not forecasts. The DDA text itself was not read, so no calendar date is derived here.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D2. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The Port's fact sheet (updated June 24, 2021) lists 'Commence construction on Phase 2, including parking structure' among its five-year milestones, and the Port's October 2023 memo says 'Phase 2 will include the parking garage'. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read, so its Land Use Table and Schedule of Performance target dates are not cited here. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.
The Port's June 2026 Phase 2 memo does not mention Block D2 or the garage, so no source says whether the garage is still planned as described in the 2023 memo.

Parking spaces at Block D2: the EIR gives about 2,300, with up to 700 more in a possible below-grade garage under Mission Rock Square; the DDA describes 3,000 structured spaces project-wide to serve the project and ballpark patrons.

Area of Block D2: the 97,498 sq ft (2.24 acres) figure is for Block D as a single block, from the March 2012 proposal's parcel table; that table predates the 2018 Design Controls' D1/D2 division and gives no D1/D2 split.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2, fitted to 16 real lot corners with a typical (root-mean-square) misfit of about 0.7 m, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, document dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so using that lot would draw the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial Mixed Use only per the Design Controls' Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1). Max height is a flat 90 ft with NO upper/tower building permitted at all (Table 6.4 lists its upper-building dimensions as 'NA') -- notably lower than some secondary summaries suggest. Directly south of Block F and Mission Rock Square, one of the two blocks (with F) that actually front the square directly.

open_questions: No program, tenant or square-footage figure for Block E exists in any document read.

The Port's June 5, 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal ('proposal for Phase 2 including development summary and Phase budget') for Winter/Spring 2027 and a 'Potential Construction Start' for Summer/Fall 2027 (Table 2; expected dates, not events). No source read reports a construction start, a Phase 2 budget approval or a vertical design submittal for this block, and none states the block's current use; the Developer's July 2019 Phase 1 overview forecast that Lot A, the remainder of Seawall Lot 337, would keep serving parking pending future-phase construction.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

The Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (Table 3, DDA Major Terms) describes the DDA's outside date for commencing construction of each later Phase as 'the earlier of 5 years after completion of vertical construction of the prior Phase or 14 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 2, 20 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 3, and 25 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 4'. These are legal deadlines, not forecasts. The DDA text itself was not read, so no calendar date is derived here.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block E. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The Draft EIR's illustrative phasing (April 2017) placed Block E in Area 3 (2019-2022), a different scheme from the DDA's four Phases, and no document read states which DDA Phase includes Block E. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read, so its Land Use Table and Schedule of Performance target dates are not cited here. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 3 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date for this block.

The Design Controls approval is numbered Resolution 18-04 in the Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (a request) and Resolution 18-05 in its September 20, 2019 memo; the adopted resolution itself was not read.
Which blocks Phase 2 covers is not stated in the Port's June 5, 2026 report either, so this block's phase is not sourced from it.

Phase 2 status for Block E: the Port's October 2023 report records that the developer sent the Phase 2 Submittal on December 28, 2022, that Phase 2 was 'not currently financially feasible' and that work on it was decelerated, and models a 'hypothetical Phase 2 start date of March 2026' for illustration. The Port's June 5, 2026 report asks the Commission to approve up to $10 million of pre-development funding to accelerate Phase 2 (Resolution 26-34), with construction possible 'as early as 2027'. Neither report lists which blocks Phase 2 includes.

records.name: Mission Rock Block I
records.summary: A flex block east of Mission Rock Square across Bridgeview Street, on Long Bridge Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, developable as commercial (90 ft) or residential (120 ft) with an elevated sidewalk zone along the boulevard. No source read shows construction on it (the Port's June 2026 report on Phase 2 does not name this block, and no source read says which phase includes it).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one: treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, document dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping this record from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Flex block (Residential MU or Commercial MU), max height 90 ft commercial / 120 ft residential, same as Block H. Flanks Mission Rock Square's east edge across Bridgeview St (one street removed from the square rather than directly fronting it, like Blocks B, C and J: Figure 6.2 shows B and C across the Shared Public Way on the west and J and I across Bridgeview Street on the east).

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

records.summary: The smallest development block, a Residential Mixed Use site on Exposition Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard next to China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry, capped at 120 ft. It was in the original Phase 1 but was swapped out for Parcel F in 2019 to bring about 100 more units into the first phase; no construction on Block K is reported in the sources read. The Port's June 5, 2026 staff memo gives a Summer/Fall 2027 potential construction start for Phase 2 (an expected date, not an event) and the Commission's June 9, 2026 minutes record its Phase 2 pre-development item as passed unanimously; neither names Block K or says which blocks Phase 2 includes.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: every edge follows a DataSF lot line (one of them, the Exposition Street lot 8719A010, carries a recorded drop date of March 18, 2025 in the Assessor data (DataSF Parcels, read October 12, 2026) while still flagged active; the dataset does not say why; the Assessor has not made Block K its own lot; it is still part of the China Basin Park lot 8719A005 in the most recent DataSF Assessor parcel data checked), and the Design Controls figure trace agrees with those lines within 1.3 m at every corner. Planned, unbuilt residential block (120 ft maximum height). ANGLE CHECK: one corner here is 12.3-12.6 degrees off square, beyond the 12-degree tolerance of Pier & Point's automated shape check. Every vertex of this polygon is a real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corner (how this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log) -- the deviation is the real lot's own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Accepted as a known exception.

Using lot 8719A005 would show the park and the block as one shape.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use, fronting China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry along Terry A. Francois Blvd. Max height 120 ft -- tied for the lowest residential height limit on the site (Flex Blocks H, I and J also allow 120 ft if residential, Figure 6.2 p.151); the March 2012 Revised Proposal's narrative says 'the shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park,' preserving sightlines/stepping the skyline down toward the water. Originally slated for Phase 1 (with A, B, G) before a real, Port-confirmed 2019 swap with Block F -- the sponsors proposed changing Phase 1 from {A, B, G, K} to {A, B, G, F} to accelerate ~100 more units (~40 more affordable) and create a four-corner pedestrian intersection instead of a linear one; an interim-parking-preservation rationale sometimes cited for this swap is not supported by any source found.

open_questions: The notes on this record's map shape quote the sentence 'the shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park'. It appears in the developer's March 2012 Revised Proposal (p. 32: 'The shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park and Pier 48 near the water’s edge', one of the 'most likely scenarios' it describes, not an adopted control); it was not found in the April 2018 Design Controls, whose Block K standards page confirms the 120-ft cap.
The swap's stated reasons (units, affordable units, intersection form) are documented; no source mentions interim-parking preservation as a reason.

The Port's June 5, 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal ('proposal for Phase 2 including development summary and Phase budget') for Winter/Spring 2027 and a 'Potential Construction Start' for Summer/Fall 2027 (Table 2; expected dates, not events). No source read reports a construction start, a Phase 2 budget approval or a vertical design submittal for this block, and none states the block's current use; the Developer's July 2019 Phase 1 overview forecast that Lot A, the remainder of Seawall Lot 337, would keep serving parking pending future-phase construction.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

The Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (Table 3, DDA Major Terms) describes the DDA's outside date for commencing construction of each later Phase as 'the earlier of 5 years after completion of vertical construction of the prior Phase or 14 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 2, 20 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 3, and 25 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 4'. These are legal deadlines, not forecasts. The DDA text itself was not read, so no calendar date is derived here.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block K. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The developer's July 2, 2019 Phase 1 overview describes the original Phase 1 as 'A, B, G, and K', and the Port's September 20, 2019 memo says the swap 'moves parcel K to a later phase' without naming which one. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read. No document read states K's post-swap phase number or gives it a target date, and even the pre-swap Phase 1 slot is moot now that K itself was removed from Phase 1, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a date for this block.

Phase of Block K: the Port memos read do not say which later phase includes Block K. The Oct 2023 Port memo says the Phase 2 submittal was delivered December 2022 and decelerated in 2023 as infeasible, with a hypothetical Phase 2 start of March 2026 in its repayment model (it does not place K in Phase 2); on June 9, 2026 the Port Commission adopted Resolution 26-34 ($10 million for Phase 2 pre-development), and the Port's June 2026 report puts Phase 2 construction 'as early as 2027'.

records.name: Mission Rock Square
records.summary: The neighborhood's planned central park of about 1.1 acres in the Port's January 2018 memo (the March 2012 proposal's parcel table gives 1.32 acres, 57,626 sq ft, while its block plan labels the square 0.7 acres), an urban green framed by Blocks E and F with a lawn, a plaza with an interactive spray ground, a cafe pavilion and a tree bosque with retail kiosks; the Design Controls require wind protection, public restrooms and preserved water views. The Draft EIR includes a 700-space garage beneath it. No source read reports it built or assigns it to a phase; the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 report does not mention the square, and the Commission approved up to $10 million of Phase 2 pre-development funding on June 9, 2026 (minutes).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt public square) on the undivided remainder lot 8719A006. North edge is a recorded lot line (~0 m); the other three edges come from the Design Controls figure through a 0.7 m RMS transform (~1-3 m). Traced area 47,724 sf, smaller than the 57,626 sf the 2012 proposal gave -- the tracing is logged in this shape's mapping log. The July 2019 Phase 1 submittal planned 'two interim pedestrian plazas south of Parcels B and F'; no source read confirms that an interim plaza was built or where it sits, and the Port's June 5, 2026 update does not describe the square's current condition (its goal of transforming 'a surface parking lot' refers to the Mission Rock project site as a whole).
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls, Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151) and Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); north edge is Verde's recorded lot line (8719C001), south edge is Block E's traced north edge.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this square -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping each block from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this square touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated public open space (Design Controls Chapter 3, Section 3.3). Directly framed by Block F/Verde (north) and Block E (south), with the Shared Public Way (west) and Bridgeview Street (east) along its sides; Blocks B, C, I and J are also one street removed (Design Controls Figure 6.2). The Design Controls text states no acreage; the Port's January 2018 approvals report gives 1.1 acres ('a 1.1 acre neighborhood central gathering place called Mission Rock Square'), which matches this record's traced figure; the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table gave 57,626 sf (1.32 ac) for an earlier, deeper layout.

open_questions: Which phase will deliver the square and whether the below-grade garage option survives: not stated in any Port memo read; the Phase 2 Garage Report was not located.

Cost of the square: none published. Phase 1's China Basin Park inland budget line (Port October 2023 memo, Table 1, 'Inland CBP': $39,184,050 to $40,657,253 revised estimates) is the only comparable figure in the Port memos.

The 1.1-acre figure in the 2018 approvals memo, the 1.32 acres in the March 2012 proposal's parcel table and the 0.7 acres its block plan prints beside the square are all unexplained; the traced shape on this record's map is about 1.57 acres after clipping, per its own accuracy note.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Mission Rock Square. No document read assigns the square to a phase. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all, and the Port's October 2023 memo lists the Phase 1 vertical buildings as Parcels A, B, F and G, so neighboring Block F was built in Phase 1 while no source read says whether the square's own construction was part of it. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read, so its Land Use Table and Schedule of Performance target dates are not cited here. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones. No later Port memo or news source gives a revised target year for the square or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date.

Area of Mission Rock Square: the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel summary gives 57,626 sq ft / 1.32 acres, and the same proposal's block plan labels the square 0.7 acres; the Port's January 2018 approvals memo describes it as 1.1 acres.

records.summary: Planned conversion of Terry A Francois Boulevard between Block K and Pier 48 into a paseo. The Design Controls say it 'will become a paseo that will accommodate emergency vehicle access for up to 150' of its length', with a 28 ft waterfront zone at Pier 48 and a vehicular turnaround with one loading space. No source read describes its current use.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence on three edges (recorded lot lines, though the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 it closes against carries a recorded drop date of March 18, 2025 in the Assessor data (DataSF Parcels, read October 12, 2026) while still flagged active; the dataset does not say why); the south edge is the Exposition Street lot line extended ~23 m east, which is where the plan's Exposition Street right-of-way ends at TAFB. Planned (Design Controls Section 4.3.4: the boulevard 'will become a paseo'); no source read describes its current use. ANGLE CHECK: the map's automated shape check flags a 12.3-12.6 deg corner here (its tolerance is 12 deg). Three of this polygon's four vertices are real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corners; the south-east vertex is not, since it closes the south edge on the extended Exposition Street line. The flagged deviation is at two of the recorded corners, so it is the real lots' own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Accepted as is. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor lot lines: the north end of the Terry A Francois Boulevard lot 8719A003 between Block K, the Pier 48 lot 8719A001 and the China Basin Park lot 8719A005; named as a paseo in Mission Rock Design Controls Figure 3.1.1 (p.45), Section 4.3 (p.90) and Figure 3.6.1 (p.71).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Part of the Terry A Francois Boulevard right-of-way lot 8719A003 (DataSF Assessor parcels, recorded 2020-06-12; it also carries the roadway south of here and Channel Wharf); mapping this record from that lot would paint the whole boulevard (our mapping rationale, not a statement of the Design Controls).

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel A
records.summary: Phase 1 office parcel at 20th and Maryland Streets (per D4D Figure 6.4.2), entitled for commercial office over retail and underground parking, of roughly 350,000 gross square feet in the Port's February 2020 staff memo and roughly 240,000 in Resolution 20-07 (the two Port texts disagree; see open questions); appraised at $66 million (reported February 2020) for a 99-year prepaid lease, but Brookfield declined to proceed in June 2020 and no vertical development has started. At an informational hearing on August 11, 2026 (staff report dated August 7; no action taken) the Port presented a proposal, not yet adopted, to require escrow on Parcels A, C2B and D to close by 2029-2030 (a proposed outside date) or the Port will publicly offer them. King Street Properties announced a life-science plan for it in 2023.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4111009, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Parcel A is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 5,307 m2 against the lot's 5,013 m2; 76% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 81% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. This block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'). No source read describes what is on the block today.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4111009 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Parcel A. Lot 4111009 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4111009; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial/life-science, 90 ft max / 6 stories per Figure 6.4.2. A revised design by Grimshaw with DES Architects + Engineers (356,400 sq ft, six stories, 90 ft) was reported by SF YIMBY in Oct 2021 with the refiled Development Agreement; King Street Properties announced in Feb 2023 a six-story, roughly 300,000 sq ft speculative life-science building on Parcel A (Bisnow). No source read links the Grimshaw design to King Street's plan, and no source read supports the earlier mention of a 2019 mass-timber design or a 365,000 GSF figure (removed 2026-09-29). No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'. DataSF's building-permit data does list a new-construction permit application for the parcel (88 Maryland, permit 201908300403, filed 2019-08-30, status 'approved' on 2023-08-22, never issued), described as a '6-story ground up speculative class office bldg of roughly 356,000 sq ft', and a storm-water control review permit (202307051517, issued 2023-08-03).

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Whether the King Street Properties partnership is still in effect: the Port's June 2025 deck speaks of the life-science effort in the past tense ('prior to collapse of that industry') and the July 2026 Real Deal report describes a 300,000 sq ft office building, not a lab.
The Feb 2020 staff memo says Parcel A is entitled for ~350,000 GSF while Resolution 20-07's recital says ~240,000 GSF; which figure the DDA option actually carries is unresolved.
No source read supports an earlier (2019) mass-timber office design by Hacker Architects with Quezada Architecture that this parcel's map notes used to mention; it was removed on 2026-09-29.

No Port or press source gives a construction cost estimate for the office building. DataSF's record of the unissued permit application (201908300403) lists an estimated cost of $75,600,000 and a revised cost of $0; that is a permit-application figure, not a construction cost.

The Real Deal (July 16, 2026, citing the SF Chronicle) reports Brookfield is 'looking to start construction on a 300,000-square-foot office building if San Francisco's office recovery gains traction'; the report does not name a parcel, so it is not recorded as a Parcel A milestone.

A 2023 DataSF permit record (M1232027, issued 2023-10-17) reads 'per port of sf request, create address 950 maryland st at apn 41111/009' and carries this parcel's block and lot (4111/009); whether 950 Maryland Street is in use as a second address is not known.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4052008 and 4052012, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Brookfield's leasing brochure reportedly lists Parcel B at about 500,000 RSF (dropped from this parcel's map notes as uncited); the brochure could not be checked (pier70sf.com/leasing shows only project-wide totals of 1.82M RSF new office and 250,000 RSF historic rehab), so no square footage is stated here.
The 2017 DDA terms tie the Arts Building start to completion of 'the office building on Parcel B-2'; whether 'B-2' is a sub-parcel of B is not explained in the retrieved text.
No design submittal or appraisal for Parcel B was found in the Port Commission documents cited on this page.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel K North (PKN)
records.summary: The 1.5-acre former Port parking lot at 20th and Illinois Streets, sold in February 2019 to a TMG Partners / Presidio Bay Ventures joint venture under a Vertical DDA after a competitive offering, generating $24.2 million of land proceeds for the Pier 70 project. Planning approved the building's schematic design in November 2019. The Port's project page describes a 65-foot, 377,506 gsf building with 245 for-sale residential units over ground-floor amenity and retail space, designed by Handel Architects, while the building permit application says 241 residential units. The developers' pages call it fully entitled, Handel lists it 'In Design', and no construction start was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4110012, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Parcel K North is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 7,450 m2 against the lot's 6,313 m2; 83% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 98% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. This block is not yet built (the developers' pages call it 'fully entitled' and Handel Architects lists it 'In Design'; no groundbreaking was found in any source read). The Port sold it in February 2019 (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: '$24.2 million of land proceeds from the sale of Parcel K North in February 2019'). Presidio Bay's page calls it 'the only privately-owned land in the Pier 70 Special Use District'; that is the developer's own description, and Port Item 11A lists 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E known as the Hoedown Yard' in the same district.

open_questions: The purchase price: the only figure found is the Port's '$24.2 million of land proceeds from the sale of Parcel K North in February 2019'; the executed Vertical DDA and the Budget and Legislative Analyst report attached to File 190055 were not opened.

No groundbreaking or issued building permit was found. A new-construction permit application for 919 Illinois St (block 4110, lot 012; permit 201911258098) was filed on Nov 25, 2019 and shows status 'approved' as of Feb 25, 2021, with no issue date in San Francisco's permit data (queried Oct 12, 2026). Bisnow's June 10, 2019 article, citing the San Francisco Business Times, says TMG and Presidio Bay 'are gearing up to break ground on around 250 units of the recently purchased Parcel K North': it reports preparation, not a groundbreaking, which is consistent with the Port page's 2020-2021 design-and-permitting timeline.

Affordable housing on PKN: the 2017 memo calls the units market-rate and the 2026 report says condo projects pay an in-lieu fee toward the stand-alone affordable sites, while the Planning conditions reference Section 415 affordable units; the actual obligation is unresolved.

Unit and square-footage figures disagree between sources: the Port page gives 245 units and 377,506 gsf; TMG's page gives 245 units and 275,000 sq ft residential; Handel Architects' page gives 245 units; Presidio Bay's page gives about 241 units and 411,273 sq ft; and the building permit application says 241 residential units.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: Parcel K North was sold to a private developer in 2019 and sits outside the 28-Acre Project's DDA phasing plan, so no Development Agreement phase window applies to it; no PKN-specific schedule statement was found (the Port's November 2025 comment reported by Potrero View concerns Pier 70 generally), and the developers' own pages (TMG, Presidio Bay, Handel Architects) give no construction start or completion date, so this record stays undated.

Current build status of Parcel K North: the developers' pages (undated) call it 'fully entitled' and Handel lists 'In Design'; no source dated 2026 that names Parcel K North was found beyond Port Item 11A's mention of the 2019 sale.

Ownership of Parcel K North: Presidio Bay's own page calls it 'the only privately-owned land in the Pier 70 Special Use District', but the Port's August 2026 Item 11A (p.2) says the Special Use District also includes 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E known as the Hoedown Yard', so the developer's wording does not match the Port's description.

Stories at Parcel K North: Handel Architects ('a new 6-story mixed-use development') and the building permit application filed in 2019 ('to erect a 6-story' building) give 6; a 2022 permit revision, approved August 5, 2022, documents 7 stories over a basement under the building code's definitions of grade plane and story above grade plane.

records.summary: The roughly half-acre '20th Street Plaza' of the D4D open-space network (Section 3.10), the landscaped entry plaza on Parcel K North's 20th Street frontage at Illinois Street, designed as the gateway from Dogpatch to the Historic Core with an entry plaza, seating terrace and planted garden. The Port's Item 9B staff report (2017) lists constructing the 20th/Illinois St. Plaza among the Parcel K North buyer's obligations, and the Port's Parcel K North page says the project will include a 20th St/Illinois St Plaza; no source found reports it built (the Port's Parcel K North page schedule stops at 2020-2021 design and permitting).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 4110009 (1,365 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-13 this record showed a bounding-box trace of the Pier 70 Design for Development's Figure 3.3.1 (an illustrative, non-dimensioned plan) trimmed to the real 20th Street centerline; 72% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 57% of the lot. No document read names lot 4110009 as the plaza (the Port's plaza parcel is described in Port Resolution 17-52 as a parcel still to be subdivided); the lot is used because it holds most of the earlier drawing (72%), at the owner's direction, and the Design for Development's own name for the space is '20th Street Plaza' (Section 3.10, about 0.5 acre), so the lot's edges are not the plaza's designed edges. The lot is zoned Pier 70 Mixed Use (P70-MU) and was mapped 2019-03-14.

search_aliases: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space (Waterfront Terrace / Slipways Commons / Waterfront Promenade / Pier 70 Shoreline)
records.summary: The roughly five-acre waterfront park system of the Pier 70 D4D (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons and Waterfront Promenade, Sections 3.5-3.7) plus the roughly 1,300-foot Pier 70 Shoreline (Section 3.8), to be built by the developer and owned by the Port. Phase 1 includes three acres of parks, but the DDA ties park completion to adjacent buildings and the Port's 2026 report says the balance of Phase 1, 'largely comprised of the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be constructed on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development' and that 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward', so none has been constructed. The Port Commission heard that report at an informational hearing on August 11, 2026 (no action taken); it proposes amendments, not yet adopted, to 'better align open spaces with revised vertical development schedule'.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4052003, 4116001, 4116003 and 4116007, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery: 4052003 is zone 1 (Waterfront Terrace), 4116001 is zone 2 (Slipways Commons), and 4116003 and 4116007 are parts of zone 3 (Waterfront Promenade). No document read names these lots. Zone 4 (Pier 70 Shoreline) has no lot assigned and is not drawn, and the Port's SUD Land Use Plan splits these spaces into separate open space segments that this combined outline does not follow. The lots are the legal boundaries and may not follow the D4D's drawn edges. The open space is planned (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development). Lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, DataSF, Delaware St) was also proposed for zone 3 but is not used: it covers Potrero Power Station Blocks 3, 4 and 9 and other Potrero shapes, and Pier & Point has deferred it to the review of the Potrero Power Station site.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4052003, 4116001, 4116003 and 4116007 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155) and Figure 3.4.1 (Overview of Public Spaces, p.52).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lots of the waterfront open space. Lots 4052003, 4116001, 4116003 and 4116007 (active) were assigned to its zones 1, 2 and 3 from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram, so its outline is their union.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3) -- specifically Sections 3.5 (Waterfront Terrace), 3.6 (Slipways Commons), 3.7 (Waterfront Promenade), and 3.8 (Pier 70 Shoreline, ~1,300 linear feet). Together with Building 12 Plaza/Market Square, 20th Street Plaza, Irish Hill Corner Plaza, and Irish Hill Playground, these comprise the D4D's total nine acres of public open space (Section 3.4).

open_questions: No Port Commission schematic-design approval for any of the four waterfront open spaces was found on 2018-2026 agendas, so none appears to have reached that stage.
Which named spaces make up the three Phase 1 acres is not stated; the reading of Exhibit A above (Slipways Commons area in Phase 1) is this project's interpretation of a diagram.

Cost of the parks: the 2017 memo gives $260.5 million of eligible horizontal costs for all three phases but no park line item was extracted; the Port and developer's June 2025 project update says of November 2022 'Received NOC from City on the Phase 1 infrastructure' and 'Represented $150m investment' (NOC is the deck's abbreviation, read here as Notice of Completion), without a park breakdown.

Interim use: the Elevation Sky Park venue is planned as a five-year interim use ('DURATION: Period of 5 years', community engagement deck, June 25, 2025) on 'Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone, away from waterfront buffer zone', and the Port's Executive Director described its location as 'where that street [22nd Street] meets the Bay' (Port Commission minutes, July 8, 2025); whether any of it sits on future park land or only on parcels E3/H2 is unresolved (see the E3 record).

Whether the hosted photograph qualifies as a 'before' view (taken within two years of construction starting) cannot be checked because no construction start is dated for this record; Wikimedia Commons titles it only 'Old shipyard building at Pier 70', and that its foreground is the future open space is our reading of the camera position.

records.name: Crane Cove Park
records.summary: Seven-acre Port of San Francisco waterfront park on the former shipyard shoreline between 19th and Mariposa Streets east of Illinois Street, built around historic Slipway 4 and a stabilized historic gantry crane, with a pocket beach and lawn, as a Blue Greenway waterfront park. Planned from 2011, its main park-improvements contract ($17.8 million, one of five contracts that delivered the park) was awarded to Gordon N. Ball in November 2018; it opened September 30, 2020, and the Port's draft FY2024-33 capital plan (May 2023) gives $36.7 million as the total cost of the entire project, including 19th and Georgia Street and Building 49 work finished in July 2021. The playgrounds and dog run followed on December 12, 2025.

notes.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (not a hand trace or estimate), independently confirmed via its own leisure=park/operator/wikidata tags. Its area (~6.26 acres) is somewhat smaller than the ~7 acres given on the Port's project page (the Port's 2018 Item 12B calls it an 'approximately eight acre site') -- likely because this specific traced way covers the core landscaped park and not every associated feature (e.g. the boat launch apron or beach edge); not adjusted to match the citation since the citation isn't itself a boundary.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 853562207, leisure=park, operator=Port of San Francisco, wikidata=Q108550863) -- a real, community-surveyed park boundary, not a diagram trace.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Port-owned public open space (OSM operator tag: Port of San Francisco). DataSF's Assessor parcels show active lots at this location without street addresses (for example lot 3941041, added 2019-02-07), so whether the park has its own Assessor lot was not established from a cited source; this feature uses the OSM boundary instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Delivered under the Port of San Francisco's Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (2010) as the public-open-space component of the Pier 70 area (Port Item 12B, Sept 2018: identified in the 2010 Preferred Master Plan; HPC 2013 packet: a separate project), distinct from and adjacent to Brookfield's 28-acre D4D redevelopment parcel from which Pier & Point's other Pier 70 shapes are drawn. Built around a stabilized historic gantry crane and the historic Slipway 4 (Port Resolution 18-61 lists 'stabilization of historic gantry crane (non-functional)'; the same resolution (memo dated Nov 8, 2018) lists 'Elimination of the crane cabs' among the construction contract's cost reductions and says the cabs 'will be delivered through fundraising' in a partnership with the San Francisco Parks Alliance and community stakeholders, and Port Item 12B, Sept 2018, puts the cabs and the children's play equipment together at an estimated cost of $4 million; no source read says whether the cabs were built); a human-powered boating center was listed only as a future development opportunity, and the Port park page lists the YMCA Dogpatch wellness center and, separately, says 'Dogpatch Paddle offers kayak and paddleboard rentals and classes' without saying where the rentals operate.

facts.value: Port of San Francisco
Approximately 7 as opened; earlier planning documents gave other figures (see open questions)
Between 19th and Mariposa Streets east of Illinois Street (the Port's 2025 release says the park is at 18th and Illinois streets)
AECOM (planning and design consultant: master plan, cost estimate, phasing, design and construction support)
Gordon N. Ball, Inc. (park improvements, Contract 2812)
Pocket beach, restored Slipway 4, historic gantry crane, lawn with picnic and barbecue areas, Crane Plaza, dog run, two play areas, restrooms, shoreline sediment cap
Designed for 50 years of projected sea level rise to at least 2065 (+28 inches)
2008 and 2012 Clean and Safe Neighborhood Parks GO Bonds, Port capital and grants; the 2008 bond allocated $33.5 million to Port waterfront parks
Historic Building 49 retrofitted for park support and restrooms; core-and-shell retrofit and permanent public restrooms completed July 2021
Delivered by the Port under the 2010 Preferred Master Plan, separate from Brookfield's 28-Acre Site

Fourth and final sale of 2008 Clean and Safe Neighborhood Parks GO Bonds for Crane Cove Park

Budget set aside from park funding for the Building 49 scope of work (park support and restrooms; a human-powered boat aquatic center, visitors' center and cafe were listed only as future development opportunities); a separate ~$4 million, for the crane tops and children's play structures, was to be raised with the San Francisco Parks Alliance and the Dogpatch community
Baker Street Foundation donation for the playgrounds and dog run, most of which the San Francisco Parks Alliance mismanaged before closing in 2025 (CBS report; the Port then shifted internal funds)
