open_questions: No image is hosted: the Port's park photographs carry no stated license, and no Wikimedia Commons or public-domain photo had been checked when this was written. The Port's opening-day photos are linked from the sources.

The 2015 approval spoke of a ten-acre park delivered in phases; whether a Phase II (the remaining acreage, to be funded from IFD proceeds per the 2018 report) is still planned is not stated in any later document found.

The exact total spent through 2025, including the playground and dog-run work, is not published; the $36.7 million figure is from the FY2024-33 draft capital plan (May 2023), which predates the playgrounds and dog run, and it equals when rounded the $36,668,550 total funding the Port stated at the November 2018 contract award, so it may restate the budget rather than an audited final cost.

The Port's 'presentations and documents - Crane Cove Park' hearing index could not be checked on 2026-09-29 (an archived copy exists, not checked: web.archive.org/web/20251208070941/https://www.sfport.com/projects-programs/completed-projects/presentations-and-documents-crane-cove-park); the June 14, 2011 award date rests on the Port project page's list entry 'Request to award master planning and preliminary design'.

Area of Crane Cove Park: approximately 7 acres per the Port project page and the FY2024-33 draft capital plan, for the park as opened. Earlier documents give other figures: the 2015 approval says Phase I would deliver 'approximately five acres of an eventual 10 acre park' (and elsewhere calls the park 'approximately 9 acre'), the 2018 report an 'approximately eight acre site', and a 2017 Port presentation 'first 6 acres'.

Building 49 at Crane Cove Park: Res. 18-61 covers its retrofit for park support and restrooms and lists a human-powered boat aquatic center, visitors' center and cafe only as future development opportunities; the July 2021 completion of the core-and-shell retrofit and the permanent public restrooms is from the Capital Plan. The Port's park page lists a YMCA Dogpatch wellness center and Dogpatch Paddle kayak and paddleboard rentals, and the Port's December 2025 release says the YMCA 'opened its newest San Francisco facility in Crane Cove Park, which also houses Dogpatch Paddle & Kayak'; neither Port source links them to Building 49.

records.summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square (flanked by rehabilitated buildings and new construction, with an opening on 21st Street between Building 2 and Parcel D and a passageway through Buildings 2 and 12), the Building 12 entry plaza south of Building 12, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. open_questions: No completion date can be stated for the plaza. The Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) gives the Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) a park outside date of '1 year after Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (“TCO”) for Buildings 2 and 12' and Market Square (OS-2) '1 year after TCO for Building D' (Port Item 9B, Sept 22, 2017, Table A, p.8), and 9B says 'Parks must be completed between 12-18 months after completion of adjacent buildings' (p.7). Building 12's rehabilitation was completed in January 2022 (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026), but none of the sources cited here reports a TCO for Building 2 or Building D, and Item 11A says 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward' and that 'Developer has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels', so no calendar date follows. The DDA's Phase 3 outside date does not apply to this Phase 1 park, and the DDA's outside dates are extended while the down market delay lasts (extended to December 26, 2026); Item 11A also proposes to 'better align open spaces with revised vertical development schedule'.

No Port Commission schematic design approval or construction record for Market Square or the entry plaza was found; the interim events documented by the Port took place inside Building 12 and under Building 15, not on a finished plaza.

Whether the Building 15 structural frame is being retained (the D4D marks it 'pending structural feasibility study'): the Port's June 2025 deck shows Building 15 relocated over 22nd Street but does not say what will remain of it.

No openly licensed or public-record post-rehabilitation photo of Building 12 was found (checked Wikimedia Commons -- geosearch, category and title search all came up empty for anything dated 2022 or later). Perkins&Will's Building 12 wayfinding photography (by Bruce Damonte, via DNCO's case study) and Pier 70's own project photography are copyrighted, but their press/media contacts may grant editorial, non-commercial clearance on request -- worth revisiting if someone follows up with them.

Phase of Building 12 Plaza and Market Square: Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) lists Building 12 Plaza (OS-1) and Market Square (OS-2) among the Phase 1 parks, and Port Item 11A cites three acres of Phase 1 parks overall. Item 11A's 2026 phasing plan (Exhibit A) is an image whose text is not legible, so this record does not state the plaza's place in the proposed 2026 phasing.

records.summary: The roughly two-acre courtyard park beside the Irish Hill remnant, bounded by Parcels C1, C2, PKS, HDY1/2 and HDY3 (D4D Section 3.12), with the smaller Irish Hill Corner Plaza at Illinois and 22nd Streets (Section 3.11) as its gateway. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- traced directly from Figure 6.4.2's own 'Public Open Space' fill color (outlined automatically by color), then trimmed to the mapped shapes of PKS, HDY3, C1, C2 and HDY1/2. Now extends north to touch '21ST ST (NEW)' directly in the gap between PKS and C1, matching the diagram's own drawn fill. The geometry is now a single Polygon: an earlier trace produced a separate small piece near Illinois St (the Irish Hill Corner Plaza zone), but it reconnects to the main body through the corridor between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (see the mapping log), and on the rendered Figure 6.4.2 the green band between HDY3 and HDY1/2 runs continuously to the Illinois/22nd corner. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. Pier & Point reads Assessor lot 4113001 (2,278 m2, active, recorded 2019-02-07) as part of this playground, and 718 m2 of it lies inside this drawing. The playground also lies partly on the Hoedown Yard lots (the D4D and Port Item 9B give the yard as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A, and the Port memo expects it to be subdivided into three parcels): lot 4110008A overlaps this drawing by 1,524 m2 and lot 4120002 by 935 m2. open_questions: No design approval, construction contract or completion for the playground or corner plaza was found. Under the 2017 DDA terms the City may ask the Hoedown Yard developer to build Irish Hill Park (see the delivery fact above); the Port's August 2026 Item 11A (p.2) still describes the Hoedown Yard as 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E', and no source read says whether the City has exercised its option to buy it. Parcel K South, which borders the playground, sits inside the Phase 2B outline of the Port's proposed phasing plan (Exhibit A), and Item 11A (p.3) says the funding sources for the affordable-housing parcels are 'currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'.

How much of Irish Hill was quarried, when, and by whom is not stated in the retrieved primary sources beyond the NRHP nomination's site descriptions; the map notes' 'quarried away in the early 20th century' summary is unsourced here.
This record combines two D4D zones (3.11 and 3.12) into one geometry, per the shape's accuracy caveat.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the 2017 DDA's Schedule of Performance ties Irish Hill Park's outside date to 1-1.5 years after the last temporary certificate of occupancy for HDY1 or HDY2 ('a Port or Hoedown Yard Vertical Developer obligation, at Port's discretion,' Port Commission Item 9B, Sept 22, 2017, Table A, p.8), but the Hoedown Yard itself is outside the 28-Acre Project and has no reported schedule (see the HDY1/2 and HDY3 records), so no window can be dated here.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel K South (PKS)
records.summary: The southern piece of the Port's 20th/Illinois Street parcel, on Illinois Street south of the new 21st Street, reserved under the 2017 approvals as a 100%-affordable housing site (65 ft under the D4D). The Port's 2026 report assigns it to Phase 2 and says its gap funding is not yet available; no developer has been selected.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4110013, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Parcel K South is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 1,709 m2 against the lot's 1,637 m2; 83% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 86% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. None of the sources read reports construction, a developer or a start date for this block. Port Item 11A (Aug 7, 2026) places Parcel K South in Phase 2 of the project and says that funding for the 100% affordable sites is 'currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'; its statement that 'construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward' concerns Phase 1 of the 28-Acre Site, not this parcel. It is Parcel K South, a Port-retained parcel created from the Port's Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Port Item 9B, Res 17-52), outside the 28-Acre Site and the developer's vertical option; Port Item 9B gives that parent parcel as Block 4110 Lot 001, which DataSF lists as retired 2018-10-02.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4110013 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Parcel K South. Lot 4110013 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4110013; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential in every D4D land-use scenario (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, and a 100%-affordable housing site under Port Item 9B. A real parcel distinct from Parcel K North: Port Resolution 17-52 (Item 9B, Sept 2017) has the Port subdivide the 20th/Illinois parcel into four parcels including Parcel K North and Parcel K South, and the Port's Item 12B memo (Feb 2020) names 'the Illinois/20th Street parcels known as Parcel K North and Parcel K South' (its Resolution 20-07 recital says 'the Illinois/20th Street parcel known as Parcel K', singular). No source found gives a specific unit count, architect, or construction-status beyond this.

records.name: Pier 70 Hoedown Yard 3 (HDY3)
records.summary: The northern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard at Illinois and 22nd Streets, zoned residential under the Pier 70 SUD and D4D (65 ft) but not part of Brookfield's 28-Acre Project: the City holds an option to buy the roughly 3-acre yard from PG&E, subdivide it into three parcels and offer them for sale, with an Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District over the yard meant to fund Pier 70's affordable housing. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- 'planned' here reflects only that the adopted D4D designates this block; no source read reports a project, a developer or a start date for it. The land is still owned by PG&E: Port Item 9B (Sept 22, 2017, Table 3) says 'The City has an option to purchase the approximately 3-acre Hoedown Yard from PG&E', and Port Item 11A (Aug 7, 2026) lists 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E known as the Hoedown Yard' in the Pier 70 Special Use District; none of the sources read says that option has been exercised. It is part of the Hoedown Yard, which the D4D (Section 1) describes as owned by Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E), with a City option to acquire it, and which is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Site. The D4D gives the yard's Assessor lots as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A (Port Item 9B gives 4120/002 and 4711/008A); DataSF's Assessor layer lists 4120002 and 4110008A (1021 Illinois St) as active lots, and this hand-traced block overlaps them, but the overlay of approximate geometry is not an identification of this block's own lot. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. SNAPPED 2026-09-17: this block's north edge had drifted 1.26m south of PKS's own south edge (both blocks were independently re-measured at different times and no longer shared an exact boundary, despite the diagram showing them as one continuous fill with only an internal divider line). Snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's south-edge coordinates exactly, closing the gap to 0m. RE-SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): PKS itself was found to be badly mispositioned (60% of its area was being clipped away against the real 21st St -- see the Parcel K South (PKS) record) and was shifted ~25m south to ground-truth against the real street. Re-snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's new south edge to stay attached; area dropped from ~2,699 to ~1,508 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of PKS moving into what was previously this block's own north portion. This block's own south/diagonal portion (touching HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground) is unchanged. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (after this block was noted to look too small relative to its peers in the drawing): checked whether this shrinkage is a real bug (i.e., whether the same northward transform bias found on PKS/C1/PKN/Building 113-116 also affects this block's own south/diagonal portion, which would justify shifting HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground south too, restoring this block's diagram-implied size while keeping everything attached). Tested this directly: interpolated the real, official 22nd St centerline's latitude at HDY1/2's own south-edge longitudes (the nearest independently-checkable real street to this cluster) and compared to HDY1/2's current south edge -- found a clean ~14m gap with NO overlap, unlike PKS's 60% real-street overlap that justified its own correction. This is the opposite signature from a 'drawn too far north' bug: if the same bias reached this far south, HDY1/2 would itself be overlapping 22nd St, not comfortably clear of it. Conclusion: the 21st-St-row bias is local to that row and does not extend to this block's own south portion or to HDY1/2/Irish Hill Playground -- there is no evidence basis to shift them south to recover this block's pre-fix size. This block's current, smaller size is treated as the accurate, forced consequence of ground-truthing PKS (which shares this block's own north edge), not an unresolved bug. This conclusion is stated explicitly because Pier & Point does not fabricate geometry: if a future source shows this block's own south/diagonal corners were independently misread (a diagram-reading error, not a bias-correction consequence), that would still warrant revisiting this specific block on its own. DataSF's active lots 4110008A (6,101 m2) and 4120002 (5,997 m2) are the Hoedown Yard lots (the D4D and Port Item 9B give the yard as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A, and the Port memo expects it to be subdivided into three parcels). Lot 4110008A overlaps this drawing by 2,344 m2 and lot 4120002 by 0 m2; each also lies under other drawn blocks and the Irish Hill Playground, so neither is this block's own lot, and the drawing is kept until the yard is subdivided.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The Hoedown Yard is PG&E's own Assessor land, not part of Brookfield's 28-acre site: the D4D (Section 1) gives it as Assessor's Block 4120/Lot 002 and Block 4110/Lot 008A (Port Item 9B: 4120/002 and 4711/008A), owned by PG&E with a City option to acquire it, and the Port memo says it will be subdivided into three separate parcels. The earlier statement that it is part of Brookfield's site and not subdivided is withdrawn; this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry because the yard has not been subdivided into the D4D's HDY parcels.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential in all three D4D land-use scenarios (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7; not 'parking support' as sometimes described secondhand), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (a uniform height, not a 40-65 ft range). Part of the approximately 3.6-acre 'Hoedown Yard' (HDY) at Illinois and 22nd streets, which the D4D describes as currently owned by PG&E; the parcel takes its name from the yard. Shown as a separate parcel from HDY1/2 in the D4D's own figure. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: Whether the City has exercised its option to buy the Hoedown Yard from PG&E: no source read says. The Port's August 2026 Item 11A (p.2) still describes the yard as 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E'. The financing district itself was formed in 2018 (see the milestones).

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the Port's Aug 3, 2017 staff report (Item 11A, p.21, DDA major terms) says 'Parcel K North and the Hoedown Yard, while in the SUD, are not part of the Project', so the Hoedown Yard is a separate transaction from the 28-Acre Project; the Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan shows it outside every phase outline; no source read gives a schedule for the City's PG&E purchase option, so this record stays undated rather than borrow the 28-Acre Project's buildout target.

Ownership and area of the Hoedown Yard: the D4D gives an approximately 3.6-acre parcel and the DDA terms 'approximately 3-acre', including a 0.2-acre unbuilt Michigan Street right-of-way easement. The D4D describes the yard as currently owned by PG&E, with a City option to acquire it if PG&E can find a new location for its heavy industrial use.

Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see the mapping log) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. CORRECTED 2026-09-17: fixed an error caused by mismatched image resolutions during tracing, which had gone unnoticed since 2026-09-16. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. DataSF's active lots 4110008A (6,101 m2) and 4120002 (5,997 m2) are the Hoedown Yard lots (the D4D and Port Item 9B give the yard as Block 4120 Lot 002 and Block 4110 Lot 008A, and the Port memo expects it to be subdivided into three parcels). Lot 4110008A overlaps this drawing by 1,651 m2 and lot 4120002 by 3,017 m2; each also lies under other drawn blocks and the Irish Hill Playground, so neither is this block's own lot, and the drawing is kept until the yard is subdivided.

open_questions: Whether the City has exercised its option to buy the Hoedown Yard from PG&E: no source read says. The Port's August 2026 Item 11A (p.2) still describes the yard as 'approximately 3 acres owned by PG&E'. The financing district itself was formed in 2018 (see the milestones).

The Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan (Item 11A, Exhibit A, p.8) shows the Hoedown Yard parcels (HDY1/2 and HDY3) outside every phase outline, since they are not part of the 28-Acre Project, so no phase is recorded here. Parcel K South, by contrast, sits inside the Phase 2B outline.
Assessor block/lot for the yard is given as 4120/002 and 4711/008A in the 2017 memo but 4120/002 and 4110/008A in the D4D; one is a typo, unresolved.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the Port's Aug 3, 2017 staff report (Item 11A, p.21, DDA major terms) says 'Parcel K North and the Hoedown Yard, while in the SUD, are not part of the Project', so the Hoedown Yard is a separate transaction from the 28-Acre Project; the Port's 2026 proposed phasing plan shows it outside every phase outline; no source read gives a schedule for the City's PG&E purchase option, so this record stays undated rather than borrow the 28-Acre Project's buildout target.
Size of the Hoedown Yard: the D4D gives approximately 3.6 acres and the DDA terms 'approximately 3-acre', in both cases including a 0.2-acre unbuilt Michigan Street right-of-way easement.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

No developer, unit count or funding plan for the C1B affordable site was found; the August 2026 Port report says the affordable gap-funding sources (condo in-lieu fee, commercial impact fee, Hoedown Yard IRFD increment) 'are currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'.
The boundaries of C1A/C1B/C1C within this block are only shown diagrammatically on the SUD land-use plan; this record's geometry covers the whole C1 block.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel C2
records.summary: Residential block on Louisiana Street between the Irish Hill playground and 22nd Street, 90 ft under the D4D. Its C2A half is the Phase 1 100%-affordable housing site, for which MOHCD selected Young Community Developers, Chinatown CDC and Catholic Charities in May 2021; the project has not advanced because its gap funding depends on market-rate development that has not started (Port staff report dated August 7, 2026). The Port Commission heard that report as an informational item on August 11, 2026 and took no action; staff expect to return with proposed amendments in late 2026 or early 2027.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4113002 and 4113003, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery: lots 4113002 and 4113003 are the two stacked cells the D4D draws for C2 (together 2,610 m2; measured against the D4D's own scale bar the block is about 126 by 229 ft, roughly 2,700 m2). Lot 4113001 (2,278 m2), just west of them, is read as part of the Irish Hill Playground, and lot 4120002 (5,997 m2) is one of the Hoedown Yard lots, so neither is used here. No document read names these lots. A building may sit back from the lot lines. No vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4113002 and 4113003 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lot of Parcel C2. Lots 4113002 and 4113003 (active) were assigned to it from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram, so its outline is their union.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential per D4D Figure 2.1.1 (which stripes C2 as Residential and Parking Garage options), 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2. C2A, a sub-portion of this parcel, is one of two 100%-affordable parcels in this cluster per Port Resolution 20-07 (Item 12B, Feb 2020: 'the 100% affordable housing parcels (Parcels C1B and C2A)'; the other is C1B, part of Parcel C1). No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.
The C2A affordable project's unit count beyond 'at least 100', its cost and its financing are all listed as TBD by the developer; no MOHCD loan approval or Port ground lease for C2A was found.

The 2017 approvals counted 320+ stand-alone affordable units across three sites (C1B, C2A, Parcel K South); the 2026 report holds the minimum at 327 and says the parties are evaluating higher unit yields, but no per-site split was published.

The developer page cited for C2A (Chinatown CDC's 'In Development' list) does not name Parcel C2A; that the 'Pier 70' entry is the C2A project is inferred from the Port's Aug 2026 report naming the same developers for Parcel C2A. A Port or MOHCD document naming C2A and the unit count would settle it.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the 2042 'completion expected' milestone was removed. 2042 is the original 2017 outside date for the whole project's Phase 3, which its own basis note said is not a completion forecast for this Phase 1 parcel, and the Port's August 2026 Item 11A says the developer's deadlines were tolled and proposes new phase timelines; no source gives C2 a completion year.

Affordable units on Parcel C2: the developer's page calls it an 'inclusionary housing project' and lists funding sources, development cost and construction type as TBD, and square footage as 'TBD- estimated 98,400'.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4114007, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lot is Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery (the lot lies west of Maryland St beside Building 2, where the D4D draws D); no document read names it. The D4D draws D as an L-shaped block; the lot is a plain rectangle, so the outline is not that L. A building may sit back from the lot lines. notes.regulatory_context: Residential (studio-3BR over 7 levels) + ground-floor retail + townhouses along 21st St, designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects, per the architect's own project page (saitowitz.com/pier-70-parcel-d): 'loft town houses along 21st street. Above are studio, one, two and three bedroom units stacked on seven levels', with a retail space along the grove, Market Square and Maryland Street. A weak secondary source implied a ~2020 completion, which no primary source supports: Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward and that no Phase 1 option parcel has been exercised. The Real Deal (Jul 16, 2026) reports Brookfield's development VP saying additional density would let the company 'break ground in 2027 on its first market-rate apartment building' (350 units, parcel not named), a conditional plan not specific to Parcel D. Treat as NOT yet built.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Unit count, square footage and the date of the Saitowitz design are not stated on the architect's page and no Planning vertical design approval for Parcel D is listed on the Planning Department's Pier 70 page.
A secondary source implying a ~2020 completion is noted on this parcel's map shape; no primary source supports it, and Port Item 11A says Phase 1 vertical construction has not moved forward.

records.summary: Residential parcel on Maryland Street north of Building 21, mostly 90 ft with a 65 ft north leg under the D4D, assigned to Phase 2C in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Under the 2017 DDA the lease of historic Building 21 is triggered within a year after completion of the building on E1.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4052009, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lot is Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery (the lot lies just east of Maryland St, west of the lot the D4D's Building 21 box falls on, where the D4D draws E1); no document read names it. The existing Building 21 stands on this lot today (its surveyed footprint lies 587 m2 inside it) and is planned to be relocated, so this block overlaps that existing building. The D4D draws E1 with a 65-ft cell next to the 90-ft strip; the lot does not show that split. A building may sit back from the lot lines. open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved. The only per-parcel figure found is a 2017 estimate in Port Item 9B, Attachment D, Table D2 (p.182), which lists 'E1 Condominiums 142,934' estimated gross square feet as an input to proposed special-tax rates; it is a tax estimate subject to approval, not a design program, and gives no unit count.

The Planning Department's project description quoted by SF YIMBY, which gives about 120,000 gsf of retail and arts space for 'Buildings E-1A and E-1B', does not say whether those buildings are on parcel E1 and conflicts with the D4D's residential designation for E1; the underlying filing was not retrieved, so this is left as reported.

The notes on this record's mapped shape say E1's real footprint is irregular around Building 21; the D4D figure shows E1 as two pieces (a 90-ft block and a 65-ft north leg) either side of Building 21's setback.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E2 (block)
records.summary: Phase 1 rental-apartment parcel at 185 Maryland Street (Block 4116 Lot 008), 50,875 sq ft, entitled for about 280 units with 20% below-market-rate, with a 2021 SF YIMBY post crediting its design to Kennerly Architecture and Planning. Its 2020 appraisal ($5 million against an $11.3 million DDA threshold) and a second below-threshold appraisal in 2021 triggered the down-market delay that has stalled Phase 1; the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would have the developer elect whether to exercise its E2 option immediately after the amendments are approved, the first of the Phase 1 deadlines the Port's report lists.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4116008, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Assessor's Block 4116, Lot 008 (185 Maryland Street), and DataSF's Assessor layer lists 4116008 as an active P70-MU lot added 2019-02-07 with no street address, so for E2 the identification rests on a Port document. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Parcel E2 is not yet built (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward, and no Phase 1 option parcel has been exercised).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4116008 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Parcel E2 has its own Assessor lot: Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Block 4116, Lot 008 (185 Maryland Street) and DataSF lists 4116008 as an active P70-MU lot; the outline is that lot.
notes.regulatory_context: Shown at 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, the same height tier as Parcel E3. The Port's sources treat this as the one Parcel E2: Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) describes E2 (185 Maryland Street) as a residential parcel entitled for approximately 280 rental dwelling units, and Port Item 9B (2017, Table A) ties Slipways Commons (SC-1) to one year after the TCO for Parcel E2; no source found describes a second 'E2', so the earlier 'possible labeling inconsistency' flag is withdrawn. No construction-start source found for this block.

open_questions: On what date the Port Commission adopted Resolution 20-07 (the E2 lease option at $5,000,000) is given two ways by Port documents: the certificate printed at the end of the resolution in the Item 12B packet says 'adopted by the Port Commission at its meeting of February 11, 2020', while the minutes of the February 25, 2020 meeting (item 13A) say 'Four of the Commissioners were in favor. Commissioner Makras cast the dissenting vote. Resolution No. 20-07 was adopted.' and describe that item as the follow-up to 'the February 11th presentation we had two weeks ago'. Neither date is shown as settled; the timeline gives February 2020.

Whether the '350-unit' first market-rate apartment building Brookfield described in July 2026 is E2: SF Planning's Pier 70 page lists a Vertical Design Approval for Parcel E2 (with Parcel K North and Parcel A), and Port documents report appraisals of E2, but no report names E2 as that building, and Port Item 11A also lists historic Building 2 as a Phase 1 option parcel.

Kennerly's own project page (kennerlyarchitecture.com/portfolio/pier-70-e2/) could not be checked; search-engine excerpts of it cite 282 homes and 10,000 sq ft of retail, not restated here until read directly.
The date of the Planning Department's vertical design approval for E2 and the June 2021 appraised value are not published in the retrieved documents.

The 'E2' label: Port documents give the address 185 Maryland Street and Block 4116 Lot 008; the D4D height figure (Figure 6.4.2, p.155) shows E2 on the east side of Maryland Street, north of 22nd Street, across Maryland Street from Building 12 and south of the open space beside Building 21 and E1. An earlier note on this record's map shape about a possible labeling inconsistency has been withdrawn (no source describes a second E2).
Height of Parcel E2: Port Item 11A proposes raising 'certain residential parcels from 65 to 90 feet' but does not say which parcels, so it states no change for E2.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E3
search_aliases: Elevation Sky Park San Francisco (interim use)
records.summary: Waterfront residential parcel at 22nd Street and the Bay, 70 ft under the D4D and assigned to Phase 3A in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Its D4D building has no construction record; instead Elevation XR, with Brookfield, is developing the interim Elevation Sky Park entertainment venue, announced in 2025 as three projection domes and a pyramid on about 165,000 sq ft for up to five years (2026 coverage mentions three domes and no pyramid). The Port places it where 22nd Street meets the Bay; Pier & Point reads that as including this parcel, but no source names the parcel. A one-day festival, Pier Play San Francisco, was held on the site on September 19, 2026, and the venue's own page calls it 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park', with no opening date yet.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4116009, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Parcel E3 is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 6,413 m2 against the lot's 5,158 m2; 61% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 76% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines.  CURRENT USE, POST-LEASE FUTURE UNCLEAR (added 2026-09-17): this parcel is being treated as the site of Elevation Sky Park, an interim entertainment venue that the SF Chronicle (June 10, 2025) reports has 'signed a five-year lease' and that the operator's Port-hosted community engagement deck (June 25, 2025) proposes for a 'Period of 5 years' (see the regulatory context). Both are a press report and a proposal; no lease or Port approval document was read, and the deck's target opening of Q1 2026 has passed without an opening. What is NOT known, and should not be assumed, is what happens here after that lease ends: the D4D's original masterplan designates this parcel 70ft-max residential, but that plan was adopted years before ESP's interim lease existed, and no source found ties ESP's lease expiration to an actual scheduled residential construction start, or confirms the D4D's original boundary/use for this specific parcel will still be pursued unchanged by then. Do not read the 'entertainment' use here as a permanent reclassification, or assume 'residential' will automatically resume -- both are open questions. The parcel-level match to ESP itself is also still an approximation: no scaled site plan for the venue was found (an earlier note cited a rendering in an SFGATE article, but no article link was recorded, so that corroboration is not relied on), and ESP's real footprint may still extend slightly into neighboring E2/E4, as the pre-merge overlap analysis found.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4116009 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Parcel E3. Lot 4116009 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4116009; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: D4D-designated use: residential, 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (no construction-start source ever found for that plan). CURRENT REAL USE: Elevation Sky Park (Elevation XR, in partnership with Brookfield Properties), a 165,000 sq ft interim entertainment venue (3 geodesic domes + a pyramid) proposed for a 'Period of 5 years' and 'fully permitted through the Port of San Francisco' (community engagement deck, June 25, 2025, future tense; the SF Chronicle, June 10, 2025, reports that Elevation XR 'has signed a five-year lease', and no lease document was read). A one-day festival, RASA World's 'Pier Play San Francisco', was held on the site on September 19, 2026; the venue's own page (Sept 2026) calls the site 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park' and invites sign-ups for opening announcements, and the July 2026 release had said the campus would open in phases beginning September 2026. No source shows the venue open. Port materials describe it as an 'interim activation on Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone' -- confirming it is temporary by design, though not tied to a specific successor project or date.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Placement of Elevation Sky Park on Parcel E3 is Pier & Point's own reading (Pier & Point merged it into E3): the primary sources say only 'Phase 2/3 sites' and 'where 22nd Street meets the Bay', which is consistent with E3/H2 but not parcel-specific. A Port license or permit for the venue, which would settle it, was not found on any 2025-2026 Port Commission agenda.

Pier Play San Francisco, the venue's first public event, was held on Sept 19, 2026 per the venue's own page (published Sept 25, 2026), which calls the site 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park'; whether the venue is open on a continuing basis is not stated by any source read. The Business Wire release itself could not be checked; a syndicated copy on Yahoo Finance was read.
Lease or license terms (rent to Brookfield or the Port) for the interim venue: not found.

Elevation Sky Park's dome capacities differ between two sources: the Port-hosted community engagement deck of June 25, 2025 lists 200-350 (small dome and pyramid), 300-500 (medium dome) and 600-800 (large dome), while Beatportal (July 24, 2026) says 'the domes ranging in capacity from 150 to 750 guests'. Neither is shown as settled; both are planning-stage figures, not measured capacities.

When Elevation Sky Park itself opens (as a venue, not the Sept 19, 2026 one-day festival): its own page (checked 2026-09-29) still calls the site its future home and offers opening-announcement sign-ups.

The number of domes at Elevation Sky Park differs between sources: the June 25, 2025 deck and SFist's June 10, 2025 report describe three domes and a pyramid, Beatportal (July 24, 2026) describes 'three geodesic projection domes' and does not mention a pyramid, and the venue's own page headlines 'One Dome Park. Many worlds.' Neither count is shown as settled.

Term of Elevation Sky Park's interim use: this is a plan, not a lease term: the June 25, 2025 deck says 'Period of 5 years' and SFist quotes the press release, 'planned as an interim use for up to five years'; no lease or license term was found.

records.summary: The waterfront arts-building parcel east of Building 21: excluded from the developer's purchase option, capped at 50 ft and five stories, and reserved under the 2017 DDA for an arts facility of up to 90,000 sq ft (with replacement studios for the Noonan Building artists) on a 50-year, $1-a-year lease once $17.5 million in private contributions is raised. The Port's proposed 2026 amendments would rezone it to allow housing if the arts facility proves infeasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4052011, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lot is Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery (the lot lies just east of Building 21, where the D4D draws E4); no document read names it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. No vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). Port Items 9B (Sept 22, 2017) and 12B (Feb 7, 2020) list Parcel E4 (the arts building parcel) among the parcels excluded from the developer's option under the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA); Port Item 11A describes the option more generally, as covering 'all development parcels within the 28-Acre Site'.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4052011 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lot of Parcel E4. Lot 4052011 (active) was assigned to it from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram, so its outline is that lot.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's land-use designation for E4 is Retail, Arts and Light Industrial (Figure 2.1.1), with office uses permitted in Building 12 and E4 except on the ground floor, and residential not permitted on E4 (Table 2.1.1) -- not residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) calls it 'the arts building parcel (Parcel E4)' and lists it among the parcels excluded from the developer's standard option under the DDA. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. Port Item 11A (2026) proposes to allow residential use on E4 if an arts facility proves infeasible. No construction-start source found.

SF YIMBY (Oct 27, 2021), quoting the Planning Department's project description for the 2021 development agreement filing, says about 120,000 gsf of the retail and arts space would come from 'Buildings E-1A and E-1B' and about 115,000 gsf from the rehabilitation of 'Buildings 12 and 21'; it names no separate arts building and does not say which parcel 'E-1A and E-1B' are on. The underlying filing was not retrieved.

Whether the Noonan Building has been demolished or its tenants relocated to temporary space: the Port's June 2025 deck lists events with the Noonan Artists in November 2021 ('Roll with Us'), May 2024 ('Hosted and supported Noonan Open Studios') and August 2024 ('art by the Noonan Artists'), but does not say whether they are still on site or what has happened to the building.

records.summary: Flexibly zoned block (Commercial-Office or Residential in the D4D) on the south side of 22nd Street west of Maryland Street, drawn as one parcel 'F/G' in the D4D's height figure (90 ft, six stories) and split into F and G only in the D4D's Maximum Residential land-use scenario; a flexibly zoned parcel shown as commercial in the Mid-Point scenario. notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of three real Assessor lots (4115001, 4115003 and 4115004), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That these three lots are Parcels F/G is Pier & Point's own inference from their location, shape and size (7,674 m2, against about 7,260 m2 measured on D4D Figure 6.4.2; both show the same pointed west tip and slanted south-west edge along the curving road). No Port document read ties these lot numbers to F/G. A building may sit back from the lot lines. No vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). Along the curving south road, the map clips about 24% of the lot union as street: about 21% (roughly 1,650 m2 of 7,690 m2) falls inside the street corridor drawn from DataSF's official centerlines (6.8 m each side), and about 2% more is cut off from the rest by that corridor and dropped. open_questions: No outside date can be stated for Parcels F/G. The Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) measures its outside dates in years after Project approval ('Phase 1 within 7.5 years ... Phase 2 within 16 years, and Phase 3 within approximately 25 years', Port Item 9B, Sept 22, 2017, p.7), but no source read says which phase F/G belongs to under the 2017 DDA; Item 9B does not list parcels by phase. The Port's August 2026 Item 11A says Port staff and the developer propose 'reallocating parcels between Phases 2 and 3 and dividing each phase into subphases' and to 'Shorten the timeline for completion of each phase', and its Exhibit A (a proposal, not an adopted plan) shows F/G alone in a proposed subphase 2A.

No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved. The only per-parcel figure found is a 2017 estimate in Port Item 9B, Attachment D, Table D1 (p.181), which lists 'F-G (could flex to Condo) Office 426,180' estimated gross square feet as an input to proposed special-tax rates; it is a tax estimate subject to approval, not a design program.
A Brookfield leasing brochure for F-G is reported to give a rentable-area figure, but no copy could be retrieved, so no figure from it is used here or kept in About this shape.

The parcel's south edge abuts the former Potrero Power Station site; no Port document retrieved describes coordination of F/G with that project beyond the shared pump-station framework mentioned in the June 2025 deck.

The lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: the parcel number is placed at the upper left of its parcel, and the H1 and H2 labels sit on either side of the dashed mid-block passage, so lots 4117002 and 4117001 are H1 and lot 4117003 is H2. open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Brookfield's leasing brochure reportedly gives a combined '+/- 430,000 RSF' for H1-H2 and calls H1 pure office; the brochure was not retrieved, so those statements were removed from About this shape on 2026-09-29.

Whether the Elevation Sky Park interim venue extends onto H2 is unresolved. The venue's community engagement deck (Elevation XR, hosted by the Port, June 25, 2025) places it on 'Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone', and the Port's Executive Director described the location at the July 8, 2025 Port Commission meeting as '22nd Street where that street meets the Bay'; neither names a parcel. See the Parcel E3 record.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel H2
records.summary: Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel (baseline scenario residential) on the south side of 22nd Street east of Maryland Street (east half of the H1/H2 pair), 90 ft under the D4D (six stories for commercial buildings, nine for residential), assigned to Phase 3A with Parcel E3 in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. No design, appraisal or construction record exists for it. The Port Commission heard the proposed plan as an informational item on August 11, 2026 and took no action; staff expect to return with proposed amendments in late 2026 or early 2027.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4117003, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: the parcel number is placed at the upper left of its parcel, and the H1 and H2 labels sit on either side of the dashed mid-block passage, so lots 4117002 and 4117001 are H1 and lot 4117003 is H2. No document read names these lots. The lots extend south of the block edge the D4D draws, into the former power-plant ground, so the outline is larger than the diagram's block. A building may sit back from the lot lines. No vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel).

notes.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lot of Parcel H2. Lot 4117003 (active) was assigned to it from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams, so its outline is that lot.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Brookfield's leasing brochure reportedly gives a combined '+/- 430,000 RSF' for H1-H2 and calls H1 pure office; the brochure was not retrieved, so those statements were removed from this record's map notes on 2026-09-29.

Whether the Elevation Sky Park interim venue extends onto H2 is unresolved. The venue's community engagement deck (Elevation XR, hosted by the Port, June 25, 2025) places it on 'Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone', and the Port's Executive Director described the location at the July 8, 2025 Port Commission meeting as '22nd Street where that street meets the Bay'; neither names a parcel. See the Parcel E3 record.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)
records.summary: A six-story board-formed concrete warehouse of 1941-44 (256 ft by 77 ft, 98,804 sq ft) north of Building 12, one of the historic buildings addressed in the Pier 70 DDA; unlike Buildings 12 and 21, it is an option parcel that must be developed under a 99-year lease consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards if the developer exercises its option. It is a Phase 1 option parcel to be held on a 99-year lease at an appraised rent; SF YIMBY's 2021 summary of the development-agreement filing described about 120 dwelling units in its shell (the Port's 2017 staff report assumed about 100 rental dwelling units), Brookfield's leasing page shows a Building 2 image captioned 'Creative office interior', and the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would have the developer assign its option and close escrow within six months of Board approval, with certain impact fees and special taxes waived. The Port's August 2026 report says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects 'has not moved forward'; no rehabilitation of Building 2 was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4114009, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lot is Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram and the satellite imagery (the lot lies beside Parcel D and Building 12, where the D4D's Historic Building box labelled 2 is drawn); no document read names it. The lot is the legal boundary, not the building's footprint. Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2) is an existing building (the D4D draws it as a Historic Building).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4114009 (recorded 2020-10-23; mapped 2021-07-07; active); cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lot of Building 2. Lot 4114009 (active) was assigned to it from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagram, so its outline is that lot.
notes.regulatory_context: Officially 'Warehouse No. 2' per the D4D (Section 6.6.1), a historic industrial shop structure labelled 236 ft x 76 ft in the D4D's Figure 6.5.4 (the National Register registration form gives it as 256 ft long and 76 ft 9 in wide). Its use is not settled: the D4D treats it as a flexible parcel (Figure 2.1.1 stripes it Commercial-Office/Residential; the land-use scenarios in Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7 show it Residential in the Mid-Point baseline and Maximum Residential and Commercial-Office in Maximum Office), a 2021 development-agreement filing summarised about 120 dwelling units (SF YIMBY), and Brookfield's leasing page (pier70sf.com/leasing) shows 'creative office'. The NRHP gross area is 98,804 sq ft; a ~100,000 RSF brochure figure and a '~50,000 GSF, Arts/Maker' description formerly recorded here are uncited and have been dropped. No source read says whether rehabilitation has started. Port Item 11A (Aug 7, 2026, p.5) proposes that the developer assign its option on Building 2 and close escrow within 6 months of Board approval of the DDA amendments, and waive certain impact fees and special taxes for Building 2 'given the high costs of historic rehabilitation'; the text of the Port's June 2025 project update deck does not mention Building 2.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 101 (Bethlehem Steel HQ)
names: RH San Francisco, The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building
records.summary: The 1917 Classical Revival main office of the Union Iron Works at the corner of 20th and Illinois Streets, designed by Frederick H. Meyer, rehabilitated by Orton Development under the Port's 66-year Historic Core master lease and subleased whole to RH (Restoration Hardware) on a 41-year sublease from February 2017; RH announced the opening of RH San Francisco, with the Palm Court restaurant and a rooftop park, on May 13, 2022. The California Office of Historic Preservation's 2023 Governor's Historic Preservation Awards include the Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation, which covers 'a half dozen historic buildings known as "20th Street Historic Buildings at Pier 70"'; the award text does not name individual buildings, so it does not say whether Building 101 is one of them.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself. The match to 'Building 101' specifically (as opposed to a neighboring structure) rests on position (33.9m from the diagram's own label, closest of any candidate) and shape correspondence, not an address or explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself, since no such attribute exists there.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The HPC packet of Nov 2013 lists Assessor's Block 4046, Lot 001 (blklot 4046001) among the lots holding its ten 20th Street Historic Buildings, without saying which building is on which lot; DataSF's footprint for this building carries that lot as its legacy id (mblr SF4046001). DataSF shows that lot retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn); the building's footprint now lies within active lot 3941027, which has no street address in DataSF's Assessor parcels. This feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Bethlehem Steel HQ, a 1917 neoclassical office building designed by Frederick H. Meyer. Its size is reported differently: RH's May 13, 2022 release calls it an '80,000-Square-Foot Landmark Building', the National Register nomination says it 'contains 56,268 square feet', and the Port gives 61,311 sq ft before and 60,525 sq ft after rehabilitation (HPC packet, Nov 2013; Port Item 12A, Jan 2019); no source settles the difference. Its floors are described differently too: the HPC packet says 'a five-story above street level office building' with 'two lower levels and a penthouse level', the nomination describes three full stories over a basement and sub-basement with a partial fourth floor and penthouse, and RH says 'five floors'. Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) starting after a Nov 26 2013 Historic Preservation Commission review (sfplanning.org HPC packet 2013.1168E); per that packet, the seismic upgrade uses shear walls, and the rehab preserves the historic exterior elevations while adapting the interior. The Port's Jan 2019 update reported Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, with completion and occupancy of Building 101 anticipated in 2020. RH announced the opening of RH San Francisco -- 'The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building' (showroom, Palm Court restaurant and two wine bars, rooftop park) in a press release dated May 13, 2022; the release gives no separate opening day, and no independent dated report was read.

open_questions: Sources disagree on the year Building 101 was built. The Port's 2019 memo gives 1917 in its Table 1 (Year Built) and the 2013 Historic Preservation Commission packet says the building "was built in 1917", as does the National Register nomination this record cites; the same Port memo's narrative says the building "was built in 1915". Pier & Point shows 1917, the figure in the other sources and in the memo's own table; the 1915 figure is unexplained.
The exact completion / certificate of occupancy date for Building 101 (the Port's 2019 memo anticipated 2020; RH opened May 2022) was not found.

Whether Buildings 122 and 123, the two outbuildings behind Building 104 that share the master lease, are on this parcel or the Building 104 parcel is not settled by any source; Pier & Point's records group them with the north-side lot.
No 'now' photograph with a stated license was found; RH's press images are the tenant's copyright and are linked, not hosted.
The Historic American Engineering Record (HAER) survey of the Union Iron Works was not located in the Library of Congress catalog; the NRHP nomination is used as the historic primary source.

RH San Francisco and its Palm Court restaurant have not been re-confirmed as operating since RH's May 13, 2022 opening release: RH's own pages and OpenTable could not be checked on 2026-09-29, and no other dated source that could be checked was found.

Architects of Building 101: STRUCTURE magazine names Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects and Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture among a Design Team that 'collaborated to seismically retrofit Buildings 14, 101, 102, 104, 115 and 116'; it does not assign each firm a role on Building 101. RH's own design architect is listed separately as the tenant's design architect.

Floor area of Building 101, by source: 56,268 sq ft (NRHP); 61,311 before and 60,525 after rehabilitation, plus a 9,000 sq ft new restaurant building behind it (Port 2019 Table 1); RH describes ~80,000 sq ft over five floors.

Seismic scheme of Building 101: as proposed in the 2013 Historic Preservation Commission packet, interior partitions 'would be removed' for an open floor plan and 'reinforced concrete shear walls will improve seismic safety'; no source read confirms this as built.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 102 (former Power House)
records.summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and, per the 2013-2014 National Register nomination and Historic Preservation Commission plan, still housed BAE Systems' electrical service shortly before rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown. The state's Office of Historic Preservation lists the 'Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation' of the '20th Street Historic Buildings at Pier 70' among its 2023 Governor's Historic Preservation Awards; its statement does not name individual buildings, but the Historic Preservation Commission's 2013 packet includes this building in that group.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself. CORRECTED 2026-09-29: this footprint's area (~1955 m2 / ~21,043 sqft) does not match the building. The National Register nomination gives Building 102's dimensions as 128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in (a rectangle of those dimensions is about 5,440 sqft, ~505 m2) and its floor area as 8,428 sq ft over the first floor and basement. No source read gives the building's ground area directly, and sources use 'footprint' for different things: Retrofit magazine (Nov 9, 2020) says a 2,600-square-foot addition brought 'the powerhouse's footprint to just more than 18,000 square feet', which reads as floor area, and the Port gives 11,266 sq ft before and 15,331 sq ft after rehabilitation (Item 12A, Jan 2019). Measured against the nomination's dimensions this outline is roughly four times that rectangle and probably includes neighboring structures or other area (against Retrofit's 18,000 sq ft it would be about 17% larger); the '11,266 sf' Port figure is not the likely source of the discrepancy. The geometry has been accepted as is and was not changed; the outline should not be read as the building's own footprint.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The former Assessor lot blklot 4046001 (listed in the 2013 HPC packet among the lots holding its ten 20th Street Historic Buildings, without saying which building is on which lot; DataSF's footprints carrying that lot's legacy id were matched to Buildings 101, 102, 104, 122 and 123) was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, active=false); in DataSF's current layer this footprint falls within active lot 3941041, which has no street address. No cited source ties the building to a current lot, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: The former Power House, built 1912, part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as Building 101 (HPC packet 2013.1168E, Nov 26 2013 review). Per that packet, Building 102 was 'in fairly good condition' at the time and in use as the powerhouse facility. Port Item 12A (memo dated Jan 4, 2019) names JUUL Labs as the ten-year sublessee of the entire building less the Port's basement electrical equipment room, and Potrero View (Mar 2019) says JUUL 'sublets offices in Building 102'; no source after 2020 confirms a current occupant.

open_questions: Current tenant: the Port's January 2019 memo gives the start of JUUL's ten-year sublease as 'TBD (upon completion of rehabilitation work)'; none of the sources listed here, the latest dated November 2020, confirms JUUL is still in Building 102 or names a successor.
Completion / certificate of occupancy date: the Port anticipated 2019; the November 2020 profile describes the finished building without a date.

The square-footage figures differ by source (8,428 NRHP vs 11,266 Port pre-rehab vs 15,500 magazine). The NRHP says its figure covers 'the first floor and basement', so the basement does not explain the gap, and the sources read do not say what each figure measures.

Construction start: the Port's January 2019 memo says construction followed the July 2015 execution of the master lease, the National Trust (Winter 2016 issue) says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' (the year is not printed), and Bisnow (April 2017) says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'. No source read settles the start year.
Size of Building 102 after rehabilitation: the Port's 2019 Table 1 gives 11,266 sq ft before and 15,331 after rehabilitation; Retrofit magazine gives 15,500 original and just over 18,000 after.

Public access to Building 102: the Port's January 2019 memo lists 'Building 102 key historic features' among 'spaces now open to the public (and to be open when construction is complete)'; the building was still under construction then, the memo does not say which listed spaces were already open, and no later source confirms public access.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters)
records.summary: The 1896 red-brick Renaissance Revival office of the Union Iron Works on 20th Street, by Percy & Hamilton, the earliest of the architect-designed buildings along that street (NRHP); red-tagged when Orton took it on, with new steel columns proposed for seismic bracing in the 2013 plan, and back in occupancy with a certificate of occupancy in June 2017. Tea Living (Tea Collection) held a sublease; the Port's January 2019 sublease list shows JUUL Labs, 'currently under sublease from Tea Living', for the entire building with a June 2017 commencement date and a ten-year term (the list does not say whose start date that is). The California Office of Historic Preservation's 2023 Governor's Historic Preservation Awards include the Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation, which covers 'a half dozen historic buildings known as "20th Street Historic Buildings at Pier 70"'; the award text does not name individual buildings, so it does not say whether Building 104 is one of them.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 104. Buildings 122 and 123 (two small one-story 'check house' buildings flanking Building 104, per the 2013 HPC packet -- 774 GSF and 400 GSF respectively) are NOT separately represented here or anywhere else in this dataset: no footprint of a matching small size was found immediately adjacent to this one, most likely because DataSF's building-footprint extraction merged them into this building's outline (or Building 102's) given how small and closely attached they are. Their combined ~1,174 GSF (~109 m2) is a small fraction of this footprint's ~1,080 m2 total, so if merged in, they would not meaningfully distort this shape -- but their own individual positions are not confirmed and are not claimed here.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The HPC packet of Nov 2013 lists Assessor's Block 4046, Lot 001 (blklot 4046001) among the lots holding its ten 20th Street Historic Buildings, without saying which building is on which lot; DataSF's footprint for this building carries that lot as its legacy id (mblr SF4046001). DataSF shows that lot retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn); the building's footprint now lies within active lot 3941027, which has no street address in DataSF's Assessor parcels. This feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: UIW (Union Iron Works) Headquarters, Building 104, a Renaissance Revival structure built in 1896 with a distinctive clerestory top floor, unreinforced masonry construction. Per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E), it was previously used as a naval hospital/medical office (WWII-era conversion) and was a 'red-tagged,' seismically challenged building at review time; rehab included demolishing demising walls from the WWII conversion. Part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. as Buildings 101/102. The Port's Jan 2019 update gives 45,237 sq ft (the NRHP nomination gives 37,641) and reports a Certificate of Occupancy in June 2017. Named occupants in the sources read: Tea Living (Tea Collection) as sublessee and JUUL Labs as its subtenant from June 2017 (Port Item 12A, Jan 2019; Potrero View, June 2018); no current tenant is confirmed.

open_questions: Current tenant: an earlier version of this record's map notes described 'a confidential corporate office tenant, 300+ employees'; no source supports that and it was removed on 2026-09-29. The only named occupants in primary sources are Tea Living and JUUL Labs (2017-2019); whether JUUL's ten-year term is still running was not confirmed, and no current occupant has been re-confirmed since those sources.
Buildings 122 and 123, the two small outbuildings adjacent to Building 104 included in the master lease, have no separate record; the NRHP nomination photographs Building 122 (photo #7).

Construction start: the Port's January 2019 memo says construction followed the July 2015 execution of the master lease, the National Trust (Winter 2016 issue) says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' (the year is not printed), and Bisnow (April 2017) says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'. No source read settles the start year.

Architects of Building 104: STRUCTURE magazine names Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects and Mark Hulbert Preservation Architecture as members of the design team that also seismically retrofitted Buildings 14, 101, 102, 104, 115 and 116; the article gives no per-building roles.

Tenants of Building 104: the Port's January 2019 sublease list shows JUUL Labs 'currently under sublease from Tea Living' with a June 2017 commencement date and a ten-year term; the list does not say whether June 2017 is JUUL's or Tea Living's start. Potrero View (June 2018) reports, citing an Orton spokesperson, that JUUL is a subtenant of Tea Living.

Public access to Building 104: the Port's January 2019 memo lists the 'Building 104 lobby' among 'spaces now open to the public (and to be open when construction is complete)'; the memo does not say which listed spaces were already open, the whole building is subleased to a single tenant, and no later source confirms public access.

records.name: Pier 70 Buildings 113–116
names: Union Iron Works Foundry and Warehouse
search_aliases: Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop)
records.summary: The 1885-86 brick Machine Shop and blacksmith/boiler shop (113/114, joined by a 1914 concrete connector, 492 ft long), which the NRHP calls the earliest remaining building in the district, and the 1916-17 reinforced-concrete foundry and warehouse (115/116) beside it. Building 113/114 was closed by the Port and red-tagged in 2001 (115/116 was used for storage). Both were rehabilitated by Orton Development with a buckling-restrained-brace steel system and public atrium, receiving certificates of occupancy in November 2017 (115/116) and April 2018 (113/114), and were subleased to Uber Advanced Technologies Group and Gusto. The state's Office of Historic Preservation lists the 'Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation' of the '20th Street Historic Buildings at Pier 70' among its 2023 Governor's Historic Preservation Awards; its statement does not name individual buildings, but the Historic Preservation Commission's 2013 packet includes Buildings 113 to 116 in that group.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprints -- high confidence in each piece's outline and in the group's overall position (confirmed to sit within Figure 6.4.2's own '113-116' box). Individual identification of which piece(s) correspond to Building 113 vs 114 vs 115 vs 116 specifically is NOT possible from the sources checked -- Figure 6.4.2 draws them as one undifferentiated box, and the 2013 HPC packet's textual description ('115 and 116 abut Building 113/114') does not give a precise position. Rather than guess, this feature represents the combined complex, consistent with how it is actually shown in the source diagram. The combined footprint here (~10,950 sq m / ~117,900 sqft, a planar estimate from this file's own geometry) is larger than Building 113/114 alone (~86,100 sqft per its documented 492ft x 175ft footprint) and smaller than 113/114 + 115/116's combined documented GSF (~95,000 + ~38,000 = ~133,000 GSF) -- broadly consistent given GSF can include multi-level floor area not captured by a footprint, but not independently verified piece-by-piece.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The former Assessor lot blklot 4111004, which DataSF's footprints for these buildings carry as their legacy id (mblr SF4111004; the 2013 HPC packet lists Block 4111, Lots 003 and 004 together with the lots of its other buildings, without assigning buildings to lots), has no street address and was retired by DataSF on 2018-10-02 (active=false). Block 4111 now has active P70-MU lots 4111005-4111010 (added 2019-02-07; lot 4111009 has the address 950 MARYLAND, and lot 4111007 shows a recorded drop date of 2024-05-08 while still flagged active) and this footprint falls within active lot 4111008, also with no street address; no source cited here ties a current lot to Buildings 113-116. This feature uses the real building footprints instead, matched to the specific area that Figure 6.4.2 itself draws as the historic '113-116' complex.
notes.regulatory_context: Union Iron Works Machine Shop and Foundry, Buildings 113/114, on the south side of 20th Street just east of Illinois Street -- 'one of the most valuable and most vulnerable historic resources on the site' per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E). Two unreinforced brick structures (built in 1885 and 1886 per one passage of the HPC packet, while its rehabilitation plans and Port Item 12A, Jan 2019, say 'built from 1885-1888'; the National Register nomination says the eastern, 1885 portion housed the blacksmith and boiler shop and the western, 1886 portion the machine shop) joined in 1914 by a reinforced concrete connector; building-length skylights, rows of high arched windows; ~95,000 GSF, 492ft long by 175ft wide, ~62ft tall. Buildings 115 and 116 abut Building 113/114, constructed 1916-1917, ~38,000 GSF, 57ft tall, with 'unusual windows and monitor skylights.' At review time the complex was red-tagged and subject to an engineer's advisory of imminent collapse. Rehab by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) was proposed (HPC packet) to include 'abatement, demolition or relocation of metal additions to the building on the western and southern facades', a new steel seismic system tied into the brick perimeter, and demolition of two minor eastern appendages (Buildings 23/24, ~1,500 GSF). Proposed for industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail, alongside Building 14, framing a shared ~45,000 sf courtyard.
