records.name: Pier 70 Building 14
records.summary: A World War II double-gable corrugated-metal heavy warehouse east of the Machine Shop, framing, with Buildings 113-116, a ~45,000 sq ft courtyard per the 2013 planning packet (the National Register nomination has it forming a courtyard with Building 2); one of the smaller of Orton's Historic Core buildings at 16,315 sq ft before rehabilitation (Port's 2019 memo), rehabilitated with a new mezzanine and seismic bracing (certificate of occupancy August 2017) and subleased whole to Obscura Digital (The Madison Square Garden Company) for seven years from September 2017. The California Office of Historic Preservation's 2023 Governor's Historic Preservation Awards include the Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation, which covers 'a half dozen historic buildings known as "20th Street Historic Buildings at Pier 70"'; the award text does not name individual buildings, so it does not say whether Building 14 is one of them.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 14: position matches Figure 6.4.2's own label (39m away, the closest and only plausible candidate among the lot's other footprint pieces once 113/114/115/116's own pieces are excluded) and its area independently matches the previously-cited 16,315 GSF within 3%. As with the other buildings Pier & Point has split from oversized Assessor lots, the match rests on position and size, not an explicit building-number attribute in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and no distinct Assessor lot of its own. Its footprint lay about 76% on the former lot blklot 4052001 and about 24% on former lot 4111003, both retired by DataSF on 2018-10-02; it now falls within active lot 4111008 (no street address, shared with Buildings 113-116). The 2013 HPC packet lists Block 4046 Lot 001, Block 4111 Lots 003 and 004 and a portion of Block 4052 Lot 001 as the project location for the ten historic buildings; the earlier statement that Buildings 101/102/104/113-116/21 shared one lot with Building 14 is withdrawn (101/102/104 lay on 4046001 and 113-116 on 4111004). This feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Building 14, a basic heavy warehouse with approximately 16,000 GSF (the 2013 HPC packet, 2013.1168E, says 'dated to 1941' in its project description and 'constructed in 1944' in its rehabilitation plans; the National Register nomination says 1941; Port Item 12A, Jan 2019, says 1944 in its text and lists 1941 in its Table 1, so no build year is settled here) of space and a 66 foot height, sits immediately east of the Union Iron Works Machine Shop complex (Buildings 113/114/115/116), framing, with them, an approximately 45,000 square foot courtyard per the 2013 HPC packet's rehabilitation concept (not the D4D). Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project; proposed for the same industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail as its neighbors.

open_questions: Obscura Digital's seven-year sublease from September 2017 would have ended around 2024; no source names the current occupant.

The year Building 14 was built is not settled: the NRHP nomination says 1941, while the Port's 2019 memo (prose: 'constructed in 1944'; Table 1: 1941) and the 2013 HPC packet (prose: 'constructed in 1944' and 'dated to 1941'; Table 1: 1941) each print both years. The milestone uses 1941.

When the rehabilitation began is not settled: the Port's 2019 memo says the master lease was fully executed in July 2015 'with construction commencing thereafter'; the National Trust's Winter 2016 issue says the work 'began this past September' without printing the year; a 2017 Bisnow article says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'.

Architects of Building 14: STRUCTURE magazine (undated) names Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects and Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture as the design team for the Building 113/114 renovation, and says that project also seismically retrofitted Building 14.

Courtyard at Building 14: the 2013 HPC packet (November 26, 2013) says Buildings 113/114/115/116 and 14 frame an approximately 45,000 sq ft courtyard, and the Port's 2019 update (January 4, 2019) lists a publicly accessible 45,000 sq ft Historic Core plaza; the National Register nomination (listed April 17, 2014) separately says Building 14, together with Building 2, forms a courtyard. records.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a stepped height envelope up to 180 ft (188 ft on the enacted height map, taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count), one of three blocks (with 5 and 13) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage; no design review approval or construction start found. The amended and restated development agreement, which includes Phasing Plan amendments, passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'); its effect on Block 1's timing has not been read.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to an Assessor parcel of its own: it lies entirely inside active Assessor lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln, added to DataSF's Assessor layer on 2024-10-15), a larger lot that is not Block 1's own. No source read describes the block's ground condition. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram by fitting it to multiple real street points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with control-point georeferencing. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third revision) in a single consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth revision) after a mis-measured control point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. The statement that the block is unbuilt is not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) does not list a Block 1 application. The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, PDF p.107) says 'Within the PG&E sub-area are a portion of Block 1, the entirety of Blocks 13 and 14', and defines that sub-area as 'a portion of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018'. records.summary: Planned residential block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a stepped height envelope of 65 ft and 85 ft (73 ft and 93 ft on the enacted height map, taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count); no design review approval or construction start found. The Board of Supervisors approved the project and Development Agreement on April 21, 2020 (Ordinance No. 62-20; the agreement's effective date is May 25, 2020).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (no design-review approval or construction start found; the 2024 annual compliance report records environmental remediation of the Project's 'Tank Farm Area and Block 4', contracted in Q3 2021) and no Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows its footprint within a much larger active lot, 4175028 (1241 Delaware St, about 21,900 sq m, recorded 2022-08-30), which also overlaps the Block 3 and Block 9 footprints. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see the mapping log), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 by georeferencing against many real-street control points. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third revision) by detecting the block colours consistently across the whole block layout at once. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth revision) after fixing a mis-measured control point -- see the mapping log. DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St, PPS-MU zoning, recorded 2022-08-30) holds 3,041 m2 of this drawing. It also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza and parts of Prequel Park and Waterfront Park, so Pier & Point reads it as an undivided parent lot; Block 4 has no lot of its own and the drawing is kept.

notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows this footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St), not a lot of its own.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) confirms residential is permitted here (Laboratory and Life Science are not). Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D gives Block 4 two height limits by its colour-coded labels, 85 ft and 65 ft; the '100'MAX' label sits on a dimension line (a plan extent of the 85 ft zone), not a height, and Standard 6.2.2 places Block 4 among the lowrise buildings (up to 100 feet). The D4D's text on Figure 1.6.4 names Block 4, on the waterfront, among its 'differentiated buildings'. No construction-start source found.

records.summary: Planned residential highrise tower on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, up to 220 ft (228 ft on the enacted height map, taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count); a July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request sought flexibility to make Block 5 all PDR space (the developer described a possible 'small data center'), and on Sept 18, 2026 the Chronicle reported the developer planned to retract that part of the amendment; the amendment package passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, after committee revisions stating that data center uses are not permitted on any block, and the amendment package was enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026); no construction start found to date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (no design-review approval or construction start found; it is not in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list) and no Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows about 93% of its footprint within the much larger active lot 4175500 (1248 Georgia Ln, about 15,900 sq m, recorded 2024-10-15). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to real street positions at multiple points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 5; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

The Development Agreement amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770) passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The Clerk of the Board's certificate in each file's 'Leg Final' attachment shows the final passage (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), although the Legistar web page's 10/6/2026 history row carries no action text. The Land Use and Transportation Committee's Sept 28, 2026 revisions state that data center uses are not permitted on any block. Whether Block 5's all-PDR flexibility sought in July survived is not settled by the documents read: the committee-amended ordinance text (Leg Ver3 of File 260770) shows Block 5's PDR column under note (4), which limits the listed PDR uses to the basement, ground floor, 2nd floor and mezzanine and makes other PDR uses not permitted, and shows Laboratory and Life Science as permitted; the Sept 28 draft Design for Development attached to the agreement shows Block 5's PDR column as 'P(5)', whose note lists the same PDR uses as permitted with other PDR uses not permitted and states no floor limit. Neither text permits PDR use without limit. The board packets, which hold the final text sent to the Mayor, were not read.

Block 5's 2031-2034 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite); no current Block 5 schedule was found. The Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary lists a proposed move of Block 5 from Development Phase 3 to Phase 2 in the 2026 amendment package, which Legistar lists as enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (the enacted text has not yet been checked for this move, so whether it is in it is not confirmed); the summary gives no new dates.

Height on Block 5: the enacted map labels the block "228'/138'" and "138'", with a 220 ft tower and 130 ft southern portion if the building is majority non-residential (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29; effective November 13, 2026 by our count, a legal date computed by Pier & Point and not printed in the text). Until then the adopted 85 ft base and 220 ft tower apply, read from the colour-coded labels in the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 ("220'/85'"; the "111'MAX" label is a plan dimension of the tower zone, not a height). How the map's "138'" base relates to the digest's 'podium' wording is not stated in the documents read; the Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary (Resolution No. 21945) proposed an 8 ft increase on blocks with residential uses.

records.name: Potrero Power Station Block 7A
records.summary: The L-shaped southwestern portion of Block 7 at Humboldt St and Louisiana Paseo, approved March 2, 2022 for a Foster + Partners-designed 27-story, approximately 237-ft market-rate tower with 325 units, ground-floor retail and childcare over a basement garage; the tallest building permitted on the site. No building permit or construction start has been reported as of September 2026. The developer's amended and restated development agreement, which includes Housing, Transportation and Phasing Plan amendments, passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (legislative event date); Legistar lists the agreement and its matching zoning ordinance as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26).

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4232019, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 7A is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size; the only source read for the name is the Planning Commission's packet for its July 15, 2021 informational hearing, whose page 14 is titled 'Block 7a Planning Commission Informational' and does not itself locate the building (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 3,877 m2 against the lot's 3,614 m2; 92% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 98% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 7A is not yet built, which is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says the developer had submitted no building permits for any market-rate housing projects.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4232019 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 7A. Lot 4232019 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4232019; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 7 as one numbered block, with its height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: the north-west part (on Humboldt St at Louisiana Paseo) is labelled 240'/85' (maximum height 240 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and the rest of the block (east side and south strip) is 85'; the two '150'MAX' markings are plan dimensions of the tower, not heights. The D4D numbers only 'Block 7'; 'Block 7A' and 'Block 7B' are the names SF Planning's own approvals use for the two buildings (e.g. 'Approval of the Design Review Application of Block 7A', March 2, 2022, Case 2017-011878PHA-04, and Block 7B, March 2, 2022). The Sophie Maxwell Building ('Block 7b, the Sophie Maxwell Building' in the 2024 annual compliance report; real blklot 4232020, addressed 1212 MARYLAND in DataSF Parcels; already mapped separately in this dataset) occupies part of this block; this polygon is the REMAINING portion, clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint (the clipping is our own work). The remainder is presumed to correspond to 'Block 7A' (Foster + Partners-designed rental tower, press-reported heights of 240-264 ft depending on source, consistent with this figure's 240 ft max) -- design review approved March 2, 2022; the 2024 annual compliance report says no market-rate building permits had been submitted; no construction-start source found.

open_questions: Construction start: none found. Searched the 2021-2024 DA compliance reports (the 2024 report says no market-rate building permits have been submitted), SF YIMBY through Sept 2026, the Chronicle (Jul 29 and Aug 3, 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025) and Potrero View (Oct 2025). SocketSite (Jul 2021) said construction was 'slated to commence in 2023'; SF YIMBY (Mar 2021) said Block 7 construction was expected to start 'by 2023, with completion by 2026'. Neither happened.

The July 2026 Chronicle line 'tallest residential tower would be permitted to reach 248 feet' does not name a block. The Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary (Resolution No. 21945, attached to BOS File 260724) says the amendment would 'increase the maximum height by 8 feet' on residential blocks, 'from 240 feet to 248 feet on Block 7', and lists Block 5's existing maximum as 220 feet; Block 7 includes 7A, whose design review approval is about 237 ft. The enacted height map (BOS File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29) labels Block 7 "248'/93'", and its bulk table (p. 32) shows the 'Highrise towers on Blocks 5 and 7' range as 191'-248'. The ordinance passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment number 209-26); it takes effect on the 31st day after enactment, November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). Until then 240 ft is the limit in force.

Unit count drift: 277 (press 2021) -> 325 (approval 2022) -> 319 (compliance reports' LBE appendix); the Planning Commission slides (July 2021) show '315' only on the 'Previous Phase 1' map inside Block 8 and '420' for Block 7 (7A with 7b) on the 'Current Phase 1' slide, so no slide gives a 7A-only count. Which figure a future permit will carry is unknown.

The SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says Associate Capital 'will move on to constructing a 300-unit market-rate apartment building and a waterfront park at the adjoining site'. The SF Standard (Aug 3, 2026) calls a 342-unit apartment complex Fifth Space's 'next building at the site', and DBI permit 202205194622 (151 Humboldt St, description '(block 8)', 342 residential units) is for Block 8, so Block 7A does not appear to be the next building.

Ground-floor childcare is assigned to Block 7 in the compliance reports. The April 25, 2023 Planning Director approval of the childcare amendment changed the Phasing Plan from two 6,000-sq-ft facilities in Phase 1 to 'two or three child care facilities' of at least 4,000 sq ft each, totaling at least 12,000 sq ft, with at least one in Phase 1; the Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary describes the existing control as 'Childcare Facilities may be provided on any Block' and proposes 'on any Block or within one mile of the Project'. Which facility goes on Block 7A is therefore not fixed by those documents; the design review approval shows about 6,270 sq ft of childcare in the building.
No cost, financing, general contractor or ground-lease information exists for Block 7A in any source found; the land is developer-owned (not Port), so no Port lease applies.

The 'Block 7A' / 'Block 7B' names are the sponsor's; the D4D treats Block 7 as one block with a single 240-ft highrise envelope. This record's map-shape note saying 7A/7B are 'informal press/developer labels' is consistent with the Planning documents, which nonetheless use 7A/7B as case names.

Block 7A rendering (Foster + Partners indicative views from the Design Review Approval packet) removed from the images shown here on 2026-09-29: the plan sheets are marked '(c) Foster + Partners 2020', which is not a licence to host them. The packet remains cited as a source (the Block 7A Design Review Approval); linked, not hosted.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the 2029 expected completion was removed. It rested only on October 2020 forecasts (the Phase 1 approval's 2020-2029 development schedule and SocketSite's October 9, 2020 block table), which its own basis note called stale; no current source gives Block 7A a completion year, and none is shown until one is sourced. The same pattern was removed from Humboldt Street Plaza on 2026-09-29.

Units on Block 7A: the design review approval (2022) gives 325 (unit mix 49 studios, 163 one-bed, 80 two-bed, 33 three-bed). Other stated values: 277 (press, March-June 2021); 319 (2021 and 2022 compliance reports, LBE section); approximately 325 (2021-2024 compliance reports, housing section). The July 2021 Planning Commission slides give no Block 7A-only count: their 'Current Phase 1' slide shows Block 7 (7A with 7b) at 420 units (their 315 is on the 'Previous Phase 1' map, inside Block 8).

records.summary: Planned ~240,000-sq-ft, 250-room waterfront hotel site around the Stack and the Unit 3 Power Block (partly demolished in 2023-24; the D4D provides for the hotel with or without Unit 3); the Chronicle reported in May 2025 that the hotel's construction 'could be a decade away' and that the developer proposed an interim park (Prequel Park) on the land instead.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built, and it is not vacant land: it is where the Unit 3 Power Block (partly demolished June 2023 to July 2024 per the 2024 annual compliance report) and the 300-ft Stack stand, and where the interim Prequel Park is planned. No Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows its footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St, about 21,900 sq m, recorded 2022-08-30), which also overlaps the Block 3 and Block 4 footprints. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, positioned by matching several points on it to real streets, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (rebuilt 2026-09-16 with a refined multi-point georeferencing of the site's diagram), and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St, PPS-MU zoning, recorded 2022-08-30) holds 5,041 m2 of this drawing. It also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza and parts of Prequel Park and Waterfront Park, so Pier & Point reads it as an undivided parent lot; Block 9 has no lot of its own and the drawing is kept.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 11; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Planning Department's October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists approximately 219,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 11 and 177,000 for Block 12 (about 396,000 together, plus retail, PDR, childcare and other uses); no source reconciles the two figures.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +15 ft height increase is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The enacted height map labels Block 11 "145'" (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29), the 15 ft the Chronicle reported, effective November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). No construction or design review date for the taller building has been found.

This record's map outline is DataSF Assessor lot 4232021 (active, unaddressed, recorded 2022-08-30), chosen because 77% of our earlier trace of the D4D figure lies inside it; that this lot is Block 11's own parcel is an inference from location, shape and size, and no document read names the lot.

records.name: Potrero Power Station Block 12
records.summary: Planned commercial block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (the design guidelines permit office and laboratory/life-science uses), paired with Block 11 in the project engineer's description of about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (the Planning Department's October 2020 Phase 1 approval lists about 177,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 12 and 219,000 for Block 11, about 396,000 together; the sources differ and are not reconciled). Design was under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report. In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Block 12's height by 23 feet and let it become residential or commercial; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'); the enacted height map gives Block 12 123 ft, or 115 ft if majority non-residential (100 ft in the adopted rules), taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count. No construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4232023, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 12 is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 2,940 m2 against the lot's 2,645 m2; 77% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 85% of it). No document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 12 is not yet built, which is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says vertical applications are under review for Blocks 11 and 12.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4232023 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 12. Lot 4232023 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4232023; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 100 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3. Paired with Block 11 on the project's MEP engineer's page (Meyers+), which describes the two blocks together as about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (see that entry for the combined GSF estimate); the final D4D's Table 3.1.1 permits laboratory and life-science uses on Block 12, but no cited source calls the pair a life-science campus. No construction-start source found; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) says vertical applications for Blocks 11 and 12 were under review.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 12; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Planning Department's October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists approximately 177,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 12 and 219,000 for Block 11 (about 396,000 together, plus PDR, retail and other uses); no source reconciles the two figures.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +23 ft height increase and added residential flexibility is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The enacted height map labels Block 12 "123'" with a 115 ft limit for a majority non-residential building (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29), the 23 ft the Chronicle reported, effective November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). The enacted use rules (residential on Block 12) have not yet been checked against this record, so its use fact still shows the adopted rule.

Whether Blocks 11 and 12 are described as a life-science campus anywhere: the Meyers+ page, which pairs them, describes about 430,000 sq ft of office (its list of uses for the wider project includes laboratory), and the 2024 annual compliance report treats them together in a single 'Blocks 11 and 12 Design Review Application' without calling them a life-science campus; the D4D permits laboratory/life-science use on Block 12, and the Chronicle (July 29, 2026) quotes developer Enrique Landa saying all commercial parcels can be 'all PDR, all offices, all life sciences or all labs', but no cited source says that is the plan for Block 12.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Update 2026-10-12: the Board of Supervisors passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (see milestones). Update 2026-10-17: Legistar lists the package as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 17, 2026); the Board's final passage on Oct 6, 2026 (Ayes: 11) is shown by the Clerk of the Board's certificate in each file's 'Leg Final' attachment (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), although the Legistar web page's 10/6/2026 history row carries no action text.

records.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard; the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 gives it 85 ft and 125 ft height limits, and its build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation. The October 2026 height ordinance's map labels the block 93 ft and 133 ft, but the block is in the PG&E Sub-Area, where the zoning controls (the 2020 limits as well as the new ones) are not operative until a Notice of Joinder to the Development Agreement is recorded or the land is conveyed to the Developer; no source read shows either, so on the sources read neither set of limits has taken effect on this land. The Board of Supervisors approved the project and Development Agreement on April 21, 2020 (Ordinance No. 62-20; the agreement's effective date is May 25, 2020).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and is not vacant land: per SF Planning's project page and the final D4D (Figure 1.2.1, printed p.12) it lies in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard (the D4D's 'PG&E Sub-area'), whose build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation. DataSF Parcels lists an active lot with an address, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, recorded 2024-10-15), covering nearly all of this approximate footprint; the dataset does not say whether that lot is the switchyard parcel. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, positioned by matching several points on it to real streets, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with a refined multi-point georeferencing of the diagram, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and re-corrected the same day after a mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Block 13's land is not part of the developer-owned 21-acre Power Station parcel: it is in the 4.8-acre PG&E-owned northern switchyard (final D4D Figure 1.2.1; SF Planning project page), which the Master Plan includes but whose build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation and on the property coming within the Development Agreement's jurisdiction. DataSF Parcels lists an active lot, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, recorded 2024-10-15), overlapping about 99% of this approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) shows Block 13 permits Residential, Institutional, Retail, Non-Retail Sales/Services (office), Entertainment and PDR uses, but the table's notes limit several of them to the lower floors: office to the basement, ground floor and mezzanine (note 8); retail and entertainment to the basement, ground floor, mezzanine and 2nd floor (notes 7 and 9); and PDR to the listed uses at the basement, ground floor, 2nd floor and mezzanine (note 4). Laboratory and Life Science are not permitted. Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D gives Block 13 two height limits by its colour-coded labels, 85 ft and 125 ft; the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on the block sit on tick-ended dimension lines (plan extents of the 125 ft zone), not heights, and Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft). The tallest limit on the site is Block 7's 240 ft. No construction-start source found.

The October 2026 ordinance redrew the PG&E Sub-Area. BOS File 260770's 'Leg Final' attachment shows the earlier Map 249.87-1 on p. 53 with a diagonal strikethrough, which the ordinance says marks an image proposed for deletion ("Images proposed for deletion are shown with a diagonal strikethrough and rectangular border", p. 56); that map shows no Block 14. Its PG&E Sub-area outline runs to the diagonal edge that ends at Craig Lane, the same diagonal that forms Block 14's hypotenuse in the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 (compared by eye), so under the earlier map Block 14 was inside the sub-area, where Section 249.87(t), existing text (p. 52), kept the controls from becoming operative (no source read shows a Notice of Joinder or a conveyance); the D4D's 90 ft label therefore did not apply to it. The replacement on p. 54, a rectangular-bordered image of the kind the ordinance says is proposed for addition (p. 55; it has no caption of its own and sits directly after the struck map), labels "PG&E Sub-Area" (printed in capitals) west of Georgia Street and shows Block 14 east of it, outside the sub-area, so the operative-date condition in Section 249.87(t) (p. 52) and Section 5(c) (p. 56) does not apply to Block 14. The 2020 D4D's Figure E.13.4 (printed p. 434) shows the earlier layout in its no-PG&E-Sub-area scenario: it labels the area "PG&E Sub-area" and shows no Block 14. Why the sub-area was redrawn is not stated in the sources read. File 260724's recital (d) (p. 2) gives the PG&E Sub-Area as "approximately 3.8 acres", against the 4.8 acres in the D4D (Figure 1.2.1, printed p. 12); the difference is not explained.
No source found for a specific intended use of Block 14 beyond the D4D's generic permitted-uses table; it is the smallest block on the site per the D4D's own Land Use Plan figure.

records.name: Potrero Power Station Block 15 / Station A
records.summary: Adaptive reuse of the 1901-02 Station A turbine hall into an approximately 456,000 gsf office building with an eight-story vertical addition, approved by the Planning Director on March 2, 2022 (the Planning Commission granted its office allocation on October 22, 2020); as of the 2024 annual compliance report, construction of the addition had not started (only 2024 brick stabilization work is described). In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Station A's height by 30 feet; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26 for the agreement and its zoning ordinance); the enacted height map gives 175 ft on the northern half and 190 ft on the southern half (145 and 160 ft in the adopted rules), taking effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4175026, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 15 (Station A) is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 5,104 m2 against the lot's 4,315 m2; 85% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 100% of it). No Port document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 15 is Station A, an existing historic building (the 1901 turbine hall; DBI permit 202406053802 in 2024 describes the unoccupied 'station a building'), so it is not vacant land; the approved vertical addition has not been started.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4175026 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 15 (Station A). Lot 4175026 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4175026; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Station A: the site's historic 1901 unreinforced-brick turbine hall (a four-story brick structure per the 2018 Draft EIR), vacant/unoccupied. The design review approves adaptive reuse into approximately 403,750 GSF of office (the Planning Commission granted the office allocation on Oct 22, 2020, Motion 20801) via an eight-story vertical addition above the retained historic shell and a public mid-block passage through the building (the design-review memo describes it as accessible from both Georgia Lane and Power Station Park in one place, and as connecting Georgia Lane and Louisiana Paseo in another), designed by Herzog & de Meuron with Adamson Associates; the Planning Director approved the Design Review Application on March 2, 2022. The design-review memo gives a total height of 205 feet measured from grade for the Station A building with its eight-story addition, but also says the addition is 'subject to the prevailing 145-foot and 160-foot building height maximums', and the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 labels the block's two strips 145' and 160'; the sources read do not reconcile the two figures. The Chronicle (July 29, 2026) reports a requested Development Agreement amendment that would let Station A grow by 30 feet; it is not shown here as enacted. Construction of the addition had not started per SF YIMBY (Aug 27, 2025) and the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which describes only 2024 brick stabilization work. The 2018 Draft EIR project proposed demolishing Station A (its Alternative D retained it); SF YIMBY (June 2021) says the adaptive reuse was included following community pushback against demolition, and no source found names who advocated for it.

open_questions: No construction-start date for the vertical addition is stated in any source found; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) describes design approval and 2024 brick stabilization work, not adaptive-reuse construction. The Oct 22, 2020 Planning Commission minutes were not found at a checkable URL; the Design Review Approval memo is cited for that hearing instead.

The 2022 design review approval describes a 205-ft total height for the Station A addition, while the adopted D4D (section 6.14.5) allows new construction on Station A up to 145 feet on the northern half and 160 feet on the southern half; how the 205 ft relates to those limits (for example whether it includes the existing walls or rooftop elements) is not stated in the sources read. The '230'MAX' label in the D4D's Figure 6.2.3, which also appears on the enacted map along the southern strip, is a dimension marker, not a height.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +30 ft height increase for Station A is tied to the Development Agreement amendment (BOS File 260724) and Planning Code ordinance (File 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and finally on Oct 6, 2026 (11 ayes), and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The enacted height map labels the strips "175'" and "190'" (File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29), 30 ft above the adopted 145 and 160, effective November 13, 2026 by our count (a legal date computed by Pier & Point, not printed in the text). Whether the 2022 design review approval (205 ft total) is affected by the new limits is not stated in the sources read.
No source found stating a cost estimate for Station A's rehabilitation and vertical addition.

The Draft EIR image shown here as a 'before' view is not a single photograph -- it is a composite DEIR report page carrying six separate existing-conditions photos of Station A's turbine hall and machine shop, each with its own caption. It may be better described as a document than as a single before photo.

The February 17, 2020 photo is shown as a current ('now') view rather than a 'before' view because the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) describes no adaptive-reuse construction on Station A (only 2024 brick stabilization), so the building's exterior likely hasn't changed much since. If construction has started since 2026-09-24, this photo is out of date.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Update 2026-10-12: the Board of Supervisors passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (see milestones). Update 2026-10-17: Legistar lists the package as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment Nos. 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 17, 2026); the Board's final passage on Oct 6, 2026 (Ayes: 11) is shown by the Clerk of the Board's certificate in each file's 'Leg Final' attachment (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), although the Legistar web page's 10/6/2026 history row carries no action text.

Story count of Station A: the 2022 Design Review Approval (March 2, 2022) describes the existing Station A plus an 8-story vertical addition; SF YIMBY (June 2021) called it a twelve-story adaptive reuse.

records.name: Potrero Power Station Block 8
records.summary: Mid-rise market-rate residential block between Maryland and Delaware streets, south of Humboldt St and north of Power Station Park East, approved March 2, 2022 for a Foster + Partners-designed 14-story, approximately 125-ft, 339-unit building with about 18,000 sq ft of retail; in August 2026 JPMorgan Chase agreed to finance roughly $200 million for a 342-unit building at 151 Humboldt St, with construction expected to begin in fall 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4232022, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. DataSF lists this lot at 151 Humboldt St, which is the address the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) gives for the Block 8 building; a City building-permit record, 202205194622 (filed 2022-05-19, a 13-story residential/mixed-use building), also lists Block 4232, Lot 022 at that address and ends its description '(block 8)'; the Block 8 design-review memo itself lists only four parent lots (4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001, 4232/006) that predate the 2022 subdivision. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 8 is not yet built (not started as of the 2024 annual compliance report, March 2025; construction expected to begin in fall 2026 per the Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4232022 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Lot 4232022 (151 Humboldt St, active, recorded 2022-08-30) lies almost entirely within the block and carries the address the Chronicle gives for the Block 8 building, so the outline is that lot; the identification rests on that address match, on location, and on a City building-permit record (202205194622) that lists Block 4232, Lot 022 and ends its description '(block 8)'; the design-review memo lists only the pre-subdivision parent lots.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D shows Block 8 with two height limits by its colour-coded labels: 125 ft (along Humboldt and Maryland Streets) and 85 ft (its south-east part); the two '90'MAX' labels are tick-ended dimension lines, not heights (the design-review staff memo describes D4D standard A.8.1 as letting the part of the building above the streetwall extend up to 90 feet in depth from the Humboldt Street and Maryland Street property lines). The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) confirms residential is permitted here (Laboratory and Life Science are not). Foster + Partners is the design architect per the March 2022 design-review approval and the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026). Unit counts differ by source: 249 (SF YIMBY, March 2021), 339 (2022 design-review approval), 342 (Chronicle, Aug 2026), 348 (2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025: 'approximately 348 new market-rate residential units'; 348 is also the proposed-units field of City permit 202205194622, whose description says 342). The approved height is about 125 ft to the last occupied floor plus up to 20 ft of screened mechanical (plan set); SF YIMBY reported 140 ft (March 2021) and 156 ft (March 2022). Construction had not started as of the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025); the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) says it is expected to begin in the fall.

search_aliases: PG&E Southern Switchyard (outside the project boundary; not part of redevelopment)
records.summary: The PG&E Southern Switchyard, one of two PG&E electrical switchyards at the western end of the Potrero Power Station site, shown on the Design for Development's site-boundary figure outside the project site boundary. The other, the roughly 4.8-acre 'PG&E Northern Switchyard' at the corner of 22nd and Illinois Streets, owned and operated by PG&E, is inside the dashed 29-acre planning-area boundary but outside the 21-acre parcel the developer owns and outside the Development Agreement's jurisdiction (this dataset shows that area as Blocks 13 and 14).

notes.accuracy_caveat: LOW CONFIDENCE, DIRECTIONAL ONLY -- this is a materially weaker approximation than this site's numbered blocks. This polygon marks the PG&E Southern Switchyard, which the final D4D (p.12, Figure 1.2.1) places outside the project site boundary, between Humboldt and 23rd Streets west of Block 5. The 4.8-acre PG&E parcel at 22nd and Illinois that public reporting and SF Planning describe is the separate Northern Switchyard, which is inside the project boundary and is not what this polygon shows (this dataset represents that area as Blocks 13 and 14). This polygon's reshaped area is ~4.6 acres, but the D4D gives no area for the Southern Switchyard, so that figure is not a check against anything. The D4D diagram does not further subdivide this area (it is entirely outside the project site boundary, so the D4D had no reason to draw its actual fenceline), so the true switchyard footprint may still differ in detail from this trace. Treat this polygon as marking the correct general block and rough shape (including wrapping around Block 5's south side to 23rd St/Georgia Lane), not the switchyard's real surveyed boundary.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-10-12) lists an active, addressed lot, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, about 30,900 m2, recorded 2024-10-15, M-2 and PPS-MU zoning), under about 78% of this drawing. The same lot also lies under about 99% of the Block 13 drawing (the Northern Switchyard area), extends well beyond this drawing, and the dataset does not say who owns it or whether it is a switchyard parcel; this drawing is only a directional placeholder, so it keeps hand-traced approximate geometry. Real ownership and the 'not part of the sale' status are documented in secondary sources, but no source read gives a precise Assessor-parcel boundary for the Southern Switchyard. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The 2018 draft EIR (Vol. 1, Ch. 2, p. 2-5) describes the 4.8-acre PG&E sub-area (the Northern Switchyard) as 'a portion of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018 and owned by PG&E'; DataSF now shows lot 4175018 as retired on 2024-10-15, the day lots 4175499 and 4175500 were recorded.
notes.regulatory_context: The PG&E Southern Switchyard: one of two PG&E switchyards at the western end of the Potrero Power Station site (final D4D p.12, Figure 1.2.1), south of the 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard and north of the Transbay Cable site, outside the project site boundary; labelled 'SWITCHYARDS (PG&E)' on Figure 6.2.3, between Illinois Street and Georgia Lane beside Block 5. The 4.8-acre Northern Switchyard at 22nd and Illinois Streets, 'currently owned and operated by PG&E as an electrical switchyard' (SF Planning project page), is a different feature: it is within the 29-acre master plan and the project boundary, and the D4D sets standards for redevelopment of the entire PG&E Sub-area (this dataset represents that area as Blocks 13 and 14). For the Southern Switchyard drawn here, 'outside the project site boundary' is the D4D's statement; the 1990s CPUC divestiture EIR describes a switchyard in the southwest portion of the plant site along the east side of Illinois Street that 'is not part of the sale, and will be retained by PG&E'. Recorded as existing on the strength of the February 2020 D4D showing it; no more recent source was found. 'Commercial' is the nearest category in this map's use list; the feature is an electrical switchyard, a utility use (the D4D's 'Utility and Infrastructure' category), and the map has no utility category.

notes.regulatory_context: The historic ~300 ft tall smokestack from the power station's Unit 3 generating block, called out on the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 as 'EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')' the plan retains (Standard 6.2.1 sets its height limit at its existing height) -- a literal, physical landmark left standing amid the redevelopment, marked on Figure 6.2.3 in the open space just south of Block 9's outlined footprint, not inside it (see the Potrero Power Station Block 9 record for that block; D4D section 4.21 treats the land around the Stack as Stack Plaza, 'the signature public space of the Power Station'), at the site's waterfront edge. open_questions: The Stack's construction date differs between sources. The 2018 Draft EIR gives 1965 (Table 4.D-1, source line 'San Francisco Planning Department HRER, 2018', lists the Boiler Stack as 1965; section 4.D: 'both constructed in 1965'; project description, section 2.D.4: 'Boiler Stack (ca. 1965)'). The Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says 'a remnant of the retired power plant built in 1962' and SF YIMBY (Oct 24, 2025) says 'the retired 1962-built power plant'; neither gives the Stack's own year. The final Design for Development says PG&E added Unit 3 'in the 1960s' and captions a '1964 photo of Unit 3 and the Stack'. The DEIR says the Third Street Industrial District was documented in 2008 with a period of significance ending in 1958, and that the 2018 historic resource evaluation extended it to 1965, adding the Stack and Unit 3. This dossier gives the DEIR's date as the DEIR's and does not choose between the sources.

ICA SF's press release (Oct 28, 2025) says it will launch a public art initiative at 'The Stack at Prequel Park' in 2027, turning the Stack into 'a vertical gallery', and its exhibition page says 'Opening Fall 2027'. The Port Commission memo (Nov 14, 2025) says the Planning Department issued a temporary use authorization for Prequel Park in June 2025 and that the developer hopes to open the park in the first quarter of 2027 (page 2) or the third quarter of 2027 (page 4). No source says whether that authorization covers opening the Stack itself to visitors. The DataSF building-permit applications for Prequel Park (202512051053, 202512051066, 202512081182) were all 'filed' with no issued date in the data read on 2026-10-12, and none of their descriptions mentions the Stack.

Structural condition: the 2018 Draft EIR (Mitigation Measure M-CR-5e) says a preservation plan 'shall include stabilization of the Boiler Stack prior to construction' only 'If deemed necessary upon further condition assessment of the resource'; no condition assessment was found. Ownership: the DEIR describes the Power Station sub-area as 'currently owned by the project sponsor' but does not say which lot holds the Stack, and no source read says who owns the Stack's parcel today. Landmark status: the DEIR says the Stack is a contributor to the Third Street Industrial District and 'is not considered to be individually significant'; no source read shows an individual landmark designation.

records.name: Power Station Park
records.summary: Planned ~1.2-acre central park in two blocks either side of Maryland Street: East between Blocks 8 and 12 (multi-purpose lawn and plaza opening to Unit 3 and the Stack) and West between Blocks 7 and 11 (play plaza). Schematic design was approved by the Planning Director on June 23, 2022 (Case 2017-011878PHA-03). A Phase 1 open space delivered with Blocks 8 (East) and 11 (West); as of the March 2025 annual report neither block nor the park was under construction. Financing of $200 million for the Block 8 residential building, which delivers the park's east half, was reported on Aug 3, 2026 (the Chronicle says the building 'would rise', so construction has not started); the amended development agreement, which includes Phasing Plan amendments, passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it as approved by the Mayor and enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Enactment No. 208-26); its effect on the park's timing has not been read.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- the outline is built from recorded Assessor lot lines except one cut. West part (between Blocks 7 and 11): the east arm of lot 4232011. The two lots 4232011 and 4232012 are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: Louisiana Paseo is the north-south strip made of lot 4232012 and the west strip of lot 4232011, and Power Station Park West is the east-west arm of lot 4232011. The line between them, about 33 m long through lot 4232011, is not a recorded lot line: it is the straight extension of the strip's east edge, which the recorded vertices of both lots lie on to within 0.1 m. East part (between Blocks 8 and 12): all of lot 4232013, a recorded lot, with no cut. No document names the lot as the park; it is matched by location to the D4D's Power Station Park East. The park is planned and not yet built.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn): the east arm of lot 4232011 (recorded 2022-08-30; active), cut from the rest of that lot along a straight line, and all of lot 4232013 (recorded 2022-08-30; active). Cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 4.25.1 - Power Station Park and Louisiana Paseo: Concept Plan Overview (printed p.119), which labels the two park areas 'Power Station Park West' (2) and 'Power Station Park East' (1), and Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The park is two areas on two sets of lots: the west part is the east arm of Assessor lot 4232011 (assigned from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams; its west edge is a straight extension, not a recorded lot line) and the east part is all of lot 4232013. Both lots are active, recorded 2022-08-30. No document names either lot as the park.
notes.regulatory_context: The site's central public open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label -- two rectangles, one between Blocks 7 and 11 (labelled 'POWER STATION PARK') and one between Blocks 8 and 12, on either side of Maryland Street; Block 9 lies east of Delaware Street and does not border it. Not yet built: consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) and the SF Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026 (Block 8 construction 'expected to begin in the fall'). Of the blocks around it, Block 7B (the Sophie Maxwell Building) sits 'between Humboldt Street, Maryland Street, Louisiana Paseo and Power Station Park' (2024 annual compliance report) and opened in October 2025 (SF YIMBY, Oct 24, 2025); the others are still planned.

open_questions: No construction start, groundbreaking or completion date for either park block was found in any source through 2026-09-17; the park is tied to Blocks 8 and 11, and the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) says Block 8 construction is 'expected to begin in the fall' after JPMorgan agreed to finance about $200 million. The map shape's 'not yet built' note is consistent with the March 2025 annual report but nothing later confirms it. The expected-completion milestone uses Phase 1's overall schedule (2020-2029 in the October 2020 approval), not a park-specific date.
No cost figure for Power Station Park was found (annual reports give contract values only for streets, Unit 3, Sophie Maxwell, Station A).

Landscape architect identification rests on the 'plural' logo and 2724 17th Street address on the 7.29.21 plan sheets plus CMG's 'Affiliated Landscape Architect: Plural Studio'; no document names the firm in text; the Design for Development credits CMG Landscape Architecture on its open-space figures.
Annual reports 2021-2023 print the design review submittal date as '3.23.20'; the Planning staff memo says March 23, 2021. The memo date is used.

The 2021 annual report lists Power Station Park East as 'Design review approved, 8.3.21' delivered with Block 12; from 2022 it is listed as delivered with Block 8 with a site permit application. The reason for the change is not stated.

Phase 1 application table (Table 5) lists Power Station Park West as moved from DA Phase 2 to Phase 1; the East block does not appear in that change table (presumably already Phase 1) - not confirmed against DA Exhibit M.

BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA) passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary (Resolution No. 21945) describes the proposed Phasing Plan changes to park delivery: now 'Power Station Park East must be provided with Block 12' and 'West must be provided with Block 11'; proposed 'East may be provided with either Block 8 or 12' and 'West ... with either Block 7 or 11'. The final text sent to the Mayor was not read.

Whether the Phase 1 Street Improvement Project was completed: the 2024 annual report expected Q4 2025, and the Port Commission staff memo of Nov 14, 2025 says the developer 'anticipates receiving a Notice of Completion in the first quarter of 2026' (an expected date); no later source confirms completion. The start is given as both April 2023 and June 2023 within the 2024 report; DataSF shows the permit filed 2023-04-03 and issued 2023-06-23.

Area of Power Station Park, by source: about 1.2 acres, two blocks (D4D 4.1); ~1.2-acre (SF Planning); 1.22 acres (DEIR); approximately 1.26 acres (Phase 1 application). The IMP gives 1.92 acres under the combined heading 'Power Station Park and Louisiana Paseo' (the text calls it a 'proposed 1.92-acre central green space' and names the paseo separately, so whether the figure includes the paseo is not stated), and the pre-application slides give '2 acres' for park plus paseo.

records.name: Waterfront Park
records.summary: Planned shoreline park along the site's Bay frontage: the D4D's ~3.6-acre 'Waterfront Open Spaces' (Waterfront Park with the Blue Greenway, The Point, Stack Plaza, Block 9 plazas and Humboldt Street Plaza), which SF Planning summarizes as a ~3-acre waterfront park opening over 1,000 linear feet of shoreline. The Port's November 2025 memo says about 2 acres of the project's open space will be on Port-owned shoreline property leased under L-16662 (66 years, $1/year); its February 2020 memo counted 2.9 Port-owned acres in three pieces (1.6 acres between the Power Station sub-area and the Bay, 1.3 acres along 23rd Street and a sliver under a tenth of an acre), and the two figures are not reconciled. A BCDC permit was issued in July 2021 (no source read shows its number; BCDC's tracker lists amendments numbered 2019.006.01 and 2019.006.02). Delivery is phased (Waterfront Park South before the certificate of occupancy for 3 million sq ft; The Point before 500,000 sq ft; North/West with Block 4); The Point's design review application, submitted Dec 3, 2021, was still under way in the latest annual report (March 2025) and SF Planning's project page lists no approval, and the interim Prequel Park precedes the permanent park: the Port Commission allowed interim improvements on the leased shoreline on Nov 18, 2025 (Resolution 25-70), and BCDC issued Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02 for them on June 26, 2026 (issue date per its application tracker).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- what is left of the shoreline strip once Prequel Park, The Point and Stack Plaza have their own shapes: one piece, south of Block 9 beside Stack Plaza, 390 m2 (0.10 acre). The Design for Development's Waterfront Park is much larger (the SF Planning project page lists 'The ~3-acre waterfront park'; Figure 4.19.1, printed p.99, draws a Waterfront Park Boundary along the shoreline strip it shows), so this shape is a remainder, not the park. It was formed by merging the earlier Waterfront Park trace with both Prequel Park sub-area drawings and cutting the result at Block 9's south edge and Block 4's north edge. The two pieces are the parts of the strip outside Prequel Park's footprint: the permanent waterfront park is read to be built along the shoreline of the interim Prequel Park when that park ends, so that shoreline is Waterfront Park's future ground and is not drawn twice here. Same 15-25 m positional tolerance as this site's other entries.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This reflects Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The Port shoreline premises are Port land under Lease L-16662 (Port Commission memo, Nov 14, 2025); DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, and whether any of them matches this park was not checked.
notes.regulatory_context: The site's shoreline public-access open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label, running along the bay side of Blocks 9 and the Stack, connecting toward Warm Water Cove Park to the south (shown on the same figure, outside the project site boundary).

open_questions: An earlier note that the BCDC permit application 2019.006.00 was 'filed complete June 2, 2020 per ceqanet' could not be verified: the CEQAnet entries (2017112005/2 and /3) show only the DEIR receipt (10/3/2018) and Final EIR receipt (12/11/2019) with BCDC as a reviewing agency. The original BCDC permit document (issued July 2021 per the Port memo) was not found on bcdc.ca.gov; the 2018-2019 DRB and Commission pages now return 404. BCDC's tracker (read 2026-10-12, last updated 2026-09-24) lists two amendments to the project permit: 2019.006.01 (received Apr. 6, 2022, issued Jun. 21, 2022) and 2019.006.02 (the interim park). No source read shows the base permit's number or issue date; the number 2019.006 is inferred from the amendment numbers.

No design review approval for The Point was found after the Dec 3, 2021 submittal; the 2021, 2022 and 2023 annual reports list it as 'Under Review' and the 2024 annual report (March 28, 2025) says 'Design review underway'. SF Planning's project page (read 2026-10-12) lists no Director's memo for The Point and no annual report later than the 2024 report. The earlier expected-completion milestone (2031, from SocketSite's Oct 2020 Phase 2 window) was replaced on 2026-09-29 because that 2020 forecast has not held and the Port's Nov 2025 memo puts open-space delivery behind vertical development expected over the next 10-15 years; no park-specific or Point-specific date exists.

Seawall/shoreline construction: the 2023 annual report (letter of Nov 22, 2024) says that in May 2023 the first phase of shoreline improvements was wrapped up, including deep soil mixing, about 800 linear feet of seawall, steel pipe piles for the future dock, riprap slope protection and the storm drain outfall. It does not say which of that work lies along Waterfront Park, The Point or the Prequel Park band, or when the seawall began. The 2024 annual report says only that the horizontal work was 'substantially complete in May 2023', and Landa (Potrero View, Oct 2025) says 'building the seawall a few years ago'. BCDC's Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.01 (issued Jun. 21, 2022) also covers 'extend seawall' and a 'retrofit of intake structure at Bay Overlook at 23rd Street'.
Area: 3.6 acres (D4D, DA, DEIR) vs ~3 acres and '1,000 linear feet' (SF Planning page only) vs 4.0 acres (IMP); this record's map shape traces only the visible strip. Not reconciled.

No source draws the footprint of Prequel Park or says how it sits against the permanent waterfront park. The Port memo (Nov 2025) says Prequel Park 'will cover approximately 2 acres, of which approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises' (the Port's leased shoreline), and BCDC's Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02 covers 'in-kind interim park improvements and outdoor food and beverage area totaling approximately 57,000- 62,000 square feet until the underlying parcels may be developed for their final authorized uses'. No source read says the whole interim park lies within the future waterfront open space, and the shapes on the map for the two are Pier & Point's own composition.
No construction cost or delivery date for the permanent park; the 3-million-sq-ft trigger is not dated by any source.
Port Commission Feb 25, 2020 minutes: the copy checked is the agenda text; the adoption of Resolution 20-12 is taken from the Nov 2025 memo's recital.
Whether BCDC is listed as a reviewing agency for the EIR on CEQAnet (State Clearinghouse 2017112005) was not re-checked as of 2026-09-29; only BCDC's scoping comment in the Draft EIR is cited.

Since 2026-10-11 The Point, Stack Plaza and Prequel Park have their own records, so the shape on this record is only the remainder of the shoreline strip (about 0.10 acre) and is much smaller than the ~3-acre waterfront park SF Planning describes. The permanent waterfront park is read to be built along the shoreline of the interim Prequel Park when that park ends, which is why only the part beside Stack Plaza outside Prequel Park's footprint is drawn here (the northern piece was dropped on 2026-10-13).

The Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724; its Legistar title lists 'amendments to its Housing Plan, Transportation Plan, and Phasing Plan') was passed on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'; page read 2026-10-14). The phasing in this record is as approved in October 2020 and as reported in the 2024 annual report; whether the amended Phasing Plan changes the waterfront park's triggers was not checked.

Landscape architect of the waterfront park: CMG Landscape Architecture is named on its own project page for the 29-acre Potrero Power Station (2017 to present, client Associate Capital); the page calls The Point 'a new one acre waterfront park', says it includes 'a bay overlook pier that will be built upon an existing footprint of the decommissioned power plant water intake structure', and lists Plural Studio as affiliated landscape architect. The D4D's text names no author and carries no CMG credit; credits printed inside D4D images were not checked.

Area of the waterfront open spaces, by source: Waterfront Open Spaces approximately 3.6 acres (D4D 4.1; DA recital '3.6-acre Waterfront Park'; DEIR 3.6 acres); SF Planning '~3-acre waterfront park' with 'over 1,000 linear feet of shoreline'; IMP 'approximately 4.0-acre waterfront park'. The Point is approximately 0.98 acre (Phase 1 application); Stack Plaza ~0.6 acre (SF Planning, Phase 1 application).

Sea level rise design of the waterfront park: the 2020 Port memo says the shoreline is elevated to accommodate 90 inches of sea level rise plus 42 inches of storm surge, 132 inches above current MHHW, adaptable beyond; the 2025 Port memo refers to a 'projected sea level rise of 66 inches'. The two figures are not reconciled.

records.name: The Point
records.summary: Planned quieter park at the south-east tip of the site, set apart from Block 9's more social uses: natural planted areas, informal discovery play, and casual seating and picnicking, with a Bay overlook on the footprint of a decommissioned power plant intake structure and a section of Blue Greenway for a future connection toward Warm Water Cove, to be completed by others (Design for Development Section 4.20). The Power Station website calls it a place set 'at the tip of the site'.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- the landform was read off satellite imagery to a few metres, and the strip around it comes from earlier approximate drawings (the Draft EIR's Port sub-area figure and the Waterfront Park trace), so treat its edges as indicative to roughly 10-20 m. The Design for Development's Figures 4.16.1 and 4.20.1 draw The Point as a rounded park with a rock edge; this shape does not reproduce that drawing. No source read gives The Point's own acreage, so the area here is only the area of this shape.
notes.digitized_from: Traced by Pier & Point from Esri World Imagery (zoom 20) against a 10 m grid in UTM zone 10N (EPSG:26910): the rounded, rock-edged landform at the south-east tip of the site, east of the Spreckels warehouse, plus the shoreline strip around it that the earlier Waterfront Park and Prequel Park drawings placed there. The Design for Development labels it (2) 'The Point' on Figure 4.16.1 (printed p.93) and gives it Section 4.20 and Figure 4.20.1; the Power Station website describes it as 'set at the tip of the site'.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No Assessor lot of its own: DataSF's active lot 4232010 (401 23rd St, PDR-1-G zoning, 44,309 m2) lies under the Spreckels warehouse and the ground west of it, and about 10% of this shape (356 m2) falls inside it; the rest lies outside every active lot (checked against DataSF Parcels, 2026-10-11).
notes.regulatory_context: Open space (4) in the Design for Development's Waterfront Open Spaces: Section 4.20 'The Point'. The Power Station website's Open Space page says: 'The Point marks the meeting of land, water, and wind at the edge of Power Station. Set at the tip of the site with uninterrupted views of the bay'.

records.name: Humboldt Street Plaza
records.summary: Planned mostly paved flexible-use plaza between Blocks 4 and 9 at the foot of Humboldt Street, giving a car-free connection from Delaware Street to the Blue Greenway and a waterside Bay overlook terrace (D4D 4.24, 4.19.2). A Phase 2 open space due before the first certificate of occupancy for the building representing 3 million sq ft of development; The Port's November 2025 staff memo says the project's open space improvements are tied to completion of vertical development, expected to be phased over the next 10-15 years. No design review or construction has been reported.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this open space directly, shown as a plaza area between Block 4 (north) and Block 9 (south). This polygon is a simplified rectangular approximation of that labeled area, built directly from the mapped corners of Block 4 and Block 9 (see the mapping log) so it shares an exact edge with both -- its accuracy is that of those two blocks' shapes. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St, PPS-MU zoning, recorded 2022-08-30) holds 1,066 m2 of this drawing. It also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza and parts of Prequel Park and Waterfront Park, so Pier & Point reads it as an undivided parent lot; the plaza has no lot of its own and the drawing is kept.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This reflects Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.)
notes.regulatory_context: Humboldt Street Plaza is labelled on the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3, between Block 4 and Block 9 near the site's waterfront edge. D4D section 4.24 says it 'is envisioned as an open and flexible space' and that it 'will provide a car-free pedestrian connection between the terminus of Humboldt Street and the waterfront'. Status 'planned': the October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval (Phase 1 Application, section 5.1, Table 5) lists the plaza as moved from Phase 1 to Phase 2 and says it 'is required to be delivered prior to the City's issuance of the First Certificate of Occupancy for the Building representing 3 million square feet of total development'. That is a delivery trigger, not a date, and no source read gives a design approval, a construction start or an opening for the plaza.

open_questions: No acreage for Humboldt Street Plaza is stated in the D4D, DEIR, IMP, DA recitals, Phase 1 application or annual reports; the geometry is a rectangle between Blocks 4 and 9 without a sourced area.

No design review application, cost, or construction date exists in any source; the plaza is a Phase 2 item behind a 3-million-sq-ft occupancy trigger that no source dates. The interim Prequel Park (mapped by Pier & Point as a Power Station sub-area) shares edges with this plaza; whether the interim park occupies the plaza's footprint is not shown in any scaled drawing reviewed.
BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA, 2026) amends the Phasing Plan; possible changes to this plaza's phase were not checked (draft DA not read).

No designer of Humboldt Street Plaza is named in any source found: in the final D4D, CMG Landscape Architecture appears only as a photo credit on precedent images (Figure 4.24.4 and elsewhere), not as the plaza's designer, and no design review application exists for the plaza.

records.distance_note: The San Francisco Chronicle describes the site as "a block from the massive Dogpatch Power Station redevelopment project, which is transforming 29 acres"; the article names Fifth Space as that project's developer, and we take it to mean the project this site calls the Potrero Power Station. Our own reckoning by street address (not a sourced figure) is closer to two blocks: the parcel is addressed on Michigan St, while the nearest currently-tracked Potrero Power Station parcel, the Sophie Maxwell Building, is addressed at 1212 Maryland St (both addresses per DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn), roughly a block and a half to the north across 24th St by our reading of the street grid.
