positions.who: Supervisor Shamann Walton (District 10, which includes this parcel)
positions.statement: Said he was unaware of the plans for 1215 Michigan St when contacted by the Chronicle. On data centers near residential neighborhoods generally, the Chronicle reports he said the moratorium was a result of the rise in data centers popping up near residential communities across the country, and having seen the "impacts, from polluting the water supply to the noise these facilities bring to the neighborhoods closest to them."

records.summary: A 4-acre industrial parcel at 1215 Michigan St, currently home to crane-rental and heavy-hauling firm Sheedy Drayage, that the San Francisco Chronicle reported (Sept 18, 2026) may become a data center. The article's headline says 160,000 square feet; its text says Nestory Park Capital lists a 160,000-square-foot flagship San Francisco project that would rise on 1.6 acres at an undisclosed location, and does not say that size applies to this 4-acre parcel. The Chronicle reported that no plans for a data center appeared to have been filed with the city as of that report.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL Assessor parcel geometry (not approximate), but the map's grey background layer of land and buildings covers an older, slightly smaller area that stops just north of this parcel, so that background is blank immediately around this shape on the map -- cosmetic only; the parcel's own outline and position are exact. The background layer has not yet been extended. That this is a real Assessor parcel rests on DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn), which lists blklot 4241004 as an active parcel addressed 1215 MICHIGAN; the Chronicle article names the address but does not discuss the parcel.
notes.digitized_from: The real DataSF Assessor parcel for blklot 4241004 (1215 Michigan St, 4.07 acres, zoned PDR-1-G), taken directly from DataSF's open data portal (data.sfgov.org/resource/acdm-wktn.json, dataset 'Parcels - Active and Retired') on 2026-09-21. Stored as a separately drawn shape rather than linked by block/lot only because the parcel sits just south of the area covered by this map's local copy of the Assessor parcel data (which stops at latitude 37.7545; this parcel's northern edge is ~37.7542) -- the polygon itself is the real, unmodified Assessor shape, not hand-traced or approximated. A small blklot 4241003 (~0.25 acres) immediately west, also addressed 1215 Michigan St, is not included: the Chronicle's reporting and the lot_area in DataSF's Secured Property Tax Rolls (dataset wv5m-vpq2, 2025 roll: 177,223 sq ft = 4.07 acres; the Parcels dataset itself has no area field, and the lot's drawn outline measures about 4.1 acres) both point to 4241004 as 'the' 4-acre parcel in question.

records.name: Mission Creek Park
records.summary: A waterfront park along Mission Creek in Mission Bay (SF Rec & Park lists it as Mission Creek Park (North and South), bordered by Berry Street to the north and west and Channel Street to the south, ending at 3rd Street), labeled P2 and P3 -- and, for its amphitheater feature, P1 -- on OCII's current Mission Bay South open-space page; its P1 segment was among the first Mission Bay parks to open (2002, per SF Rec & Park's Workshop 3 timeline). The San Francisco Recreation and Park Department assumed management and maintenance of the park on July 1, 2023. The 'complete' status describes the built park; the P8 land and the not-yet-built part of P2 inside the mapped shape are the planned Mission Creek Park South Extension, which Rec and Park's page lists as 'Construction begins, Late 2026 / Early 2027' (an expected date). No source checked gives the surrounding park landscaping's own original construction or opening date, as distinct from the separately dated Mission Creek Park Pavilion within it (see that record).

notes.accuracy_caveat: The status covers the built park only -- 'complete' describes the built Mission Creek Park (P1, P3 and the Huffaker Park part of P2). The P8 land and the part of P2 not yet built, which this shape also includes, belong to the Mission Creek Park South Extension (Parcels 2 and 8): SF Rec & Park's project page lists 'Construction begins, Late 2026 / Early 2027' and 'Open to the Public, TBD' for it. Those are expected dates; no source read says construction has started. See the separate P2 and P8 records, which show that land as existing and planned. HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (matches SF Rec & Park's own facility listing). Other OSM ways (579664205 further east, and 27369705) may cover parts of this same park; they are not cited and had not been checked as of September 2026; this feature uses the single most detailed, currently-tagged way covering the park's main extent along Mission Creek's south bank. A later revision could merge the full multi-segment shoreline extent. Updated 2026-09-20: now a MultiPolygon that also includes P1, P2 and P8's geometry (P1 a separate segment further northeast along the creek; P2/P8 real scraps of land not contiguous with this record's original OSM shape; no source read says which bank of the creek each piece is on). Each sub-piece keeps its own sourcing/confidence as documented in its own original record (P1, P2, P8) -- this union does not upgrade their confidence to this record's own 'HIGH CONFIDENCE, real OSM' rating. Pier & Point reads lot 3810006 (16,093 m2, active, Channel St 202) as covering both P1 and the already built Huffaker Park part of P2, and lot 8710002 (16,398 m2, active, recorded 1999-09-21) as covering the part of P2 not yet constructed and P5 (which has no shape of its own on this map). Lot 3810006 overlaps this record by 13,647 m2 and lot 8710002 by 7,854 m2; the shape here (an OpenStreetMap park outline unioned with P1, P2 and P8) is kept.

open_questions: The map shows one status, 'complete', for the whole mapped shape, but about 43% of its area is the P2 and P8 land (14,157 m2 and 10,559 m2 of 57,038 m2), where part of P2 is the built Huffaker Park and the rest, with P8, is the planned Mission Creek Park South Extension. The status describes the built park; no source read says construction of the extension has started.

The 2019-09 and 2022-10 milestones are both for the P3 extension specifically (a 1.2-1.65-acre addition extending the park toward China Basin Park; Potrero View puts the existing Mission Creek Park west of Fourth Street and does not say the extension is), not the original park. The Potrero View source's fall-2021 target (after a COVID-19 pause) did not hold -- the Landscape Performance Series case study gives an actual completion date of October 2022, about a year later.

No source checked gives Mission Creek Park's own original construction/opening date; the Mission Creek Park Pavilion within it has a separately sourced 2003 completion (see the Mission Creek Park Pavilion record), but that doesn't establish when the surrounding park landscaping itself opened -- background reading (a Southeast Waterfront community history page, and a landscape-architecture magazine mention of a 2004-dated EDAW site-plan rendering seen only in a search-result summary, not confirmed against the actual article text) suggested an early-2000s completion but nothing specific enough to cite as a fact.

OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation (slide 5, a plan to be presented for approval in October to December 2023) says RPD "will manage NP1-NP5; P1, P2 Parking Lot Landscaping, P3, P5, P6, P10, P11/11A, P16, P17 & P26 (Plus P2/P8, P7, P9, P12, P13, P15 and P27 when built)", so P2/P8 are listed among the parcels to be managed 'when built' (i.e., not yet complete as of Sept 2023); the presentation does not say that any parcel was already RPD-managed -- the union of this shape with P2 and P8 on 2026-09-20 (About this shape) is consistent with those specific pieces being a later, smaller addition rather than part of the original park; not used to date the union since the two documents describe different things (a funding/management list vs. a geometry merge).

OCII's plan-label usage for this park is inconsistent across documents over time: the Nov 2024 CAC deck's slide 3 is titled 'MISSION CREEK PARK (P3)' while its slide 2 map labels P1, P2 & P8 and P3 separately; the current sfocii.org open-space page splits it into P1 (amphitheater), P2 and P3; and a 2015 Successor Agency LRPMP (cited on Pier & Point's neighboring P7/P8/P9 records) uses P2, P7, P8 and P9 for nearby, separately tracked open-space parcels along the same creek. Not reconciled here.

records.name: Mission Bay Commons
records.summary: A roughly two-acre lawn and green space at 450 Mission Bay Boulevard South in Mission Bay (per SF Rec & Park's facility page), part of the city's Mission Bay Parks system; the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department assumed management and maintenance on July 1, 2023 (SF Rec & Park). OCII's November 14, 2024 timeline gives opening years for the eastern Commons segments (P16 in 2010, P17 in 2002), but which of the two is this lawn is not confirmed, so no opening date is stated for it.

notes.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon tagged with the Mission Bay Parks system's own missionbayparks.com URL for this facility. Covers only this one mapped lot (roughly the Mission Bay Blvd. lawn/plaza between the Radiance and Nektar/Bayer buildings); the wider Mission Bay Commons interim-use area further west (Spark Social SF, Stagecoach Greens, the soccer field) is a separate, still-interim installation tracked as its own record below (Parklab Gardens & Mission Bay Commons interim area) pending the Future Parks Project. These are expected dates, not events, and the sources differ: SF Rec & Park's project page gives an estimated schedule of design mid-2026, construction beginning late 2028 and opening to the public early 2030, yet the same page says the remaining parks 'are anticipated to be complete by 2028'; OCII's Nov 14, 2024 CAC update lists 'Transfer to SF Rec Park and Park (end of 2028, upon completion)'. No source reconciles the 2028 and early-2030 completion dates.

open_questions: Dated events found: SF Rec & Park's July 1, 2023 assumption of management from OCII (a management transfer, not a construction-completion date, so not used as a completion milestone), and the opening years in OCII's November 14, 2024 timeline (P16 in 2010, P17 in 2002; see the milestone). Which of P16 and P17 is this lawn is not confirmed, so no opening date is stated for the lawn itself.

As of 2026-09-22, OCII's own Nov 2024 CAC map places labels P16 and P17 specifically at the east end of the Mission Bay Commons strip, matching this record's own mapped lawn -- resolving which OCII labels apply here, versus the P11/P12/P13/P15 labels used for the separate, still-interim area further west (the Mission Bay Commons, Parcels P12, P13 and P15 record). The only dated source found (a Nov 2011 EPA press release) names just P16, not P17, and says the park was "recently completed" rather than giving a construction date or a dedication date -- so the milestone above is deliberately narrower than that OCII grouping might suggest.

The Future Parks Project that will rebuild the interim western parcels has expected dates that differ: SF Rec & Park's project page gives construction beginning late 2028 and opening to the public early 2030, yet also says the remaining parks 'are anticipated to be complete by 2028', and OCII's November 14, 2024 update lists 'Transfer to SF Rec Park and Park (end of 2028, upon completion)'. All three are expected dates, not events.

The EPA release (2011-11-04) is a media advisory for a tour, names P16 only and has no location; the opening years (P16 2010, P17 2002) come from slide 9 of OCII's Nov 14, 2024 deck, whose timeline lists them, and the location of P16 and P17 comes from that deck's legend. This record's mapped shape leaves the P-number unconfirmed, so the milestone is stated about the eastern Commons segments, not this exact lawn.

records.name: Bayfront Park
records.summary: A 5.4-acre waterfront park at 16th Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, between Chase Center and San Francisco Bay, developed by the Mission Bay Development Group in partnership with the Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure and to be owned and maintained by the Port of San Francisco, with open lawns, a stretch of the Bay Trail, multiple plazas, and shade structures and other site furnishings made from reclaimed Bay Bridge steel; it had its public grand-opening celebration on October 22, 2024.

The way carries a website tag (sfport.com/bayfrontpark) and operator:wikidata=Q3398575 (the operator's Wikidata item, not the park's); it has no operator name tag or Wikidata tag of its own, so the confidence judgement is ours. Opened Oct 22, 2024 (5.4 acres at 16th St and Terry A. Francois Blvd, opposite Chase Center). Which plan parcels it occupies is not settled: Lotus Water's page calls it 'P-22'; that it also occupies P21 is not stated by any cited source (SF.gov notes a previously completed portion of Bayfront Park to the north).

October 22, 2024 is the public grand-opening celebration date; a separate physical-construction-completion date (permit final, certificate of occupancy) was not found in any source checked.

The sources also give different reasons for the closure: Urban Life Signs says the transfer of redeveloped land to the city; SFist cites Board of Supervisors approval and, in the developer's statement, completing and getting the city's acceptance of Long Bridge and China Basin streets. Neither confirms 2015 versus early 2016; 2015 is used here as the more specific of the two estimates but is flagged as approximate.

The lot is condominium-mapped: 614 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8702011 and 613 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Update 2026-10-12, cost: $1.52 billion is the contractor DPR's stated project value, and the only total in a readable source that describes the finished hospital. The UC Regents' September 2008 presentation (slide 27) shows a $1.686 billion project cost breakdown (construction $1,094.9 million; equipment and furnishings $239 million; special items and capitalized interest $174.6 million; contingency $54.7 million; design fees $70 million; project management $30 million; surveys, tests, plans and specifications $22.8 million) and slide 28 the same total as funding sources. The difference between a contractor's project value and a 2008 approved budget is not reconciled, and UCSF's own November 2014 release could not be read (access refused). The opening date of February 1, 2015 is from DPR's project page.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate; the west edge is idealized to a straight line (2 points instead of the OSM trace's 3, dropping a sub-meter digitizing jog), not a surveyed change. open_questions: When was the Community Center Garage built, and is it a multi-level structure? UCSF's parking page (undated) offers parking at 1625 Owens St, and the city's address point is inside the outline, but no source read dates its construction or opening. A 2021 DBI permit record on the lot lists an existing public parking garage of 8 stories (see below).

STRUCTURE QUESTION: the May 2000 Regents item describes an interim parking lot beside the community center, to be replaced by a parking structure in a later phase. In UCSF's June 12, 2025 Mission Bay CAC figure (an image) the label 'COMMUNITY CENTER GARAGE (21A)' sits beside a flat, building-less parcel with a parking symbol, where it was viewed by eye, not as text. The map label alone does not settle whether a structure stands there. DBI permit 202111081961 (filed 2021-11-08, 1625 Owens St, block 8709 lot 011) records "existing_use": "prkng garage/public" and "number_of_existing_stories": "8", which indicates a multi-story public parking garage, but its description is of telecommunications equipment, not of the garage, and no source read gives a construction date. The geometry file's rooftop-deck reading comes from the project's own satellite review and is not corroborated by a document.

The Assessor's 2022 roll has one parcel (8709011, listed '1675 1625 OWENS') for the community center and the garage together, with no year built; a DBI permit search on block 8709 lot 011 returned two permits: a 2019 street-space permit (M1170767) and permit 202111081961 (filed 2021-11-08), an alteration to an existing T-Mobile telecommunications facility whose record lists the existing use as "prkng garage/public" with 8 existing stories. Neither is a new-construction permit for a garage, so no construction permit or date was found.
Architect, builder, space count and operator are not found. UCSF's Parking and Transportation pages were not opened (blocked).
The garage is distinct from the 1670 Owens garage (DBI permit 200801243180, 823 spaces), which has its own record.
No UC Regents capital item for a community-center garage was located.

Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history. The same September 2008 Regents presentation (used for Byers Hall, Genentech Hall, Rock Hall and Rutter Center) includes one more photo on its "Architectural Context" slide labeled only "Housing," showing what looks like more than one building together; it wasn't used here because it can't be confidently attributed to this specific one.

The November 2002 Regents item covers the whole Block 20 project (one tower plus three mid-rise buildings) rather than naming this building individually; identification of this record as one of the three mid-rise buildings follows from its own facts entry, not a direct name match in the Regents record.

Searched for a cost figure specific to this building alone (versus the whole four-building Block 20 project). The only figure found anywhere is the November 2002 Regents item's own $112,816,000 project budget, which the Regents item itself states as a whole-project total covering Hearst Tower and all three mid-rise buildings together -- no source breaks it down per building, so no record-scope figure is added here; a per-project figure belongs in a site- or phase-scope table, not this record's own costs.

As of 2026-09-29, no source read states when the building actually opened; the 2005 opening shown earlier rested only on a housing page that could not be checked and on Langan, which gives no date. The milestone now carries the October 2005 full occupancy anticipated by the November 2002 Regents item, marked expected. 'Student and faculty' was changed to 'student, postdoctoral scholar and family' housing because Langan and the Regents item say so and no readable source mentions faculty.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the October 2005 'full occupancy anticipated' milestone was shown as an expected completion although its date passed two decades ago and no source confirms it. The completion milestone now rests on SFGate's May 31, 2009 report that the campus had four residential buildings, which bounds the opening but does not date it; the actual opening date is still unconfirmed (a July 2005 UCSF news item, 'Community Center, Housing Complex Nearly Complete', could not be read). The approval milestone no longer names individual buildings, because the Regents item names none.

Architect not shown: arcCA (originally published 4th quarter 2006) says "A 760-bed student apartment complex, by SOM with Fisher Friedman"; Langan's project page for the same complex lists "Architect Verde Design, Inc." The sources may describe different roles, but neither says so, so no architect is stated here.

Size and capacity of the four-building complex: the building names (Hearst Tower and the North, West and South buildings) are UCSF's housing page's, which could not be read on 2026-10-12. Langan: "four separate buildings totaling 298,800 SF to house more than 750 UCSF students, postdoctoral scholars, and their families"; the November 13, 2002 Regents item planned "717 students and postdoctoral scholars and the family of one manager" and "298,800 residential asf"; arcCA (2006) calls it "A 760-bed student apartment complex". The capacity and the measure behind 298,800 differ between sources and none is chosen here.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- OpenStreetMap building footprint (crowd-mapped, not an official survey), not a hand trace or plan estimate. Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). open_questions: No source confirms the garage's actual completion date; the March 2004 start and July 2005 completion are the November 2003 Regents item's projected schedule, stated in the 2003-11 milestone above, not a completion announcement. A UC construction schedule commonly slips, so no completion date is shown.

The 2003 Regents item describes a nine-level, 822-space structure; this record's map data cites OpenStreetMap tagging of 8 levels -- not reconciled here, since OpenStreetMap levels and the Regents' 'nine levels (including a half level at the top)' description are plausibly the same building described two ways. The building's own general contractor (Overaa, added 2026-09-22) separately gives 882 stalls -- likely the as-built figure versus the Regents' pre-construction budget estimate, but not reconciled here either.
Exact capacity today (after any reconfiguration) is not confirmed by any source found, per this record's map notes.

Overaa Construction's own project page for this building, which gives no dates, is the only source read that names a general contractor; whether Overaa built the original structure, which the 2003 Regents item projected for 2004 to 2005, is not confirmed by any dated source.

As of 2026-09-29: the earlier '2021 facade replacement' was wrong: Facades+ (March 15, 2021) gives the completion date as January 2020 and says the channel-glass facade was removed in 2015; The Architect's Newspaper article cited before could not be read. The November 2003 Regents item is a request for approval; the committee minutes recording the vote were not found (no 2003 minutes page could be located online).

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the March 2004 construction start and July 2005 completion projected in the November 2003 Regents item were shown as expected milestones (the completion with status complete), two decades past and unconfirmed. Both were removed; the projection is now stated in the budget-item milestone, and the earliest sourced evidence that the garage stood is Facades+'s report that its original facade was removed in 2015. The actual construction start and completion dates are still unknown.

Update 2026-10-12: no source that could be read dates the garage's completion or its facade work. Facades+ (March 15, 2021), cited earlier for the original channel-glass facade being removed in 2015 and the new facade being completed in "January 2020", refused access (Cloudflare) on every attempt, as did The Architect's Newspaper and Architizer coverage of the facade, so those two dates were taken off the timeline and are not confirmed. The readable sources are Hohbach-Lewin (June 9, 2020, calls the facade "new", no date), Overaa Construction (describes the finished garage, no year) and the November 2003 Regents item (a projection only). The garage is shown with no completion date.

Floor area of the garage: the November 2003 Regents item planned 253,993 gsf (249,140 gsf parking plus 4,853 gsf shelled retail space); Overaa Construction's project page gives 256,276 SF; the two figures are not reconciled.

open_questions: Correction (2026-09-29): 1670 Owens is on the Assessor secured roll as parcel 8709022 (Garages (Commercial), year built 2010, 7 stories, with a College/University exemption in the 2025 roll), so an Assessor parcel exists; the DBI permit for the garage (200801243180) was filed on block 8709 lot 009 and is complete (2010-01-29). No UCSF announcement or Regents document dating this specific garage was found; the earlier note that the year built comes only from PropertyShark and that UCSF land is not on the secured roll no longer holds for this parcel.

Searched UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings agenda items for an Owens Street parking structure matching this garage's 823 spaces and found none that names 1670 Owens. The Regents' November 2003 item for the separate Mission Bay Building 23B Parking Structure (Block 23) describes "a nine-level parking structure containing 822 parking spaces in Phase 1 with another 52 surface spaces, for a total of 874 spaces" and 253,993 gsf, statistics close to this garage's; no source read links that item to 1670 Owens, so the two are not tied together here. WRNS Studio's "Mission Bay Parking Structure" project page ("seven-story, 1,420-space parking structure", completion 2009, "Located next to the Chase Center and UCSF") was considered but not used: its capacity and floor count do not match this garage's, and the page gives no street address. It is left unlinked rather than guessed.
Capacity: DBI's permit description says 823 spaces (now recorded as a fact); parking aggregators' ~820 figure agrees.
No architect or design-build team was identified for this specific address.

Another candidate was checked and ruled out (2026-09-22). UCSF's William J. Rutter Community Center (Block 21B, architect Ricardo Legorreta with MBT/Perkins+Will, per a May 2000 Regents design-approval item and Forell/Elsesser's own project page) has its own, separately-addressed parking garage -- confirmed via UCSF-affiliated contact pages and parking directories to be at 1625 Owens St, not this record's 1670 Owens St. These are two distinct structures a few hundred feet apart; the Rutter Center's own garage material does not apply to this record.

open_questions: Apartment-listing aggregators (Apartments.com, Redfin, ApartmentHomeLiving, among others) give 2014 as this block's construction year, but DataSF Assessor records and the project architect's own project page both give 2016; not resolved which reflects actual first occupancy versus an earlier leasing target that slipped.

Contemporaneous press (SFGate, CBS News San Francisco) reported a 5-alarm fire on March 11, 2014 that destroyed an under-construction MB360 building (CBS News, May 7, 2014: "a 172-unit building was being built as part of the MB360 development project ... The unfinished building was destroyed and demolished in the days following the massive blaze"); no source read says the building was rebuilt; no source found specifies which of the two street addresses (701 China Basin St, this record, vs. 1200 4th St) was the one destroyed, so it is not asserted here which block the fire affected.
Precise month of this block's actual completion/first occupancy is not sourced beyond the bare Assessor year.
Developer of record beyond BRE Properties/Essex Property Trust, and any subsequent sale history: not yet researched.

The Registry's own article (already cited above) reports that BRE Properties "expects total development cost of $227 million, or $630,000 a unit" (an expected figure, May 2013, not a final cost) -- but that figure covers the whole 360-unit MB360 development, which the architect's page describes as two blocks (this record's 701 China Basin St block plus the separate 1200 4th St block) as one project, not this 188-unit block alone. No block-specific figure was found, so no record-scope figure is added here.

The Apartments.com listing could not be checked on 2026-09-29; an archived copy exists at web.archive.org/web/20211031174227/https://www.apartments.com/mb360-san-francisco-ca/bzdysc8/ (not checked). The 701 China Basin St address is confirmed by the Assessor and OpenStreetMap.

Unit count: the Assessor roll gives 188 units for 701 China Basin St. The architect's project page cited here (Ignition Architecture, which designed two of the five buildings on Block 5) lists "Units 362 total; Block 5 = 170 / ...; Block 11 = 190 / ..." (its own per-block figures add to 360, not 362) and no street addresses; the page of the project's other architect, MVE + Partners, could not be read on 2026-10-12. A 2014 CurbedSF report quoted by LocalWiki gives 172 units for the destroyed building and 188 for the other, which is not tied here to a street address.

records.name: J. David Gladstone Institutes
records.summary: The J. David Gladstone Institutes' Mission Bay headquarters at 1650 Owens Street: a six-story, roughly 200,000-sq-ft biomedical research building for this independent nonprofit research organization (in academic partnership with UCSF), completed in 2004. The expansion of the six-story building from 200,000 to 275,000 sq ft (about 75,000 sq ft added, around $160 million) was announced in February 2023, with construction then expected to start in late 2024 and finish by 2026; whether it was built is not confirmed. In March 2026 Gladstone announced more than 105,000 sq ft of future lab space in a new building at 1450 Owens Street, opening in early 2027.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8709008 (5,570 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8709008)); 100% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 58% of the lot. The announced expansion (see notes) is not confirmed complete and is not reflected in the status.

records.name: Mission Creek Park Pavilion
records.summary: A San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department building at 290 Channel St within Mission Creek Park, with floor-to-ceiling windows and patios overlooking Mission Creek (SF Rec & Park: "Mission Creek Pavilion and patios, featuring floor-to-ceiling windows with great views of Mission Creek"), built as a space for a café. names: Mission Bay Education Center and Dental Clinics
records.summary: Two buildings tracked as one record, their mapped footprints sharing DataSF Building Footprints id SF3940003: 499 Illinois Street (the southern footprint), a 6-story biotechnology building (its structural engineer describes a 500,000 sq ft center in two buildings) completed 2008 and owned by Alexandria (SF Standard: "long-time landlord Alexandria Properties") until UCSF bought it; and 409 Illinois Street (the northern footprint), which SF Standard says was bought from the same landlord together with 499 Illinois St for $767,000,000 (closing on December 17, 2025) and which UCSF plans to renovate into a new School of Dentistry and a shared education center for students in dentistry, medicine, nursing, pharmacy and physical therapy (the university's project title is Mission Bay Education Center and Dental Clinics). UC filed a Notice of Exemption on May 7, 2026 for an "Advanced Work Phase" of site preparation, and American School & University (September 8, 2026) says "Early construction activities are underway". That magazine reports a completion date targeted for late 2029; SF Standard reports the building is expected to be ready for occupants in the first quarter of 2029. The City's 2006 building permit #200607186938 lists both 409 and 499 Illinois St and shows status "complete" with a completed date of 2009-04-06 (a permit closure date; the permit does not say what stands at 409 today). SF Standard says 409 "will get a 'gut remodel,'" while "only minor work is needed at the other building"; no source read dates the start of the main renovation. The record's status, complete, rests on the 2008 completion of 499 and the 2009 permit closure for both addresses; the 409 renovation is not complete, and the "under construction" milestone below is an expected one that rests on the early work only. UCSF's Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St is a separate record, across Illinois St.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 3940003 (15,223 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 3 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 3940003 and 2 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the two surveyed building footprints (DataSF Building Footprints, mblr SF3940003); 98% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 55% of the lot. The lot also takes in the courtyard and yard between the two buildings and a strip of the neighbouring parks P23 and P24; those two park outlines were trimmed back to this lot's edge on the same date, so the records no longer overlap.

open_questions: This record combines two footprints that share one DataSF Building Footprints id (SF3940003): 499 Illinois St (south) and 409 Illinois St (north). It was formerly named '490/499 Illinois Street' and also carried UCSF's Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St, which is the building across Illinois St on block 33 and now has its own record (corrected 2026-10-10).
Exact month/day of the 2008 completion of 499 Illinois St is not sourced, only the year.

The 2006 construction permit's own block/lot for 499 Illinois St (block 3940, lot 001) differs from the lots the Assessor now uses (lot 3940004, addressed 499 Illinois St, and lot 3940005, addressed 409 to 499 Illinois St). DataSF shows lot 3940001 as retired, with a recorded drop date of 2009-06-04, so the permit used a lot that has since been dropped; the address, biotechnical/medical-research-facility description, 6 stories, and $90M cost all line up with this parcel, so this is treated as the same building under a later lot number, not a different building. The permit's own completion sign-off (2009-04-06) also runs slightly later than the Assessor's 2008 year, which may reflect a lag between substantial completion and permit closeout.

2026-09-28: exact month/day for 409 Illinois St's 2026 renovation start, and the completion date within 2029, are not given by any source found: American School & University magazine (2026-09-08) says 'a completion date targeted for late 2029', while SF Standard (2025-12-17) says construction 'is expected to take about three years and be ready for occupants in the first quarter of 2029'. No project cost is shown because the one source is inconsistent with itself: Construction Dive (published September 1, 2026) says in its headline and text that the project "will cost approximately $278 million, per a prequalification notice on the project from the university", while the page's own project box lists "Value: $287 million". Neither is a contract amount, and the source does not say whether either covers construction alone or the whole project. No source read gives an SF Planning case number for this renovation; CEQAnet's notices list the University of California as the agency, and no source read says whether local planning review applies. DataSF Parcels, read 2026-10-11, lists three active lots on block 3940 with Illinois St addresses: lot 3940003 (409 Illinois St), lot 3940004 (499 Illinois St) and lot 3940005 (409 to 499 Illinois St), all with the same outline and all recorded as added on 2009-06-04. Lot 3940001, which the 2006 permit used, is retired. No source read says which lot the Assessor treats as 499 Illinois St's own or why three active lots share one outline.

No source read says who developed 499 Illinois St. SF Standard (2025-12-17) says UCSF's clinics, labs and offices leased space at 499 Illinois 'for more than a decade' and occupied 90% of the building before buying it.

Size of 409 and 499 Illinois St: 499 Illinois St has six stories per its 2006 DBI permit (its structural engineer, SGH, describes two five-story buildings over two levels of parking). SGH describes a 500,000 sq ft center in two buildings; SF Standard (2025) says 409 and 499 together add up to 470,000 sq ft; UC's own December 2025 acquisition filing gives about 525,421 rentable sq ft for 409 and 499 combined, on 3.6 acres with a 587-space shared garage. 409 Illinois St's renovation into the School of Dentistry / Interprofessional Education Center is 261,117 gross sq ft.

Pier & Point's outline is a small triangular wedge of about 1,029 m2 between the I-280 ramp and Owens St, about 86% inside that Assessor lot, drawn by hand rather than taken from the lot's boundary. OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P27' among the parcels Rec and Park will manage "when built"; no source read says it has been built, and in USDA NAIP imagery viewed 2026-09-29 the ground is a strip of dry grass and bare ground.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- an outline drawn by hand, traced as the leftover ground between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes; not a surveyed footprint or a parcel line. About 86% of it lies inside Assessor lot 8723002, the lot OCII's Long-Range Property Management Plan names for parcel P27, but it covers only 61% of that lot (1,029 m2 of 1,457 m2), so the lot's own lines are not used. Its west side is cut along the continuation of the curved west edge of the Assessor lot to its north (The Exchange on 16th), because the rest of the earlier shape lay over I-280 ramp lanes; that edge is an extension of the lot line, not a traced boundary. Shown as planned: no source read says the parcel has been built.
notes.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and neighbouring mapped shapes near the UCSF Medical Center campus, picked by hand by Pier & Point from a numbered map of such leftover pieces, not taken from a surveyed parcel. The chosen piece was then cut further by hand: it forks into two thin parallel strips (~13-21m wide, running north alongside a building courtyard) above a wider single base (up to 46m wide); the base was kept and both forks were dropped.

records.name: Mariposa Park
names: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P26
records.summary: Mariposa Park, a park on the north side of Mariposa Street between Owens and 4th Streets, which a photo caption on OCII's open-space page labels 'P26 Mariposa Park'. Its outline is the union of Assessor lots 8723003, 8723004 and 8723006, three of the four lots OCII's Long-Range Property Management Plan names for parcel P26 (the plan also lists part of lot 8723007, which the outline leaves out). An undated Rec and Park page says the park includes a playground, picnic area, trellis area and lawn and that, as of July 1, 2023, the department will assume its management and maintenance. No source read gives an opening date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is the union of Assessor lots 8723003, 8723004 and 8723006 (8,217 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lots and can sit a little off the park's own edge. OCII's Long-Range Property Management Plan (Attachment A, row 32) lists parcel P26 on lots 8723-003, 004, 006 and 007(p); this outline leaves out the part of lot 8723007 the plan lists, because the plan does not say which part. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the open ground left between street centerlines and neighbouring mapped shapes (hand-picked, not a surveyed parcel); 70% of that outline lies inside the lots and it covered 100% of them. That earlier outline also took in the parking lot to the north, which is part of lot 8723008 and is no longer in this record.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 8723003, 8723004 and 8723006 (mapped 2001-03-20, 2003-02-05; active), joined into one outline; the earlier outline came from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and neighbouring mapped shapes near the UCSF Medical Center campus. Of the separate pieces this left, Pier & Point picked by hand the one showing an oval running track and central field (clearly visible on satellite imagery) as its real extent (it was then labelled P27); not taken from a surveyed parcel.

changes.text: OCII's plan lists Park P26 on lots 8723-003, 004, 006 and 007(p), on the north side of Mariposa between Owens and 4th Streets, and Park P27 on lot 8723-002, at the northwest corner of Owens and Mariposa Streets. The 2000 permit's own block/lot references (spanning several small blocks in the 3839-3851 range, an older pre-redevelopment block grid) differ from the Assessor's current parcel 8721011; the address (550 Terry A. Francois Blvd), six-story office description, and 2002-09-13 permit-completion date (matching the Assessor's 2002 year exactly) line up with this parcel, so this is treated as Mission Bay's redevelopment-era block renumbering, not a different building.

The building's developer/architect (reported elsewhere as Studios Architecture) was not independently confirmed by any source read as of 2026-09-21 -- left out of this record rather than repeated unsourced.

OpenAI's deal at 550 Terry A. Francois Blvd: The San Francisco Standard (2024-09-20) says OpenAI "just finalized a lease for 350,000 square feet"; Hoodline (2024-09-20) calls it a lease of 315,000 square feet; The Real Deal (2024-09-23) headlines "OpenAI subleases 350K sf building" yet says in its text that OpenAI "plans to occupy a 315,000-square-foot building" and that terms of the deal with owner DivcoWest were not disclosed. Whether this is a lease from the owner or a sublease, and whether the size is 315,000 or 350,000 sq ft, is not settled by these sources; REBusiness (2022-05-25) gives the building as 320,000 sq ft. No lease record was read.

records.name: 1180 Fourth Street
records.summary: A 150-unit affordable apartment building at 1180 Fourth Street in Mission Bay South for low-income families, 50 of them formerly homeless, built for Mercy Housing California (the client Mithun names, and the organization that announced the completion in December 2014) and designed by Mithun (formerly WRT/Solomon E.T.C.), with Kennerly Architecture and Planning as associate design architect. DataSF's Assessor tax roll records the parcel's construction year as 2015, and Mercy Housing held its official opening celebration on May 6, 2015.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8711501 (6,026 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 4 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8711501 and 3 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8711014)); 95% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 72% of the lot.

records.name: Rich Sorro Commons
records.summary: Rich Sorro Commons is a 100-unit affordable housing building at 150 Berry St in Mission Bay for families and people living with HIV/AIDS, with a project page on Mission Housing's website (the organisation calls itself 'the community's affordable housing developer since 1971'; the page does not say in so many words that it developed this building). That page states the building opened in July 2002, the first affordable family housing development in Mission Bay. The page and DBI's permit give 100 units; the Assessor's roll for the residential lot records 101.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is the union of Assessor lots 8706264 and 8706003 (6,453 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8706264)); 95% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 69% of the lot. names: UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center
records.summary: UCSF's June 2025 presentation to the Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee lists Block 18C among its undeveloped parcels remaining, with open space as the long-term use and a childcare center as the near-term use. That matches this record's status of existing, not yet redeveloped: a childcare center is listed on the block, on ground UCSF still counts as undeveloped. Bright Horizons lists the UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center at 727 Nelson Rising Lane (undated page), a city business registration (registered 2024-01-01, not an opening date) exists for that address, and the city's address point for it falls inside this outline; no source read says a building stands here or when it opened.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE BOUNDARY -- traced as the leftover open ground between the mapped street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, rather than from a specific real parcel or building-footprint source; the pieces making up this shape were chosen and combined by hand. The small smoothing step used to bridge two internal walkway gaps may slightly overstate area at those two seams. IDENTITY: this shape is identified as the UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center by four sources together: (1) Bright Horizons' own centre page names 'UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center' at 727 Nelson Rising Lane; (2) DataSF Registered Business Locations lists 'Ucsf Child Care At Mission Bay', owned by Bright Horizons, at 727 Nelson Rising Ln (certificate 0941054); (3) the City's address point for 727 Nelson Rising Ln (DataSF Addresses, address ID 743045, at -122.39330278, 37.76944026) falls inside this shape, about 2.7 m from its edge, and the nearest other mapped shape (Block 15B) is about 20 m away; (4) UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation gives Block 18C's near-term use as 'Childcare Center'. Limits: the address point is a frontage point, not a building footprint, so it places the centre in this block, not this exact outline; 727 Nelson Rising Ln also carries other business registrations (a UCSF shuttle fuelling business), so the address is not exclusive to this building; and no source gives an opening date (the business registration's 2024-01-01 location start is a registration date, not an opening). Marked 'existing' rather than 'complete' because the UCSF map treats this as an interim use ahead of a long-term 'Open Space' redesignation, not a finished build-out.

records.name: Mission Bay South Block 22 (park)
records.summary: A landscaped lawn with trees on Mission Bay South's plan Block 22; not a formally named park in any source checked. Pier & Point's own satellite review found no building footprint on the site, and a September 2026 on-site visit by Pier & Point confirmed it is already a completed small park rather than still-planned open space, correcting an earlier satellite-only assessment. No source read confirms a name or date for it; UCSF's June 2025 presentation map labels a park 'KORET QUAD (22)' on its North Campus, but whether that is this block is unconfirmed (see open questions).

notes.accuracy_caveat: PARTIALLY REAL -- the outer boundary is a real polygonized city block from real street geometry, not hand-traced, except the south-west corner: the source outline cut that corner with a diagonal about 63 m long, and it is squared off here by extending the south and west edges until they meet (about 992 m2 added), because the OCII Land Use Map (December 2019) draws the block as a rectangle. The added corner point is a construction, not a surveyed point. No internal A/B split needed (this label is a single block). A check against DataSF's Assessor parcels and building footprints found no building footprint on the site and traced the dominant underlying parcel to a retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder (parcel 8799TBA3, dropped 2005) plus scattered UCSF campus parcel fragments; that is consistent with open, non-built land but does not show when the current landscaping was built.
notes.digitized_from: Real block boundary: the city block outlined by DataSF's official street centerlines, trimmed back to allow for the full street width. The south-west corner is completed by extending the block's south and west edges until they meet (see the accuracy note).

records.summary: P8 is one of two parcels (P2 and P8) of the planned Mission Creek Park South Extension, which San Francisco Recreation and Parks says OCII and the Mission Bay Development Group are responsible for developing; the department's page gives construction as starting late 2026 or early 2027 and the opening date as to be determined.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real turf/median extent per Esri satellite imagery and a hand-drawn scheme by Pier & Point (traced as the leftover ground bounded by streets and the creek, not surveyed). The three freeway-median strips and the strip beside the site of the proposed Pump Station No. 4 (the schematic design calls that pump station 'proposed'; no source read says it has been built) are deliberately kept as separate polygons in a MultiPolygon (they are physically separated by pavement/ramp lanes, not one contiguous parcel). Overlaps the already-tracked real 'Mission Creek Park' polygon for part of its northeast extent -- not reconciled with it yet, per Pier & Point's own framing that Mission Creek Park will eventually evolve to encompass P1+P2+P8. Pier & Point chose to keep this drawing and cite the Assessor lots under it. Active lots 3809006 (164 m2, 150 m2 inside this drawing) and 3809002 (6,082 m2, 4,104 m2 inside it) are read as P8's lots, but they run under the freeway ramps and cover more than the drawn park, so the drawing is kept. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY DISPLACED -- one of the two pieces making up this shape (the paved path further southeast) really lies about 17-22 m south of where it is drawn here; Pier & Point shifted it on purpose to close a real gap (a planting/tree strip between two paved features) with a single deliberate move rather than tracing that gap's own edges. The other piece (the strip along the creek's near bank) is a computed shape bounded by streets, the creek and neighbouring mapped shapes, not hand-traced. Overlaps the existing 'Mission Creek Park' shape; the map does not yet reconcile that overlap with this record or with P8. Meets the Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge) record (P1) exactly along a line through the south-west end of the striped crosswalk beside the Pavilion (the crosswalk belongs to the east reach). Deliberately not trimmed back from the street lines: this record includes area covering today's paved road across the corridor (a park-corridor concept, not today's satellite extent) -- the same kind of exception as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza. This is not a mispositioned trace; it is an intentional choice to keep the corridor continuous rather than split by a road the park is meant to cross at grade. Pier & Point chose to keep this drawing and cite the Assessor lots under it. Pier & Point reads lot 3810006 (16,093 m2, active, Channel St 202) as covering both P1 and the already built Huffaker Park part of P2, and lot 8710002 (16,398 m2, active, recorded 1999-09-21) as covering the part of P2 not yet constructed and P5 (which has no shape of its own on this map). Against this drawing, lot 3810006 overlaps it by 7,982 m2 and lot 8710002 by 6,164 m2; the two lots together are about 32,500 m2 and run out over the creek and up the strip into P1, so neither is P2's own lot. Both lots also lie under the tracked Mission Creek Park, which already unions P1, P2 and P8.

The schematic design is undated; its one dated item is a plan sheet of June 23, 2006, so the 'existing' conditions it describes are as of an unknown (probably 2000s) date. The February 10, 2022 Citizens Advisory Committee overview deck could not be read (connection reset) and is not cited.
No construction cost, opening date, designer or contractor was found.

open_questions: No source read dates when this specific stretch was built. OCII's Nov 2024 timeline gives 2002 for the opening of "Mission Creek P1", but whether this traced stretch is that P1 is not confirmed. It was hand-traced from satellite imagery because it was visibly already landscaped, not because any source dated its construction.

Pier & Point read OCII's plan labels P1 and P3 as both falling somewhere in this general stretch, based on the Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update' -- but that deck's slide 3 is titled 'MISSION CREEK PARK (P3)', while its slide 2 map image labels 'MISSION CREEK PARK P1' on the south-bank strip and P3 separately; which label (if either) applies to this exact segment, versus to the separately tracked Mission Creek Park record's own P1 (an amphitheater, per OCII's current open-space page), is not resolved.

Name/operator: presumed to be part of the same SF Recreation and Park Department-managed Mission Creek Park system as its neighbors (the department's Mission Creek South list includes "An esplanade (between 3rd and 4th streets)"), but no source read names this specific segment.

As of 2026-09-22, flagged rather than resolved: this record is currently classified 'Mission Bay South' and its own sourcing leans on Mission Bay South's P1/P3 plan labels (see above). But this record's own coordinates sit at the same latitude as other already-tracked Mission Bay North records (The Beacon, Rich Sorro Commons), north of the core of the separately tracked, South-side Mission Creek Park record. A landscape architecture firm's own project page (Munden Fry Landscape Associates, mflastudio.com/mission-creek-park-north) describes "Mission Creek Park North" (client Catellus; "TIMELINE 1999-2011", "STATUS Built", 7.5 acres -- a project timeline, not an opening date) as framed "on the north by mid-rise and tower residential developments and on the south by Mission Creek and a thriving, eclectic house boat community", which matches this record's own traced bank; OCII's September 2023 transition presentation separately lists parcels 'NP1-NP5'. Whether this segment is actually part of Mission Bay North's NP system rather than South's P1/P3 is an open identity question bigger than a date, not resolved here -- flagged for a closer look, possibly including whether this record's site classification itself should change.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the summary previously said this stretch is on Mission Creek's north/west bank; the traced polygon sits on the Channel St side (south/east bank), as does the Pavilion, and OCII's Nov 2024 map shows the P1 label on the south-bank strip. Berry St, the north bank, is about 200 m away.
No source read gives a completion date for this stretch of park (OCII's 2002 date is for "Mission Creek P1", not confirmed to be this reach), and no building-permit search has been made for it.

open_questions: No source read gives this median island's own construction date or says it was built. OCII's September 2023 presentation lists it with P11 as parcels RPD "will manage" (transfer planned "by the end of December 2023"; the Board of Supervisors adopted Resolution 574-23 on December 5, 2023 authorizing termination of OCII's ground lease), which is a plan; the draft parks agreement's statement of who holds it is in the next question.

Who built and who holds it: the City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement (recital D) lists P10, P11 and P11A among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and section 5(j) says they 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works), with any CFD funds used by RPD to maintain them on PW's behalf or passed to PW. Recital C says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay parks; no source read says who built these three parcels. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo says the Board would need to vacate the public right-of-way status on the park parcels, and the Board's December 5, 2023 resolution (File 231132) approved the agreement and said Port and RPD expected to seek the jurisdictional transfer by a separate ordinance in early 2024. No signed agreement, transfer ordinance or later source on these three parcels was found, so Public Works is the holder per the draft only.
The 'P11A' label appears on OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map, but no source read gives the island's name, operator or completion date.

open_questions: OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map labels this strip "P11", and SF Recreation and Parks' April 2025 timeline says "P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)"; neither gives a month or describes the strip. OCII's September 2023 presentation is a plan (RPD "will manage" P11/11A) and does not itself say the strip was built.

OCII's November 2024 CAC update lists "Mission Bay Commons (P11, P12, P13, P15, P16, P17)" as one group of parks; its map puts the "P11" label at the Mission Bay Circle roundabout, where the December 2019 Land Use Map also draws P11, and shows only P12-P15 as current interim use or pilot sites.

Who built and who holds it: the City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement (recital D) lists P10, P11 and P11A among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and section 5(j) says they 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works), with any CFD funds used by RPD to maintain them on PW's behalf or passed to PW. Recital C says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay parks; no source read says who built these three parcels. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo says the Board would need to vacate the public right-of-way status on the park parcels, and the Board's December 5, 2023 resolution (File 231132) approved the agreement and said Port and RPD expected to seek the jurisdictional transfer by a separate ordinance in early 2024. No signed agreement, transfer ordinance or later source on these three parcels was found, so Public Works is the holder per the draft only.

The shape of P11 rests on Pier & Point's judgment: SF Rec & Park's April 2025 timeline lists 'P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)' without describing the parcel, and OCII's November 2024 CAC update groups P11 with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 as 'Mission Bay Commons'. OCII's December 2019 Land Use Map draws the 'P11' label on a thin strip just east of Mission Bay Circle, where this strip is. Whether P11 is only this 4.8 m median or a larger Commons segment has not been settled.

records.summary: P10 is a park parcel labelled on OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, tracked here as the landscaped center island of the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout (the map draws the label 'P10' on the circular island inside the ring labelled 'MISSION BAY CIRCLE'; EPA's July 2012 fact sheet names 'Park P10 and Mission Bay Circle' together as one funded construction project). OCII's September 2023 open-space transition presentation lists P10 among the parcels the Recreation and Parks Department will manage, not among the 'when built' parcels; the presentation is a plan and does not itself say whether P10 was complete. The City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement lists P10 among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and says P10, P11 and P11A 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works); the draft says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay Parks, but not who built this parcel, and no signed text of the agreement was found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- hand-traced from satellite imagery, not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. Deliberately not trimmed back from the street lines: this is a real roundabout center island, ringed by the circulating roadway in DataSF's street data -- trimming it against the standard street buffer would cut real, visible parts of the island, not correct a mispositioning. lot 8709003 (1400 Owens St per DataSF, MB-RA zoning, recorded 1999-09-21, active, 12,999 m2) lies under this island and its neighbours. Pier & Point reads it as split between P10 (the roundabout island), P8 and P7 or P9 across from P8; against our drawings it overlaps P8 by 3,603 m2, P10 by 983 m2, P7 by 3,431 m2 and P9 by 136 m2. P10 has no lot of its own, so the drawing is kept.

open_questions: EPA's July 2012 brownfields fact sheet names "Mission Bay Park P10" (Subgrant 4, $760,000) for "the construction of Park P10 and Mission Bay Circle" and carries the photo caption "Landscaping and hardscaping enhance the look of Mission Bay Park P10"; it gives no start or completion year. EPA's November 4, 2011 advisory announces a tour "to celebrate the completion of Mission Bay Drive and Circle", while Bay Crossings (December 2011) calls Mission Bay Circle "a landscaped turnaround that will eventually serve as a gateway" and says a new road "will open in early-to-mid 2012"; those two sources differ on how finished the Circle was in November 2011. No source read dates the start or completion of the park itself.

Who built and who holds it: the City's September 22, 2023 draft Mission Bay parks agreement (recital D) lists P10, P11 and P11A among the parks 'completed and accepted' and managed by OCII under its ground lease, and section 5(j) says they 'are not being accepted by RPD, and will remain public rights of way under the jurisdiction of PW' (Public Works), with any CFD funds used by RPD to maintain them on PW's behalf or passed to PW. Recital C says the master developer (Catellus and its successors) was obliged to develop the Mission Bay parks; no source read says who built these three parcels. The Port's October 6, 2023 memo says the Board would need to vacate the public right-of-way status on the park parcels, and the Board's December 5, 2023 resolution (File 231132) approved the agreement and said Port and RPD expected to seek the jurisdictional transfer by a separate ordinance in early 2024. No signed agreement, transfer ordinance or later source on these three parcels was found, so Public Works is the holder per the draft only.

As of 2026-09-29, no source read dates the start or completion of Park P10 itself. The July 2012 EPA fact sheet (undated construction, 'projected' workers) and the Nov 2011 EPA advisory (completion of 'Mission Bay Drive and Circle') do not separate the island; the earlier '2010 under construction' milestone had no source for its year and was removed, and the Nov 2011 milestone's 'under construction' status was removed because the EPA advisory contradicts it.

Whether Park P10 is only the roundabout's center island is unconfirmed: EPA's fact sheet gives $760,000 for 'the construction of Park P10 and Mission Bay Circle' together, which looks large for an island alone. The 'landscaped with grass and trees' description rests on Pier & Point's reading of satellite imagery, not a document.

A Rec and Park update posted October 5, 2026 says "the new skate and roll space is likely to go on the parcels labeled 'Future Active Recreation Parks' (P9/P7)".

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- computed from real DataSF street/curb data plus a stopping line drawn by Pier & Point (not a surveyed parcel or GIS file from the project team). The north/west edges are exact real street-buffer boundary. The south edge is a line drawn by Pier & Point, not a mapped street or parcel boundary -- there appears to be bare ground between it and the buildings further south that isn't included here (an imagery observation, no document cited), since Pier & Point judged that the parcel doesn't extend that far. The P9/P7 split is a straight line, not sourced to any drawn plan boundary. SF Rec & Park's Mission Bay Future Parks Project page names P7 & P9 as future 'Active Recreation' parks (anticipated skate park, pickleball courts and a ballfield), fully funded through OCII, with construction to begin late 2028 and opening early 2030; no schematic design specific to P9 was found. lot 8709003 (1400 Owens St per DataSF, MB-RA zoning, recorded 1999-09-21, active, 12,999 m2) overlaps this drawing by only 136 m2; most of the lot lies under P7, P8 and P10. Pier & Point reads it as split between P10 (the roundabout island), P8 and P7 or P9 across from P8; against our drawings it overlaps P8 by 3,603 m2, P10 by 983 m2, P7 by 3,431 m2 and P9 by 136 m2. P9 has no lot of its own, so the drawing is kept. The south edge is a line drawn by Pier & Point, not a mapped street or parcel boundary -- there is real bare ground between it and the two buildings further south that isn't included here. The P9/P7 split is a straight line, not sourced to any drawn plan boundary. Pier & Point reads it as split between P10 (the roundabout island), P8 and P7 or P9 across from P8; against our drawings it overlaps P8 by 3,603 m2, P10 by 983 m2, P7 by 3,431 m2 and P9 by 136 m2. P7 has no lot of its own, so the drawing is kept. Pier & Point kept this drawing and cites the Assessor lots under P7 and its neighbour: active lot 8709002 (10,178 m2) overlaps this drawing by 640 m2 and lot 8709003 (12,999 m2) by 3,431 m2. The lot lines cross the space as diagonal bands and do not follow the park as it is on the ground, so neither is P7's own lot.
notes.digitized_from: Computed from DataSF's official street centerlines, with extra generous clearance around Owens St's own centerline and around the P10 roundabout island, rather than hand-traced from imagery. search_aliases: P23 -- landscaped plaza and lawn (north of the pavilion, toward Chase Center)
records.summary: A landscaped lawn and plaza between Illinois Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, extending toward the Chase Center roundabout and next to a pavilion (not the Mission Creek Park Pavilion, which is about 800 m to the north-west); per Pier & Point's own reading of satellite imagery, real landscaped/paved open land; its outline was traced by hand by Pier & Point as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, not taken from a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P23' among the parcels the Port of San Francisco will manage (not among the 'when built' parcels); that presentation is a plan and does not say whether the area was built. SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. OCII's November 14, 2024 update map labels 'P23 & P24' with the colour its legend gives as a completed park; the deck gives no completion date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/paved open land per Esri satellite imagery, outlined as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes and divided at seams chosen by hand by Pier & Point, rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. Operator: the Port of San Francisco per OCII's Sept 2023 transition presentation ('Port will manage P18, P21, P23 & P24'); SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. The remaining ~5,785 sqm of the original fragment (the building-hugging plaza strip, the panhandle, and P24's own dropped horns) is deliberately left off the map, pending further review of whether it is a separate plan parcel. DataSF's Assessor layer has active lot 3940002 (MB-RA|P zoning, active, 4,806 m2) near this park: 57% of this drawing lies inside it and the drawing covers 80% of the lot; the drawing and the lot overlap only in part, so the lot is not this park's own and the drawing is kept. Since 2026-10-12 the outline stops at the edge of Assessor lot 3940003 (409/499 Illinois Street), which overlapped it by 2,032 m2; that strip is part of the lot, not of this drawing.
notes.digitized_from: Outlined as the open ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes around the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St / Chase Center area (one piece of 19,181.78 sqm before cutting). Pier & Point split that piece in three at its two natural narrow points (lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then combined parts by hand: P23 is the north part (the lawn wedge by the Chase Center roundabout) with its thin building-hugging 'panhandle' dropped, plus the part of the middle piece (the plaza) that lies east of the line where the lawn narrows into that panhandle, extended south. Not taken from a surveyed parcel.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own: lot 3940002 was compared and does not match (see the accuracy note).

open_questions: The April 2019 SocketSite article names the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park' -- not to be confused with Mariposa Park, OCII's own official P26 per its current open-space page (listed separately from P23/P24; see the open questions on Pier & Point's record for P26, the landscaped wedge at the 16th/3rd/Owens St interchange, for a related P26 label conflict). Not reconciled here, only noted so the two 'Mariposa'-named places aren't conflated.

No source names this specific lawn/plaza or gives its own completion date. SocketSite (April 22, 2019) described the P23/P24 open space as "yet to be completed" and "expected to be completed by the end of this year" (an expected date), and OCII's November 2024 map points its "P23 & P24" label at an area coloured as "COMPLETED PARK"; OCII's September 2023 presentation says only that the Port "will manage" P23 (a plan).

By Pier & Point's reading of the map it sits adjacent to the Chase Center arena (SocketSite, April 22, 2019: "slated to be completed this August", an expected date) and to the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St area, but no source ties this landscaped area's own completion to either project.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P23' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed -- OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page (sfocii.org/projects/mission-bay-south/open-space) does not list a P23 at all among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).

The April 2019 SocketSite article says only that the P23/P24 open space had 'yet to be completed' and was expected to be completed by the end of 2019; it does not say construction had started, so the 2019-04 milestone is 'planned', not 'under construction'.

names: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P24
search_aliases: P24 -- waterfront lawn (Bayfront Park approach, south of 499 Illinois St)
records.summary: A triangular waterfront lawn with a curved path south of 499 Illinois Street, labelled P24 on OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map; it visually resembles Bayfront Park's own style and may be a continuation of it (an observation from satellite imagery, with no document cited), and its outline was traced by hand by Pier & Point as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, not taken from a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P24' among the parcels the Port of San Francisco 'will manage' (not among the 'when built' parcels); that presentation is a plan and does not say whether the lawn was built. OCII's November 14, 2024 update map shades the area labelled 'P23 & P24' as 'COMPLETED PARK' (a reading of the map as of that date; no completion date is given). Name and specific operator not confirmed by any source found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- landscaped open land (lawn, curved path, scattered trees) as seen in Esri satellite imagery (an imagery observation; no document cited), outlined as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes and cut by hand by Pier & Point at a point where the shape forks, rather than at a surveyed parcel boundary. Operator: the Port of San Francisco per OCII's Sept 2023 transition presentation ('Port will manage P18, P21, P23, & P24'); SocketSite (April and June 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. A hedged observation from imagery (no source cited) is that it visually resembles Bayfront Park's own style and may be a continuation of it. DataSF's Assessor layer has active lot 3941032 (MB-RA zoning, recorded 2018-10-02, active, 10,721 m2) near this park: 86% of this drawing lies inside it and the drawing covers 53% of the lot; the lot is larger than this park (10,721 m2 against 6,605 m2), so using it would claim ground beyond the park, so the lot is not this park's own and the drawing is kept. Since 2026-10-12 the outline stops at the edge of Assessor lot 3940003 (409/499 Illinois Street), which overlapped it by 509 m2; that strip is part of the lot, not of this drawing. Its north edge is the straight extension of that lot's southern edge to this drawing's west and east edges.
notes.digitized_from: Outlined as the open ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes around the 499 Illinois St / Bayfront Park area (one piece of 19,181.78 sqm before cutting). Pier & Point split that piece in three at its two natural narrow points (lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then cut it by hand the same way as P26: the wide, single 'head' was kept and the thin, branching 'horns' were dropped. Not taken from a surveyed parcel.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own: lot 3941032 was compared and does not match (see the accuracy note).

open_questions: Pier & Point first identified the building here as UCSF Neurosurgery at Mission Bay from its own knowledge (correcting an earlier mis-resolution to Genentech Hall), and at first that identification was not independently corroborated by a primary source. Later research found strong, independent corroboration: a contractor project page names this same OCII Block 23A as the site of the Joan and Sanford I. Weill Neurosciences Building, and UCSF Health's own clinic-location page places its 'Neurosurgery Mission Bay - Fourth St.' service at 1651 4th Street, the Weill building's address, directly adjacent to Third Street Garage as this record's geometry describes. Not treated as fully closed: no single source explicitly ties the parcel-level footprint to the 1651 4th Street address by lot number.

Exact opening day is not confirmed: UCSF Health's Weill page gives only the month ('It opened its doors in July 2021'), which is the date shown. UCSF's own news article, dated 2021-10 by its web address, could not be read (access refused on 2026-10-12), so no source read gives an opening day.

Construction cost is not stated in any source read: Architectural Record's project data lists 'Cost: Withheld'. The only figure on record is the $357.6 million project budget approved by the UC Regents in May 2017 (Regents item F4: 'The total project cost of $357.6 million, including $12 million of capitalized interest incurred during construction'), a budget rather than a construction cost.

The March 2016 Regents preliminary-plans item (270,000 gsf, six stories) predates the Weill naming gift and 'Weill Neurosciences Building' name; identification with this record rests on the Block 23A site match (confirmed elsewhere in this record's own sources), not a name match in the 2016 item itself.

The opening month shown is July 2021, as UCSF Health's own Weill page says ('It opened its doors in July 2021'); the UCSF news release dated 2021-10 could not be read and is likely an announcement date. The March 2016 Regents item planned full budget approval for March 2017, while the Regents' budget and design item for this building (Item F4, cited in this record's sources) is for the May 17, 2017 meeting, so that schedule slipped. The March 2016 item is an agenda item requesting approval; the minutes recording its vote, and the minutes of the May 2017 meeting, were not read.
