records.summary: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois Street, a 347,500-sq-ft eye-care facility in three buildings (a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and a 3-story north wing) that SF YIMBY reported open on November 27, 2020 (SmithGroup architect). The UC Regents approved a $237.13 million total project budget for it in January 2017: "The total project cost of $237.13 million (including $12 million of capitalized interest incurred during construction)"; that is a budget, not a construction cost. It stands on OCII plan block 33, between Third St and Illinois St: the City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside this outline, and UCSF's own 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'. Its footprint here is approximate (see the shape's accuracy caveat).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL BUILDING, APPROXIMATE BOUNDARY -- a real, standing structure clearly visible in Esri satellite imagery (not open land): UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St. The City's official address point for 490 Illinois St (DataSF Addresses, address ID 743049, on Assessor parcel 8725001) lies inside this outline; UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation map labels block 33, between Third St and Illinois St, 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)'; and SF YIMBY (2020-11-27) places the facilities 'along 3rd Street, immediately across from the UCSF Medical Center'. Boundary is the edge of the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes (following the estimated curb radius), with one corner redrawn to the real street angle (see the mapping log), not a hand-traced or surveyed building footprint. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. DataSF's Assessor layer has one active lot, 8725001 (480 16th St, MB-RA zoning, recorded 1999-09-21, 15,504 m2), under this building and the two other tracked buildings on this strip between Third St and Illinois St (UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, UCSF Bayfront Medical Building and UCSF Illinois Street Garage). No lot separates them, so this outline is a drawing of the building from imagery, kept because the lot is not this building's own.

SPLIT 2026-09-22: this record was previously a single OCII plan block 34 record (a probable, geographically-inferred identity for the WHOLE of a mapped area that also included the Illinois Street Garage to its south). This was corrected: UCSF built three real structures where the OCII plan showed two, and Bayfront Medical Building is only the north piece of that area (the Illinois Street Garage record covers the south piece). The split follows a visible satellite roofline seam, not a surveyed or permitted lot line, and its exact boundary should be treated as indicative rather than authoritative.

Floor-area figures disagree and none is shown as this building's size. SF YIMBY (October 2, 2021): "The structure will span 182,800 square feet of floor area." Healthcare Facilities Today (August 29, 2024): "The five-story, all-electric, 181,000-square-foot building". Stantec (September 17, 2024): "the clinic's 183,000 square feet". Clark's project page: "The 190,000-square-foot clinical building". Guttmann & Blaevoet: "Clinical Building: 190,000 SF". Some figures are pre-construction plans and some were written after opening, and the sources do not say what each measures. A total project cost of about $335.8 million for the clinical building and garage together was cited in an earlier version of this record with no named source; it could not be traced to one, so it is not shown. Other figures found: Guttmann & Blaevoet gives "a $210M, 190,000sf clinical building" and "a $32M, 500-stall parking garage" ("Cost: $242 million"), and Commercial Property Executive's $228 million (see costs) is attributed to the San Francisco Chronicle; they disagree, and none is a UCSF or Regents document.

As of 2026-10-12, UCSF Real Estate's project page could not be read (access refused). Stantec's news release (September 17, 2024) and Clark's project page and 2021 release are readable and support the story count, the architect and the construction team; the 520 Illinois St address rests on Commercial Property Executive (unreadable on re-read) and on DBI permit M1227947, which lists "520 illinois street and 590 illinois street" for UCSF block 8725, lot 001. The Regents outcome for the May 2020 Block 34 items was not found (only the committee agenda was read). The construction start is Clark's September 2021 groundbreaking announcement; CPE and Clark say the garage began earlier (April 2021). UCSF's Department of Ophthalmology directions page gives "a UCSF parking structure at 590 Illinois Street (same block as our 490 Illinois Street clinic building)", and the DBI permit lists 590 Illinois Street beside 520 without saying which building is which; SF YIMBY puts the garage at 499 Illinois Street. Whether CPE's $228 million includes the garage is not stated.

Update 2026-10-12: the opening is confirmed by sources written after it, but none read names the opening day. Hospital Management (August 26, 2024) says the building was "due to start receiving patients on 27 August" (a scheduled date, published the day before); Healthcare Facilities Today (August 29, 2024) and Stantec (September 17, 2024) report it open without giving the day; Commercial Property Executive's opening coverage (commercialsearch.com), UCSF Real Estate's project page and UCSF's news site refused access. The opening is therefore shown at month level. The $228 million figure and the garage "came online in 2023" statement also come from the Commercial Property Executive page, which could not be re-read. SF YIMBY (February 8, 2023) had said the building was "expected to open later this year"; the sources do not say when the opening date moved.

records.name: UCSF Illinois Street Garage
records.summary: A nine-story, 500-car parking garage on UCSF's Block 34 at the corner of 3rd and Mariposa Streets, listed at 590 Illinois Street by the UCSF Department of Ophthalmology's directions page ("a UCSF parking structure at 590 Illinois Street") and at 499 Illinois Street by SF YIMBY (see open questions). Pier & Point identifies it as the southernmost portion of what had been tracked as one combined "block 34" shape -- split off 2026-09-22 along a visible roofline seam from the Bayfront Medical Building immediately north of it, both described by Clark Construction and SF YIMBY as part of UCSF's development of Block 34.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL BUILDING, APPROXIMATE BOUNDARY -- a real, standing structure clearly visible in Esri satellite imagery (not open land). The boundary is the edge of the open ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes (following the curb radius of the street lines), with the north cap (and, for the garage, the cut from the building to its north) re-aligned to the real street angle -- see the mapping log -- not a hand-traced or surveyed building footprint. The split between this building and its neighbor follows a visible satellite roofline seam, not a surveyed or permitted lot line -- treat the exact boundary as indicative, not authoritative. DataSF's Assessor layer has one active lot, 8725001 (480 16th St, MB-RA zoning, recorded 1999-09-21, 15,504 m2), under this building and the two other tracked buildings on this strip between Third St and Illinois St (UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, UCSF Bayfront Medical Building and UCSF Illinois Street Garage). No lot separates them, so this outline is a drawing of the building from imagery, kept because the lot is not this building's own.
notes.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and neighbouring mapped shapes between 3rd St and Illinois St, south of 16th St, extended down to Mariposa St. Pier & Point identified this piece as capturing two separate real buildings, not one, and cut it at the visible gap between the two rooflines in Esri satellite imagery (lat 37.76578) -- see the record formerly filed as Mission Bay block 33 (now UCSF Valley Center for Vision -- west building) for the piece north of that cut.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The strip holds one Assessor lot, 8725001, under three separately drawn buildings (see the accuracy note), so no lot of its own exists for this building.

The match is by location only and is never treated as confirmed on its own, so this is logged as corroboration, not an independent primary source.

SPLIT 2026-09-22: this record was previously Mission Bay block 33 (a probable, geographically-inferred identity for the WHOLE of what is now the UCSF Valley Center for Vision -- west building record -- a mistaken pairing). This was corrected: the garage is the southernmost piece of the former Mission Bay block 34 shape, not block 33. This record's shape is now the south piece of that split (the Bayfront Medical Building record holds the north piece); the split follows a visible satellite roofline seam, not a surveyed or permitted lot line, and its exact boundary should be treated as indicative rather than authoritative.

An earlier version of this record cited a combined clinical-building-plus-garage project cost of about $335.8 million with no named source; it could not be traced to one, so it is not shown. Figures found for the garage: Guttmann & Blaevoet (engineering firm) project page for UCSF Mission Bay Medical Office Building and Parking Garage at Block 34: "a $32M, 500-stall parking garage" ("Cost: $242 million" for the whole project). That is a consultant's figure, not a UCSF or Regents document, and is not recorded as a cost here.

The April 2021 construction-start milestone comes from Clark Construction's own release of September 23, 2021: "Clark started construction on the garage portion of the development in April 2021." UCSF Real Estate's combined project page for the Bayfront Medical Building and Illinois Street Garage could not be read (access refused), so it is not used for this date.

As of 2026-09-29, UCSF Real Estate's project page (the source for the 590 Illinois St address, 9 stories / 500 spaces and the May 15, 2023 opening) could not be checked, nor could its archived Wayback copy or other UCSF pages, so those details are unverified. The readable Clark Construction release confirms Block 34 with a new 9-level, 500-space garage whose construction started in April 2021, and projected delivery of the garage and clinical building in summer 2024. Correction 2026-10-12: the 590 Illinois Street address is also given by a readable page, the UCSF Department of Ophthalmology's directions: "there is a UCSF parking structure at 590 Illinois Street (same block as our 490 Illinois Street clinic building)"; the nine-level, 500-space figures are in Clark's release: "a new 9-level parking garage that will provide 500 spaces".

Update 2026-10-12, opening date: two sources conflict or cannot be read. SF YIMBY (February 8, 2023) already calls the garage "now-open", which is before the May 15, 2023 opening reported from UCSF Real Estate's project page; that page refused access (as did its archived copy), so it could not be checked, and the opening could be earlier than May 2023, including in 2022. Commercial Property Executive (commercialsearch.com), cited elsewhere on this site for the garage "coming online" in 2023, also refused access. Clark Construction's September 23, 2021 release only projects delivery of the garage and clinical building for summer 2024 and is not an opening source. The milestone shows the earliest date a readable source reports the garage open, not an opening date.

Update 2026-10-12, address: UCSF Real Estate's project page (not readable) is the source of 590 Illinois Street; SF YIMBY (February 8, 2023) puts the garage at "499 Illinois Street". The Department of Building Inspection's permit M1227947 (June 2022) gives "520 illinois street and 590 illinois street" as the addresses for UCSF block 8725, lot 001, the lot under this garage and the Bayfront Medical Building, without saying which building is which; its permit data places 499 Illinois Street on block 3940, a different block. The address is shown as 590 Illinois Street with the 499 report noted, not resolved.

records.summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated a development concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), anchored by a tower as tall as 850 feet (SF Standard, March 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path, the same one used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 8701004, 8701003, 3797004 and 8700001, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. DataSF lists these four active lots (700 4th St, 311 Townsend St, an unaddressed lot, and 797 7th St) as the rail yard, and the earlier outline, built from the surrounding street centerlines, lies 83% inside them and is about 10 m wider along the long sides. The lots total about 16.7 acres, while SF Planning and Caltrain's FAQ describe a '20-acre site'; whether the planning site includes ground outside these lots, or the figure is rounded, is not settled. The lots are the legal boundaries; the 4th & King Street Station and the tracks are inside them. Status and use are as shown on this record.

notes.why_no_real_parcel: The rail yard is made of four active Assessor lots (8701004, 8701003, 3797004 and 8700001; DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn), and this record's outline is their union. The lots total about 16.7 acres against the planning site's described 20 acres, which is an open question.

records.notes: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 8701004, 8701003, 3797004 and 8700001 (see the accuracy note). SF Planning Case No. 2023-000384CWP, 'SF Railyards Planning Program'. The 20-acre site at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square: Caltrain's northern terminus and an active service/maintenance yard, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. A Development Agreement is the expected approval path (precedent: Pier 70, Mission Rock, Potrero Power Station, all DAs). Adjoins Mission Bay North. OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, as seen in the map image (linked in this record's sources), labels N5A, N6 and N7 in this area with no land-use color and no drawn boundary, unlike the numbered Mission Bay North blocks beside it. That does not settle whether the site lies outside Mission Bay North: in DataSF's redevelopment project areas layer about 41% of this polygon lies inside 'Mission Bay - North', and parcels 8701003 and 8701004 are zoned MB-O. The map PDF and the project-area boundary have not yet been checked to settle this.

records.name: Chase Center
records.summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (February 2025 press reports disagree on who leases the adjacent towers: The Real Deal says Uber and the Warriors each lease office space there, Commercial Observer says both buildings are 100 percent leased to Uber), 100,000 sq ft of retail (Wikipedia's figure; Chase Center's Thrive City page describes retail stores and restaurants "in the surrounding district of Chase Center" and gives no area) and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019. On May 19, 2026 the OCII Commission adopted a sixth amendment to the Mission Bay South Signage Master Plan, raising character heights and awning-sign flexibility for the event center sign program and mixed-use retail.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, DERIVED BOUNDARY -- the outer edge is a real DataSF Assessor Parcel boundary (blklot 8722025); the two notches cut into its NW and SW corners are real OpenStreetMap building traces (the Uber towers), not estimates. The resulting shape has not been independently verified against a surveyed Chase Center site plan -- it is real-minus-real, not a single authoritative source. Two small structures inside this polygon (an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others) remain unidentified. The shape is deliberately not trimmed to DataSF's official street centerlines: that layer shows several stale/closed street segments cutting straight through the arena bowl itself (visible as a literal cross running under the roof when the shape is drawn against the street lines) -- leftover records from the four separate plan blocks (29/30/31/32) that were consolidated into one superblock when Chase Center was built, not real current streets. Trimming against them would remove 16% of this polygon's real area, so it is left untrimmed for this stated reason, as is Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor Parcel blklot 8722025 (Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32), with the two Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office-tower footprints (real OpenStreetMap building outlines, OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655) subtracted out; how it was built is logged in its mapping log.

open_questions: Chase Center's cost is reported at different figures, and none gives a scope or breakdown. $1.4B: Construction Dive, August 6, 2019 ("the $1.4 billion Chase Center", at substantial completion), Bisnow, July 28, 2020 ("its privately financed, $1.4B arena") and Wikipedia's infobox (marked citation needed). $1.5B: Construction Dive, February 15, 2019, headlined "NBA's Warriors propose hotel, condos at $1.5B Chase Center", whose text refers to "its $1.5 billion Chase Center arena project". $1B: Wikipedia's text ("With a $1 billion investment", marked citation needed). Neither Construction Dive article says why its figure differs, so the $1.4 billion shown here is one press figure, not a reconciled cost. A $1.3B alternate figure attributed to a Warriors executive had no support in its cited source and was removed on 2026-09-29.

Who leases the adjacent office towers: The Real Deal (2025-02-14) says "The Warriors and Uber each leases office space at the property for their headquarters"; Commercial Observer (2025-02-11) says "two adjacent office properties 100 percent leased to Uber". Neither was checked against a lease record or a primary source. An earlier '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claim was removed on 2026-09-29 because no readable source states it.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex is described by Bisnow (July 28, 2020) as "next to their home arena" and by SocketSite (September 14, 2020, tagged "Blocks 29-32") as replacing the existing three-story retail building on the northeast corner of the Chase Center site; no source read gives its own block or lot, so whether it falls within parcel 8722025 or on a distinct parcel is not confirmed. SocketSite also reports that a later amendment would allow up to 230 hotel rooms and no condos. No source read says whether it has been built or started.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
No openly licensed image was found; recommend linking rather than hosting until one is confirmed.
No opening date found for The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way): checked its own Thrive City vendor page for a firm date; retail_confirmed.csv's own opened field is also blank.

As of 2026-09-29: the first photo (exterior, taken 2019-07-27) shows the arena under construction, before the 2019-09-06 opening milestone, so it fits none of the image categories used here; it keeps the 'now' category pending a decision. The interior photo (2019-12-27) was re-tagged 'completed' (within a year after opening). Chase Center's Thrive City tenant list was read on its live page on 2026-09-29 ('Open Now'); tenants not on it (Siren, b8ta, Mission Bay Wine Bar) have not been re-confirmed open.

b8ta is listed as closed on the strength of the chain's closure: Wikipedia says b8ta 'closed its last retail stores in the United States on February 18, 2022'. The page does not mention Thrive City or Chase Center, and no source read places a b8ta store at Thrive City or gives its opening or closing date; the location shown for it is therefore not stated. open_questions: Uber's SEC EDGAR company record lists 1725 3rd Street as its business address (read 2026-09-29), though a May 2023 SF Standard report said that specific building had never been occupied by Uber and was being marketed for sublease -- current occupancy is genuinely unclear and not resolved here.

DataSF business-registration data lists Uber-related registrations at the two towers' addresses (Bon Appetit @ Uber, a cafeteria service, on many floors of both 1655 and 1725 3rd St, and Uber Freight Holding Corporation at 1725 3rd St), not yet researched or added as facts. A Mercedes-Benz garage registration appears at 99 Warriors Way, in the arena block, not at either tower address. A registration is not evidence of occupancy.

No dedicated primary source (an Alexandria or Uber press release specifically) was found for the exact completion date of each tower individually; 2021 (SF Standard) is used as a combined year; Office Snapshots shows 'Year 2020' with no stated meaning. Uber's own annual reports on Form 10-K (sec.gov) include a note on the Mission Bay 3 & 4 joint venture that may state when construction was completed; they refused access on 2026-10-12, so no completion year from Uber's own filings is shown, and the 2021 year is SF Standard's alone.

No total development or construction cost for the two towers was found as of 2026-09-23. Press coverage only turns up financing: The Real Deal (2025-02-14) reports a $500 million loan from Goldman Sachs and Barclays that followed a $100 million paydown of the joint venture's previous $600 million JPMorgan Chase loan. A loan is not a construction or development cost, so none is recorded here. Uber's own SEC filings may state its contribution to the joint venture and its lease commitments; they could not be read on 2026-10-12 (access refused), so no such figures are shown.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the 'January 2022 occupancy', '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claims were removed because no source that could be read states them (Office Snapshots has no lease or headcount; SF Standard cites Uber's 2022 blog for 'more than 3,500 employees' across four buildings and says 1725 3rd St was never occupied). ArchDaily's page credits SHoP Architects and lists 423,000 ft2 and a 2022 year, but it describes 'an eleven-story tower at 1455 Third Street and a six-story structure at 1515 Third Street', the campus's other two buildings, so it is not used for these towers. Completion is dated 2021 (the SF Standard says the four-building campus was 'initially completed during the pandemic in 2021'; Office Snapshots shows 'Year 2020' without saying what it refers to); no month is sourced.

Who leases the offices: Press reports disagree. The Real Deal (2025-02-14) says "The Warriors and Uber each leases office space at the property for their headquarters", while Commercial Observer (2025-02-11) calls them "two adjacent office properties 100 percent leased to Uber". Neither was checked against a lease record, so no tenant split is stated here.

Corrected 2026-10-12: this record's 2021 completion milestone had cited Office Snapshots for 'a 2021 completion date'. The Office Snapshots page (2022-01-24) shows 'Year 2020' in its project details, without saying what the year refers to, so it is not cited for the completion year; the 2021 date rests on SF Standard (2023-05-18) alone.
Building numbers: Office Snapshots calls the two towers Uber's 'Buildings 3 & 4', and no source read says which address is which building number.
Architect of the towers: Office Snapshots credits the interiors of Buildings 3 and 4 to Huntsman Architectural Group; no source read names an architect for the towers' shell.

Occupancy of 1725 Third St: in May 2023 the SF Standard reported that Uber was marketing all of 1725 Third St for sublease and described the building as never occupied by Uber; an Uber spokesperson said only that 'one of our buildings is currently unoccupied', so current occupancy is not established. The marketing materials cite 73 parking spaces for that building; Uber's 2022 blog post (as quoted by SF Standard) said more than 3,500 employees would be based at its four-building headquarters.

records.name: Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks
records.distance_note: The dry docks belong to the Pier 68/70 shipyard, next to Crane Cove Park and outside the tracked Pier 70 boundary (the Port's December 2025 park release describes new fencing along the Shipyard at the park's east side). Sources differ on when the shipyard closed: the Port's January and February 2026 memos say it operated until 2016 and has been inactive since, while a Port slide and Potrero View say 2017.

records.summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission's President and the Port's Executive Director declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. The Port is carrying out emergency stabilization repairs to Dry Dock No. 2 and plans to demolish and dispose of both structures; no source reports that demolition has begun. Potrero View reported in July 2026 that the Port has directed the engineering firm GHD to prepare preliminary demolition plans and expects initial plans "by next March" and a demolition contract tendered "the second half of 2027" (the paper's wording, not a Port document). The total estimated cost is $61.2M; as of February 2026 about $20.0M was identified ($18.5M of a requested supplemental appropriation plus $1.5M of BAE settlement funds) and the remaining $41.2M was anticipated in the FY2026-27 budget.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- two hand-traced hull outlines from satellite imagery, accurate to a few metres at best, not a surveyed footprint and not a Port or Assessor geometry. Which hull is Dry Dock No. 2 and which is the Eureka is inferred from their measured lengths against the 900 ft the Port memo gives for Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka lengths Mission Local (528 ft) and Potrero View (570 ft) give, which disagree (Marine Log, 2025-07-24, reporting the Port's request-for-proposals notice for the dry docks, lists the Eureka's length over pontoons as 528 ft and its overall length as 569 ft); no source read places them. The outlines cover the two floating hulls only, not the shipyard as a whole (the Port's July 11, 2017 release describes the shipyard lease as 'nearly 15 acres of land with numerous buildings, over 17 acres of submerged land, and Port-owned equipment'): the Pier 68 wharf arms, the quay, the cranes, the sheds and four unidentified floating tank sections west of the Eureka are left out. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or the Dry Dock Memorandum's own site figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: Assessor lot: both hulls lie inside lot 9900068 (98% of the outline). DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' dataset (acdm-wktn), queried by lot number on 2026-10-10 and read again on 2026-10-11, lists Assessor lot 9900068 in block 9900 (lot 068), marked active, with a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02. The dataset's own description of its recorded-drop-date column reads 'This is the date that the documents related the to dropping/retiring of the parcel was recorded, as tracked by Public Works.' The same row has no map-drop date, is flagged active, and is on the Assessor's secured roll in the copy dated 2026-10-01. The dataset does not say why a recorded drop date and an active flag appear together, so this record states only what the row shows. The lot is the whole shipyard lot, not an outline of the two hulls: the traced hulls cover 18% of it. Port structures carry no street name in that dataset, so a search for PIER-numbered street names finds nothing. Outline: two hand-traced hull outlines -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29). The earlier placeholder box lay in open water north of the shipyard. Hulls were told apart by length. The Port Commission memo (Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09, PDF p. 3) says: 'DD2 is a 900-foot single-section steel floating dry dock constructed by the Bethlehem Steel Corporation in 1970.' Mission Local (2026-02-23) says: 'Dry Dock No. 2, which was built in 1970, ...' and 'The adjacent dry dock, Eureka, which was built in 1945, is 528 feet long'. Potrero View (2026-07-15) gives the Eureka as longer: 'Eureka Drydock is 570 feet.' The sources disagree on the Eureka's length (528 ft is 161 m; 570 ft is 174 m) and agree on its 1945 build. The large eastern hull measures about 283 m (Dry Dock No. 2: 900 ft is 274 m) and the central hull about 169 m including wing walls, so the central hull is the shorter dock whichever Eureka length is right. No source read says which hull sits where, so this match is Pier & Point's own inference. Still no Port GIS layer or site-plan figure to trace from.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Both hulls lie inside Assessor lot 9900068, the whole shipyard lot (DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, checked 2026-10-10 and again 2026-10-11), which this record does not use as an outline because the hulls cover only 18% of it. That row carries a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02 yet reads active; see 'Traced from' above.
notes.regulatory_context: Dry Dock No. 2 (a 900-foot floating dry dock built in 1970) developed excessive listing after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding in November 2025; the Port Commission President and Executive Director declared an emergency on 2025-12-08 (Port Commission memo, Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09). Port staff anticipate advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026 for Dry Dock No. 2 and the neighboring Eureka Dry Dock (a second floating dry dock at Piers 68/70, formerly USS Steadfast/AFDM-14, per Marine Log, 2025-07-24, reporting the Port's request-for-proposals notice, which calls it formerly known as Steadfast (AFDM 14) -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP). Total estimated cost of stabilization and disposal is $61.2M (Capital Planning Committee memo, 2026-02-09); see the record file for the funding breakdown and what remains unfunded.

milestones.text: Port Commission takes up Calendar Item 9A, an informational item with no action required, on the dry dock emergency. The staff memo for it is dated 2026-01-09 and says: auxiliary industrial pumps installed by Port Maintenance staff to pump out the ballast tanks, with staff moving portable pumps from tank to tank; emergency repairs (welding and patching to reduce water intake, and stabilizing or removing the cranes on the wing walls) at a total not-to-exceed cost of $10,000,000; proposals received from three marine contractors on 2026-01-05, with the contract award anticipated the week of 2026-01-20 (so not yet awarded when the memo was written); and staff's anticipation of advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026. The 2026-01-13 meeting date is from the Capital Planning Committee's timeline; the memo itself carries only its own date.

open_questions: The Eureka Dry Dock's length is given as 528 feet by Mission Local (2026-02-23) and as 570 feet by Potrero View (2026-07-15) and by a slide in the Port's Feb 9, 2026 presentation to the Capital Planning Committee ("Eureka (570' x 125')"); the Port's January 2026 memo gives no length for it, and the sources conflict, so no length is shown as settled here. Whether the Board of Supervisors adopted the $18.5M supplemental appropriation (ordinance File 251248, introduced Dec 16, 2025) and whether the remaining $41.2M was appropriated in the FY2026-27 budget is not reported in any source read; the Port's Feb 9, 2026 memo shows the $18.5M and $1.5M of BAE settlement funds as the first $20.0M of the $61.2M total.

Whether demolition will be completed "before winter storms" (a claim in an unsourced summary, not repeated in this record) is not supported by any primary source found; SFist (2026-03-05) reports it will likely be a year before the dry dock situation is resolved, and roughly $41.2M of the $61.2M total remained unfunded as of Feb 2026.

Has demolition of the dry docks begun, or has the Port advertised or awarded a demolition contract? As of 2026-10-12 no source read reports that demolition began, and no Port Commission item or Port contract notice was found reporting an advertisement or award; the July 2026 Potrero View report describes the design-build contract as still to come. The dry docks are therefore shown as existing, with demolition planned.
What becomes of BAE Systems' ship-repair operations at the adjacent Pier 70 shipyard once these dry docks are removed is not addressed in the sources reviewed here.

records.summary: Pier 54, a Port of San Francisco pier just east of Chase Center and the Mission Bay neighborhood (per SFGate), was red-tagged in early July 2024, according to SFGate. In an August 2024 memo, Port Engineering recommended closing it to the public and tenants for safety reasons, and the 11 tenants were told to vacate by the end of 2024. The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) proposes $2.0M to demolish the pier's shed; that is a proposed budget line, and no source read says demolition has started or gives a start date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 9900054, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. DataSF lists the pier as its own lot, 9900054 (block 9900, with the pier number as the lot), and the earlier hand trace lies 92% inside it, so the match is clear; no Port document read names the lot. The lot's edge can run a few metres off the visible deck edge, and the lot is the legal boundary, not the deck and shed. Status and use are as shown on this record.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 9900054 (recorded ; mapped 1998-07-01; active); cross-checked against Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Pier 54 has its own Assessor lot, 9900054 (DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, active), and this record's outline is that lot.
notes.regulatory_context: Red-tagged in early July 2024 (SFGate, Sept 2024); Port Engineering recommended closing the pier to the public and tenants for safety reasons, and its 11 tenants were told to vacate by the end of 2024 (Port memo, Aug 9, 2024, written before that date). The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31, Feb 2026) proposes a 'Pier 54 Shed Demolition' line item totaling $2.0M ($500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28); it is a proposed budget line, no source read says demolition has started, and no line item for full substructure removal appears in that document.

records.summary: A WETA/Port of San Francisco ferry terminal on Terry A. Francois Blvd near Agua Vista Park, in the Mission Bay/Central Waterfront area. The Port's undated project page lists "2025 Phase 2a Marine Demolition and Mattress (complete)" and "2026/2027 Phase 2b Mission Bay Ferry Landing and Agua Vista Park (in progress)"; the San Francisco County Transportation Authority (SFCTA) said on April 28, 2026 that completion is expected by the end of 2027 (an expected date). The City's 2018 environmental review covers it together with a separate water taxi landing about 400 feet to the south.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- the two landings as drawn in the City's 2018 layout plan (Final Mitigated Negative Declaration, Figure 3), placed on satellite imagery by overlay, accurate to a few metres at best. This is the 2018 design, not an as-built survey: imagery captured 2025-08-29 shows no landing built yet, and no later plan was found, so the design or its position may have changed. Each shape joins the landing's pieces (Ferry Landing: connecting ramp and pier, gangway, float; Water Taxi Landing: platform, gangway, float). Lengths measured off the drawing differ from the sizes the document states: the gangways scale to about 70 ft against the stated 85 ft (ferry) and 80 ft (water taxi), and the ferry float to about 128 ft against 135 ft. The shapes follow the drawing. The Ferry Landing's landward end is trimmed to Bayfront Park's boundary, where the drawn corner overlapped it by about 35 m2. Landside improvements, dredge areas and the fender piles are not included.
notes.digitized_from: Assessor lots: the City's environmental review gives the project's lots as 9900/064 and 9900/064H (Final Mitigated Negative Declaration, San Francisco Planning Case No. 2017-008824ENV, cover page, PDF p. 1: 'Block/Lot:         9900/064 and 9900/064H', 'Lot Size:         153,257 square feet'). DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' dataset (acdm-wktn), queried by lot number on 2026-10-10, lists both: Assessor lot 9900064 in block 9900 (lot 064), marked active, and Assessor lot 9900064H in block 9900 (lot 064H), marked active. The traced shapes do not follow those lot outlines: 33% of the Ferry Landing shape lies inside lot 9900064, and 12% of the Water Taxi Landing shape lies inside lot 9900064H; the rest of each lies outside the lots. A search for PIER-numbered street names finds nothing, because Port parcels carry no street name there. Outline: two shapes traced from the layout plan in the City's own environmental review -- Figure 3 (PDF p. 10) of the Final Mitigated Negative Declaration, San Francisco Planning Case No. 2017-008824ENV, amended 2018-06-18 (https://sfmea.sfplanning.org/Mission%20Bay%20Ferry_Final%20MND_061818.pdf) -- the Ferry Landing (connecting ramp, pier, gangway and float) and the Water Taxi Landing (platform, gangway and float). The plan was placed by overlaying its own aerial backdrop on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, captured 2025-08-29): its printed structure sizes set the scale (about 0.21 m per plan pixel), no rotation was needed, and the existing Agua Vista Park fishing pier, the shoreline and the roadway match the satellite image. These are the structures as designed in 2018, not as built.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The City's environmental review names Assessor lots 9900064 and 9900064H for this project, and DataSF Parcels (acdm-wktn, checked 2026-10-10) lists both as active. The traced landings lie mostly outside those lots' outlines, so this record keeps the traced shapes.
notes.regulatory_context: A WETA/Port of San Francisco ferry terminal project. The San Francisco County Transportation Authority approved sales-tax (Prop L) funding toward the project, including a further allocation reported in April 2026.

open_questions: Whether the Port's draft Five-Year CIP line item "Pier 64 Sediment Cleanup" covers the same area as this project is not established by the sources read; the City's 2018 environmental review places the project area at the former Pier 64.

The project's total is stated differently across sources: SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post says "a new $77.1 million ferry landing", while SFCTA's Prop L five-year prioritization program (approved June 25, 2024) shows a total project cost of $82,450,000 ($4,500,000 Prop L and $77,950,000 other funds; construction $74,330,000). The structure sizes and positions here are from the City's 2018 design. No later site plan was found, so whether the design changed before construction is not established.

Whether Phase 2b is already under way is stated differently by two sources: the Port's undated project page lists it as "(in progress)", while SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post says its Prop L funds "will support the installation of piles, gangways, fixed piers, canopies, utilities, and landside improvements", which reads as work still ahead. The record's "under construction" status rests on the completed earlier phases and the Port's "in progress". No source gives a start date for Phase 2b or phase-by-phase dates beyond the year-end-2027 expected completion.

records.summary: A proposed 3-story-plus-basement laboratory building at 700 Indiana St in Dogpatch, replacing an existing one-story building. SF YIMBY (February 2025) names Dewey Land Company and MBC BioLabs as responsible for the application; no source read says a lease has been signed. The SF Planning Commission approved the project in June 2024. The Board of Supervisors rejected a neighborhood appeal of its CEQA exemption in September 2024, which affirmed the exemption only: Potrero View (November 2024) reported a separate Board of Appeals hearing on whether the project can proceed, and its outcome was not found. No building permit had been issued as of September 2026.

notes.regulatory_context: SF Planning Case No. 2023-001074ENX. Planning Commission approved the project 2024-06-13 (Motion No. 21576): a 3-story-plus-basement, ~70,650-72,350 gross sq ft lab/office building (sources give slightly different figures) replacing an existing ~15,068 sq ft one-story building, for MBC BioLabs. On 2024-09-24 the Board of Supervisors affirmed the Planning Department's CEQA general plan evaluation exemption, rejecting a neighborhood appeal of it, by 9-1 with Supervisor Walton dissenting (Motion No. M24-089; Board of Supervisors minutes of 2024-09-24, File 240778: 'Ayes: 9' and 'Noes: 1 - Walton'). Potrero View (Nov 2024) reported an 'eight-to-two vote'; the minutes record eight Noes on the separate motions to table and to reverse, which failed. A separate Board of Appeals appeal of the Planning Commission's approval (Appeal No. 24-040, filed 2024-06-28 by the Dogpatch Neighborhood Association and Potrero Boosters) was still to be heard in late October 2024; Potrero View reported on 2025-01-27 that the two groups withdrew it, but the Board of Appeals' own record of the withdrawal was not read. No DataSF building permit found as of 2026-09-28, so construction has apparently not yet started.

Height: the CEQA Notice of Exemption and Motion M24-089 give 48 ft on the north side and 33 ft on the south side, or 54 ft and 39 ft including rooftop mechanical equipment and elevator penthouse. SF YIMBY (February 2025) calls it "The 54-foot tall structure", the north side's height with equipment; the Board of Supervisors agenda says "48-foot tall".

No source dated within the last 12 months describes this project. The newest are SF YIMBY (February 2, 2025) and the CEQA notice (January 24, 2025). On October 13, 2026 the City's building-permit dataset showed no permit for new construction at 700 Indiana St (the latest permit listed there is a 2012 sign permit), and the outcome of the Board of Appeals matter is still not found.

records.summary: A long-stalled Port of San Francisco redevelopment of Piers 38 and 40, led by San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP); the Port's April 2026 memo calls Pacific Waterfront Partners an SFWP affiliate, while the Port's project page names Pacific Waterfront Partners as the negotiating party. The original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (dated March 12, 2021) expired on March 15, 2023, and the Port's April 2026 memo says the developer is out of compliance with it because of missed Performance Dates. In April 2026 the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA giving the developer a 12-month "Evaluation Period" to rework the project's scope and financing. The Registry SF reported on August 12, 2026 (publication date) that the piers "are being offered for long-term lease to major credit tenants"; that listing is not a lease or a Port-approved deal. No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's last_verified date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 9900038 and 9900040, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. Pier 38 is lot 9900038 and Pier 40 is lot 9900040 (DataSF lists both as active, block 9900, the pier number as the lot, street name KING), and the earlier traces lie 95% inside the two lots together, so the match is clear; no Port document read names the lots. Each lot's edge can run a few metres off the visible deck edge, and includes ground the traces left out (the Pier 38 bulkhead building along the Embarcadero and aprons); the lots are the legal boundaries. Status 'planned' means proposed only: the Port's April 28, 2026 staff report says the term sheet 'was never executed' and that the Port and developer agreed to 'suspend active negotiation of transaction documents' for twelve months 'to further evaluate project costs and other key obstacles to Project feasibility'; completing environmental (CEQA) analysis and executing a lease are still future benchmarks. Use is as shown on this record.

notes.why_no_real_parcel: Each pier has its own Assessor lot (Pier 38 is 9900038 and Pier 40 is 9900040; DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, active); this record is one project over two lots, and its outline is the two lots.
notes.regulatory_context: Developer: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP). Original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement: Port Commission Resolution 21-10 (2021-02-23), expired 2023-03-15 for missed performance dates. PWP separately owed the Port over $980,000 in back rent on three unrelated leases (Pier 28, two Agriculture Building suites), unpaid since it vacated them 2024-01-31. On 2026-04-28 the Port Commission adopted a Settlement Agreement (Resolution 26-21: PWP to pay $720,000 over 3 years, with the remainder of the debt forgiven on compliance) and an Amended and Restated ENA (Resolution 26-22: a 12-month 'Evaluation Period' to explore value engineering, project phasing and a new financial partner, with a new Schedule of Performance due before the period ends around April 2027). No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's own last_verified date.

records.summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. The design phase is funded and scheduled, not shown as started: the SFCTA Board approved $1.3 million for it in April 2026 and Caltrain expects to complete design by summer 2027. Sources disagree on when the station would open for use: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 2026 post and presentation), December 2029 (the project description in SFCTA's April 14 packet) and "the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 2026), all subject to funding. In September 2026 the Federal Transit Administration announced a $14.1 million All Stations Accessibility Program award to Caltrain's board for the station (Trains.com, September 16, 2026). Sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box (60 m by 80 m) under the I-280 viaduct just south of 22nd St, where the owner places the existing below-grade station; not a traced footprint of the platforms or the planned ramps themselves (one ~305ft ramp on the northbound platform, one ~465ft ramp on the southbound platform, per the project's own design description). The platforms are hidden from aerial imagery by the freeway above, so the box's size and exact position are not measured. The box is not clipped against the I-280 street lines: the station is below grade, beneath the viaduct, so the freeway's own footprint is not a reason to cut it.
notes.digitized_from: The owner's direction (2026-10-13): the existing station sits under the I-280 viaduct, south of 22nd St. Placement is a coarse locational box in that spot, built from DataSF's official street centerlines: 60 m across (centred on the I-280 corridor between its two carriageway centerlines), running 80 m south from the 22nd St curb line (6.8 m from its centerline). No Caltrain/Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available, and the platforms are hidden from aerial imagery by the elevated freeway, so its size is a placeholder, not a measurement. DataSF's Assessor layer has no lot of its own for the station's tracks (active rail right-of-way); about half of the box lies in active lot 4168011 (zoned Public), which no source read names as the station's lot.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The station's tracks and platforms are active Caltrain rail right-of-way with no lot of their own in the Assessor layer, the same situation as the existing 4th & King Street Station (mapped in Pier & Point's Mission Bay railyards record). About 51% of this placeholder box lies in active lot 4168011 (zoned Public, on the secured roll), a much larger lot of which the box covers 19%; no source read names that lot as the station, so it is not used as the outline.
notes.regulatory_context: The Caltrain 22nd Street Station is the railroad's only regular-service station that is not wheelchair accessible: its platforms sit about 25 ft below street level, reachable only by stairs. Sponsor: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain); funded in part through SFCTA's Prop L. Total project cost per SFCTA's April 2026 Board Packet: $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L, approved by the SFCTA Board 2026-04-14 and given final approval 2026-04-28; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The FTA's 'All Stations Accessibility Program' separately awarded the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board $14.1 million for this project's ADA improvements, announced in September 2026 (the day is not given by the sources read) -- matching almost exactly the funding gap SFCTA's own April 2026 plan had left as 'Planned TBD'.

The month differs by source: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post, "seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029", and the April 14 presentation, "Open for use expected June 2029"), December 2029 (SFCTA's April 14 packet, project description: "have the project open for use by December 2029, subject to funding availability"; its allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029) and "project completion by the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). Construction was not yet funded in April 2026; the FTA announced a $14.1 million award in September 2026, but no source gives a construction schedule.

record.name: 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement

open_questions: This record's placement under Pier 70 rather than Potrero Power Station reflects a roughly equal real-world distance (about 400-450m to each tracked boundary) plus the station's more established association with the Dogpatch/Pier 70 corridor in transit planning -- not a precise geometry test against a real station footprint (no Assessor parcel or site-plan figure exists to test against; the map shape is a coarse placeholder box; see its accuracy note).

No source says design work has begun or how far along it is. SFCTA's April 14, 2026 packet schedules design from April 2026 to September 2027 ("Review 30% design and other documentation: 7/1/26 – 8/1/26"; geotechnical report "anticipated October 2026") and gives "Start Construction" as April-June 2028, but that is a plan written before the work, and no source dated after the planned start reports progress.

When the station would open for use is given three ways: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post and its April 14 presentation), December 2029 (the project description in SFCTA's April 14 packet) and the end of 2029 (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). The packet's own allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029 and "Project Completion (means last eligible expenditure)" in July-September 2029. All are subject to funding, which was not secured when the dates were written; the record shows 2029 only.
